Sports.title: Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1: Clarke scores 90th-minute winner against old club as Premier League new-boys get opening-day win
Sports.content:
PROMISED LAND Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1: Clarke scores 90th-minute winner against old club as Premier League new-boys get opening-day win

SUPER-SUB Jack Clarke sent Portman Road into bedlam with a deliciously curled winner over Sunderland as the match entered injury-time.

Two years ago, the Tractor Boys lost too many points from winning positions, especially at home, and slipped back down into the Championship with barely a whimper.



Gary O’Neil’s new side are adamant that they won’t be doing that again this season. A rip-roaring game that crackled from the first whistle appeared to be destined for a draw which would have brought uncomfortable memories for those in Suffolk.

After new signing Emersonn had scored a debut goal in the 24th minute to match his £24m transfer fee from Toulouse, visitors Sunderland fought back through a stunning Nilson Angulo free-kick.



That paved the way for Clarke to play the hero from the subs bench, curling the ball into the bottom corner with ice-cool precision in the 90th minute.

Two seasons ago, Ipswich largely stuck to the players who had hauled the club up from League One in successive seasons only to discover that the step up in class was too great for most of them.

This summer, led by new manager O’Neil who has no bond to last season’s team under Kieran McKenna, they have tried another way. The Sunderland way.

Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris brought in 14 new players to his promotion-winning squad and took them into the Europa League places.

So far in this transfer window, Ipswich have signed 12 new players, seven of whom were thrust into the opening day line-up by O’Neil. The returns will not be instant but the points gained from this tight encounter will give them breathing space.

Two of the new signings combined to glorious effect in the 24th minute to send Portman Road wild with delight. Julio Enciso, who was on loan at the club two seasons ago, sped away from two challenges, hurdling his way past Luke O’Nien before picking out Emersonn, who turned the ball over the line.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The 22-year-old Brazilian, signed from French club Toulouse, fell to his knees in a mixture of delight and relief at starting to repay his hefty transfer fee.

He almost returned the favour for Enciso minutes later but the Ecuador international found himself crowded out.

It was another new signing who maintained their lead on the half-hour. Dutch keeper Kjell Scherpen is the tallest player to ever play in the Premier League.

With arms like rotor blades, he had to contort his giant frame inwards to push away a Noah Sadiki header from a free-kick.



For all the excitement swarming around Portman Road whenever an Ipswich player broke a tackle, it was Sunderland who kept opening up the Ipswich defence, with a succession of crosses just evading players in red and white stripes.

The Sunderland players have the advantage of knowing each other’s play. They also have the experience confidence gained from last season’s stellar campaign as they surged into Europe behind the leadership of manager Regis Le Bris and his lieutenant on the pitch, Granit Xhaka.

They began to break up the Ipswich play more frequently and carved out a number of promising attacks.



Ipswich’s luck ran out seven minutes before half-time after new central defender Issa Diop clumsily fouled Xhaka just outside the Ipswich area.

The Switzerland international appeared poised to take the free-kick with his left foot. Instead, it was Nilson Angulo who stepped up from the other side to whip his right-footed shot up and over a static Ipswich wall and in off the underside of the bar.

The equaliser punctured the Suffolk air and brought a reality check to the home fans who remember only too well how many times their side led at Portman Road on their last visit to the Premier League, only to succumb later in the game.

O’Neil clearly had no intention of allowing that to happen, sending his team back out super-charged after the interval super-charged.

The second period began like a basketball game with chances at first one end, then the other. Abdul Fatawu used his trickery to beat defenders at will and sent over a number of enticing crosses, one of which almost converted by Enciso with an imaginative floated effort, before he flicked another Fatawu delivery just wide of the far post.



Daizen Maeda also went close with a glancing header that missed the far post by inches.

It didn’t seem possible that the scoreline would end up at 1-1. Brobbey was usual combative self, muscular as well as determined and it took two Ipswich defenders to charge down his shot following a Reinildo Mandava pass.

Sports.title: Joe Hart, 39, reveals he’s had hair transplant to give his confidence a ‘boost’ – and shows off results
Sports.content:
FOOTY ace Joe Hart has followed in the footsteps of his pundit pal Wayne Rooney by having a hair transplant.

The former England and Manchester City goalkeeper revealed he underwent a treatment to give his confidence a “boost” – nine months after making his Match of the Day debut.



Hart, 39, acted to save his locks – which he famously showed off during his career in a Head & Shoulders ad campaign – after he realised they were thinning.

The Premier League winner secretly underwent a 2,500 follicle FUE transplant last May.



And he showed off the impressive results while working for the Beeb during this summer’s 2026 World Cup, sparking speculation about his refreshed look.

The keeper’s fresh summer look stunned so many viewers that comedian Paddy McGuiness joked on his football podcast: “Have you seen his hair? An unbelievable transplant. It’s like an Axminster [carpet]. It looks fantastic. I was like, ‘give me the name of that surgeon’.”

Man Utd legend Paul Scholes smiled and added that pundit Hart now “looks like Action Man”.

Since then Hart – who won five league titles with Man City and Celtic, four Premier League Golden Gloves and played for his country 75 times – has opted to come clean about having FUE surgery because, in his own words, “my hair was going.”

And he has also revealed that his hair transplant, ‘has made me feel a lot more easy, comfortable and confident.’

Hart explained the reasons for having FUE surgery in an Instagram post on his hair transplant surgeon’s page.



He said: “I always had really thick hair growing up and loved having thick hair. I felt strong. I felt confident with it. Then my hair started to thin when I was in my early 30s.

“I’ve come away from football now so I’ve got a little bit of time where I can take care of me, and I thought it was the right time to do it.”

Hart’s 2500 follicle procedure was completed byDr Furqan Raja in May last year.

The Leeds-based surgeon has worked wonders with the hair of several leading UK sports and entertainment stars.



He most recently completed new Gladiators star and former England rugby player Joe Marler’s hair transplant to help him retain his trademark Mohawk cut.

About his procedure, Joe said: “When it came to it, I had good people around me and I asked all the important questions of Dr Raja’s team, so I felt comfortable and I felt ready to go. It was always nice and reassuring to know I had the top man doing the work.”

He also revealed that his hair transplant is the reason changing his look. Reflecting on his new buzz cut hairstyle, seen during his World Cup work, Hart said: “I’ve actually changed my style. I didn’t have shorter hair before.

“People have asked me, ‘why have you got it done if you’re only going to have short hair?’ But I like having the option of either. If I want to grow it, I can. If I like it short, I’ll keep it short. Now, I can have the choice.



“Before, if I’d have had short hair, I’d have felt I’d had to have done it because my hair was going.”

Asked by Dr Raja if he’d expected such a transformation, Joe replied: “A good result for me would have been anything that improved what I already had – a little bit thicker through the middle, that I’d see when I was looking in the mirror or getting myself ready. Anything that could have been improved, would have made me feel better.

“And confidence and looks-wise, it has helped me. If it hadn’t have worked it wouldn’t have broken my heart but the fact that it has, has made me feel a lot more easy, a lot more comfortable, confident.”

Dr Furqan Raja explained how he undertook Joe Hart’s FUE hair transplant on his Instagram post.

The surgeon said: “When planning Joe’s procedure, we carefully studied earlier photographs of him to design a natural contour that closely reflected the hairline he previously had.



“Using FUE, we transplanted approximately 2,500 grafts to rebuild Joe’s hairline and add density through his frontal and mid-scalp regions. Then we tapered the area towards Joe’s crown.

“A year on, I’m extremely pleased with how natural Joe’s result looks and there is still further maturation to come.

“It has been fantastic to see the response to Joe’s hair over the past year, and particularly during television coverage of the World Cup last month.

“Seeing Joe and his hair looking so good, as he provided expert analysis on the biggest stage, was particularly satisfying.

“We are delighted for Joe.”



Joe joins a long list of footballers who have had hair transplants.

On the BBC he sits alongside Wayne Rooney who pioneered the procedure in 2011.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Since then, Mohamed Salah, David Silva, Jurgen Klopp, Antonio Conte, Xerdan Shaqiri, Ryan Giggs and Andros Townsend, among other players, have had FUE hair transplants.

Joe joined the MOTD studio panel following his retirement at the end of the 23/24 season and officially became a pundit on BBC’s Match of the Day in August 2024.

Sports.title: Numb Newcastle hero Rob Lee shut himself off from world and wept after tragic death of ‘second dad’ Kevin Keegan
Sports.content:
ROB LEE loved Kevin Keegan and hailed the late Newcastle legend as the “next best thing to my dad.”

And the feeling was mutual as former Toon boss Keegan claimed Lee was his finest-ever signing at St James’ Park.



That is some tribute because King Kev smashed the transfer world record to bring Alan Shearer home from Blackburn for £15million in 1996.

He also brought the likes of David Ginola and Tino Asprilla to the Toon so Lee is in fine company.



So Keegan’s death last month at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer, hit Lee hard.

Former Magpies and England midfielder Lee, 60, was at home on his own when he heard Keegan had passed away.



He emotionally revealed: “I have got to admit I shed quite a few tears that day.

“In fact, I shut myself off from the world for a few hours.

“Within minutes of it breaking, I was inundated with requests for interviews but I had to turn them all down. I was just too numb.”

Lee will be back on Tyneside for the visit of Liverpool, along with many of his former team-mates from the 1990s who together became known — and still are — as ‘The Entertainers.’



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Lee said: “I am quite fortunate because in my capacity as Hornchurch director of football, I’m in Carlisle over the weekend, which is only 50 miles from Newcastle.

“But even if we had been playing in the south west, I would still have been there.

“Nothing in the world would stop me.”

Keegan’s Magpies may have missed out on major honours but Lee regards the five years he played under the legendary England forward were the best years of his life.

Lee, who like Keegan, wore the No 7 black and white shirt, said: “He changed my career and he changed my life.



“People did not believe me when I said I had Keegan posters plastered all over my bedroom walls — but it’s true.

“He was my boyhood hero and I was lucky enough to play under him.

“Believe me, it was the biggest of dreams come true.”

Lee kept in touch with Keegan long after the two left Tyneside and saw him most recently last November.

He said: “It was at a do in Upminster, near where I live. His wife Jean was there with him and my family went along too. It was a great night.



“He was the same Kevin I’d always known. He was witty, bubbly, friendly and oozing charisma.

“And, of course, he stayed long after midnight signing autographs and chatting to people.

“Little could I imagine that would be the last time that I ever saw him in the flesh.”



Lee is now looking forward to a reunion with so many of Newcastle’s greatest-ever players who starred in the Keegan era.

And, of course, the Newcastle versus Liverpool fixture evokes so many memories — some particularly painful.

Lee admitted: “I have lost count of the number of times I’ve been asked if I want to see another 4-3 thriller!

“Let’s not forget we lost the most famous one, which was a result which really cost us.

“There is this myth surrounding Kevin that he’d prefer to lose 4-3 than to win 1-0 — but that’s rubbish.



“Remember, he was a winner throughout his life and winners hate losing.

“Don’t get me wrong, he loved attacking football and he was so proud of that Entertainers’ tag.

“He’d always tell us we had a duty to entertain our public and I think it’s fair to say we managed to do that.

“I cannot recall too many goalless draws when he was in charge.

“I just wish we could have got over the line that season because that’s what Kevin deserved.”



So will Sunday’s afternoon’s Prem clash at St James’ be another high-scoring affair?

Lee said: “Well, I’d love to see it because that would be the ultimate tribute to the man himself — but only with Newcastle winning, of course!”

Since his death, there has been much talk of Keegan being honoured with a statue outside St James’ or even having a stand named after him.



The club have already announced there will be official recognition of the great man.

But Lee feels that perhaps the club should have paid tribute to one of their favourite sons a long time ago.

He added: “Look, it’s all a bit late, isn’t it? Something should have been done years ago.

“I loved Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer is a big mate, but Kevin’s statue should have been erected before anyoneelse’ss.

“Kev rescued Newcastle United from oblivion not once but twice.



“First as a player in the early-Eighties and then as a manager.

“Newcastle were in the old Second Division when he joined as a genuine footballing superstar and led them to promotion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And what he did as a manager is now the stuff of folklore.”

There will be tears and cheers for Keegan at around 4.25pm but you suspect that when the minute’s applause is over, no-one will have a bigger lump in his throat than the great man’s greatest-ever signing.

Sports.title: Man Utd chiefs risk resembling Ed Woodward after Hull horror show as knee-jerk buys fail & Carrick endures toughest day
Sports.content:
THE broadcasters did not miss their cue with Manchester United 2-0 down at Hull.

One of the cameras homed in on director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, a duo who have had to adopt deadpan poker faces in directors’ boxes for two years now.



Wilcox and Berrada are entitled to expect much better than the lethargic and leaden performance United served up at the MKM Stadium.

Patrick Dorgu had the benefit of starting all six pre-season friendlies and lasted a half. Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven partnered each other four times in the friendlies yet looked incompatible.



Many of Michael Carrick’s calls were questionable. Why pick Heaven, United’s rawest defender? Why does he think Dorgu is a winger? Why move Bryan Mbeumo to the wing when he has played all of his pre-season up front? Why put Matheus Cunha up front after a mere 60 minutes there against AC Milan?

Carrick had his worst day as United head coach and a theme has developed. Whenever he makes substantial changes, personnel or tactical, United lose.

The upside is a defensive midfielder is about to beef up United’s soft centre. The downside is the defence will not get overhauled until next year.

With Carlos Baleba expected to be confirmed in the coming days, if not hours, United could feasibly sign a defensive midfielder and a defender in the final days of the window. They will look reactive in a summer that they should have been proactive.

A £70million fee for Baleba was admittedly agreed before the Hull horror show but it should not have taken that long.

Brighton man Baleba knew United wanted him more than a year ago and he spoke with Michael Carrick, as well as future teammates, at the Amex Stadium three months ago.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Getting Baleba in the building for July would have been doubly advantageous as Cameroon did not qualify for the World Cup. Mbeumo, Baleba’s compatriot, was United’s standout performer in pre-season and the only outfield starter who produced a passable performance at Hull.

United still had two new signings in their side on the opening weekend. The issue is neither is necessarily considered a starting signing when Saturday comes.

Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, on their full debuts, lived up to their squad player billings.

Baleba, a probable long-term partner for Kobbie Mainoo, would be deemed a starting signing. He will not get a kick until next month, at the earliest, due to an ankle injury.

The knee-jerk nature of United’s deal-making has been a theme of their window. Elliot Anderson wanted Manchester City, so it was onto Mateus Fernandes, who took the money and ran to Tottenham. So they turned to Santos.



A deal for Ederson collapsed, so the £35m scheduled to be deposited in Atalanta’s account made its way into Aston Villa’s for Tielemans.

Santos and Tielemans were prudent purchases completed quickly. They should have been good enough to see off Hull, hardly an acid test. Neither passed it.

They will now know how much more demanding it is to pull on the United shirt. Santos has been upgraded from bit-part player at Chelsea to Casemiro’s heir apparent at United. It is an onerous burden on the 22-year-old’s shoulders.



Tielemans recently revealed that his body “switched off” at the World Cup. He was not switched on at Hull and was fortunate to re-emerge for the second half.

A five-year contract for a midfielder who turns 30 next year who made his professional debut aged 16 was excessive. The biggest insult one could level at Wilcox and Berrada is that it was a piece of business reminiscent of Ed Woodward’s days.

Failure to bolster the midfield with an enforcer has contributed to another records-tumbling defeat to Hull – and inflicted reputational damage on Wilcox and Berrada. Finalising incomings in the wake of an August defeat would be another unwanted parallel with Woodward.

It happened last year amid the indecision over which goalkeeper to recruit. While United pondered, Altay Bayindir and Andre Onana chucked the ball in against Arsenal and Grimsby.

A defensive midfielder was always a must at United this summer but they have been complacent at left back and up front.



They have probably left it too late with Lewis Hall and Mikel Arteta has quashed talk of Arsenal cashing in on Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Hall would be the ideal successor to Luke Shaw, into his 13th season at United. Shaw has had three good seasons in 12 and one was in the meaningless and misleading pandemic campaign of 2020-21.

As alarming as United’s defending at Hull was how impotent they were. Striker Benjamin Sesko is back from a long-term shin injury but senior United figures say a new striker is not on their radar.

Joshua Zirkzee, signed on the assumption he was a striker, made one competitive start during Sesko’s three-and-a-half month lay-off and is barely of consideration.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zirkzee was the first signing of the Berrada and Wilcox era. They’ll need to adopt that poker face again if United are to shift Zirkzee.

The Brazil international was part of the team that won the Saudi Pro League in 2025 as well as the King’s Cup.

Fabinho played a total of 111 times for the Saudi outfit but is now looking towards the next chapter of his career.

Salah, meanwhile, will go down as one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history after ending his incredible nine-year spell at the club in May.

He scored 257 goals in 442 games for the Reds and was crucial in helping the club win two Premier League titles.

But his final season at the club ended on a rocky note as he gave a bombshell interview accusing Liverpool of “throwing him under the bus” over a lack of game time.



He was heavily linked with a move to the Saudi Pro League himself but ended up sealing a shock move to Turkey.

Salah has already made his debut for the club in a 1-1 draw with rivals Kasimpasa.

He played the final 32 minutes of that game before starting a 1-0 Europa League qualifying defeat to Ferencvaros.

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos show Michael Carrick why Man Utd desperately need Carlos Baleba after stinker vs Hull
Sports.content:
ANDREY SANTOS and Youri Tielemans put the mid in midfield as Manchester United stunk the place out against Hull – and that is being generous.

Michael Carrick‘s new-look pairing were completely ineffective behind Bruno Fernandes and left much to be desired in an embarrassing 2-0 loss.



The opening day competitive debuts for each went terribly as they were hooked after 67 minutes.

In a minor positive, neither Kobbie Mainoo nor Benjamin Sesko had any more luck after coming on, and nobody else had any luck for United.



But with the club still looking to buy a THIRD midfielder of the window, Brighton may well be thinking about bumping up their asking price for Carlos Baleba.

A deal worth around £65million for the player has been agreed but United are so desperate in the centre of the park that they would surely settle for paying even more at this stage.



Historic tough negotiators, Brighton could ask United to throw money at them for Baleba and little argument would surely be put up, he is that big of an addition.

Where Santos and Tielemans were short against Hull, Baleba drives from deep and covers ground for fun.

He is a wide-ranging passer and explosive in marauding across the pitch.

None of those words could be used to describe United’s £85million pair on Humberside.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Santos, who cost £50million of that figure from Chelsea, had been one of the standout performers in pre-season.

He and Mason Mount, another ex-Blue costing £65million, impressed on tour.

But at newly promoted – and massive favourites to go straight back down – Hull, he was stunted.

Brazilian Santos may well have completed 52 of his 56 passes (93 per cent) but almost half of those were safely in his own half.

He lost the ball FIVE times and only produced one progressive carry despite Hull sitting on the edge of their own penalty area.



Usually an adventurous line-breaker, Santos couldn’t impact the game at all.

He committed one foul and ended up making more clearances (three) than chances.

If Santos stumbled then Tielemans fell flat on his face.

The Belgian, a £35million signing from Aston Villa, was even worse.



Another player used to advancing play in possession, he misplaced EIGHT passes and completed less than 50 per cent of his 62 in Hull’s half.

He lost the ball FIVE times trying to get it forward in the middle third and was a hinderance when travelling with it.

Hull nabbed the ball off him on 11 occasions and made light work of getting past him when attacking.

Tielemans made one foul, was dribbled past twice, and made ZERO defensive contributions.



Even Baleba, coming off the back of a tough year on the south coast, will be able to offer more impetus.

And Carrick best hope that it moves along quickly as he seeks to get United going.

Mainoo was left on the bench from the start which frustrated some.



And Santos was described as being “nowhere near good enough at this stage of his career to be a starter” by one fan online.

Another said: “Santos and Tielemans struggled to even keep the ball.”

Sports.title: Tottenham fall flat as Roberto De Zerbi's new-look team dealt brutal lesson by Brentford
Sports.content:
Tottenham fall flat as Roberto De Zerbi's new-look team dealt brutal lesson by Brentford

BRENTFORD 3-0 TOTTENHAM: Roberto De Zerbi has been dealt a serious reality check as his lavishly assembled side were hammered in their Premier League opener

View 2 Images Brentford made light work of Tottenham's expensively-assembled side

Roberto De Zerbi has claimed Tottenham "can't forget what happened last season" - but there was no danger of that as their losing habit continued at Brentford.

‌



The Italian kept Tottenham afloat last term, just, and after a summer that will likely see £300million spent there was a sense of a new beginning. Instead those in the away end in west London will simply have felt a sense of deja vu from last season.

‌



It felt like digesting defeat became a weekly occurrence for Tottenham and, despite boasting £100m record signing Sandro Tonali in midfield, were outclassed in every facet by the Bees, who were three goals to the good before the hour mark.

‌



Only an Igor Thiago penalty that came off the post prevented it from being 4-0 by sixty minutes. Keane Lewis-Potter had the hosts ahead inside 12 minutes with Vitaly Janelt doubling their lead by half-time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

De Zerbi threw on Mateus Fernandes and Rodrigo Bentancur to start the second-half, but they did little to turn the tide. Fernandes spent a short period as Tottenham's record buy after signing for £85m but after successive relegation he did little to prove his doubters wrong on his first run out.

‌



The Tottenham boss said on Friday: "At the end of the transfer market, I will be more accurate in my opinion. Maybe we will know now. Maybe we have to see on the pitch. To be honest everyone we are very excited but in the end the pitch speaks."

It did speak. Volumes. Tottenham's spend has dwarfed that of Brentford but Keith Andrews' side again showed that a solid system and plenty of continuity can still power over a host of multi-million signings.

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi was regularly left looking like he had no answers

‌



Jan Paul van Hecke, the £52m new centre-half in the Tottenham backline, was unable to halt the Brentford wave. Had Tottenham got the first goal of the second-half it would've been game on, instead it was game over when Michael Kayode reacted quickest from a corner to score Brentford's third.

There is talk of Savinho and Omar Marmoush both joining from Manchester City, which would add more than £100m to Tottenham's summer spend. The addition of individual quality seems to have done little to improve Tottenham's fortunes so far, so watch this space.

James Maddison appeared from the bench after spending last season out injured, which was about as positive as Tottenham's evening got.

Article continues below

De Zerbi has clearly added quality to his squad, but Saturday showed that moving on from last year's 17th place finish is going to be a lot harder than it may have seemed in pre-season when record signings were arriving on a weekly basis.

Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'

Arsenal remain in the market for a new forward but, after missing out on Vinicius Jnr, Juventus have made it clear that they will not sell Kenan Yildiz

View 2 Images Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has continued to impress in Turin (Image: Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images)

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti insists Arsenal "can offer whatever they like" but the Italians will not be selling Kenan Yildiz.

‌



The north Londoners failed with an initial enquiry for Yildiz earlier this summer and the Old Lady have now made it clear they're not prepared to entertain the forward's sale.

‌



Juventus are ultimately in no hurry to sell and have the 21-year-old tied down on a contract until 2030, which he signed back in February. Yildiz scored 11 times in 47 outings last term and his displays saw him named the Serie A Rising Star of the Season.

‌



Yildiz has continued to blossom since heading to Juventus as a free agent from the Bayern academy in 2022 and Spalletti is now adamant that, regardless of what figure is produce, the club will not sell their young star.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace star stretchered off in tears as injury nightmare returns on opening day
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace star stretchered off in tears as injury nightmare returns on opening day

Crystal Palace's 2-0 defeat at Everton came with a further blow after defender Chadi Riad was stretchered off, having sustained a nasty-looking knee injury

View 2 Images Chadi Riad was stretchered off after being injured (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Crystal Palace star Chadi Riad was in tears after sustaining what looked like a serious injury on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

‌



Riad appeared to twist his left knee while defending a cross from Vitaliy Mykolenko in the second half against Everton. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson immediately waved for medical treatment, with the Morocco international in obvious pain and distress.

‌



He pulled his shirt over his head and was in tears as he was stretchered off to warm applause at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Riad was replaced by Takehiro Tomiyasu in the 72nd minute of the 2-0 defeat.

‌



Palace wrote on X: "We're right behind you, Chadi." The 23-year-old's time at the Premier League club has been marred by injuries.

Palace defender Chris Richards told Match of the Day: "You never want to see an injury, Chadi has battled with injuries throughout his career here, my prayers go out to him. We will rally around him, this season is for Chadi."

Manager Pierre Sage added: "At the moment I don't know, I hope it will be better than we think. We await the medical tests."

Chadi joined from Barcelona in June 2024 for a reported £14million fee, yet has only made 16 appearances for the club. Riad was injured in August 2024, with the knee issue keeping him out until December that year.

He returned in the second half of the 2025/26 season and featured enough for the Eagles to make Morocco's 26-man squad for the World Cup. But it now seems that Riad could be set for another prolonged period in the treatment room.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold reveals abuse after Liverpool exit but still watches every game
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold reveals abuse after Liverpool exit but still watches every game

Trent Alexander-Arnold speaks exclusively to the Mirror about his acrimonious move to Real Madrid in his first wide-ranging interview

View 3 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold opens up to the Mirror (Image: Daily Mirror)

Trent Alexander-Arnold has laid bare the scale of abuse he received after leaving Liverpool but says he will always love his boyhood club and watches every game.

‌



The England star has opened up in depth for the first time about his acrimonious departure to Real Madrid last year including being booed on his return to Anfield.

‌



He says there was a difference between supporters expressing their fury inside a football stadium and the “stuff that crossed the line”.

‌



He said: “Abuse online and threats made via social DMs or in other ways are a sad part of life in 2026 if you’re in the public eye and doing things that create a lot of attention. I choose to keep those things away from me because they don’t feel real.”

He adds: “I can rationalise that by knowing it’s not representative of a football club I love, LFC, and it’s not representative of my home city.”

The right-back returned to Anfield last November for a Champions League match in which they lost 1-0. Alexander-Arnold was jeered by fans when he was introduced from the bench in the 80th minute, as well as during the warm-up.

‌



He said: “The booing and disappointment from Liverpool supporters is something I’m absolutely able to shoulder. I can understand it, in my own way. I heard a lot during that period that Liverpool fans didn’t want to be told how to feel or think, and I agree. But I hope one day there’ll be a degree of understanding about the decisions I wanted to make around my own life.

“It hurts because of how much I’ve put into the club over the course of 20 years and the sacrifices I made for the club during that period. So of course it hurts, but I understand the disappointment. I even understand anger expressed through booing.”

View 3 Images Trent opens up (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



As well as anger inside the stadium, the word "rat" was repeatedly daubed over a mural celebrating Alexander-Arnold nearby. The football ace was sent the image by a friend, and it weighed on him when he returned to the city for the match.

“Going back to Liverpool after everything that’s happened it was on my mind,” he says, adding that his family were also left upset.

“If I'm honest, if something affects me and upsets me, it shows in my family as well. They are in it with me…we’re together.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold found the whole day hard to process. He admits: “Even from the outset, even the thought of going into the away changing room was strange. I’d never actually stepped foot in there before.”

The football star believes the wider impact of online abuse is a serious issue, although one he feels ultimately needs to be addressed by politicians and technology companies. Alexander-Arnold, who has also previously suffered abhorrent racist abuse online, said: “On threats to people via social media, social media pile-ons and the impact they can have on people’s mental health, I think that’s a proper topic.

“But it’s for governments and tech companies to solve. I’ve kind of protected myself from that as much as possible, but I get that for some people it’s not possible.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold has found reassurance in the stark difference between the vitriol directed at him online and the reception he receives when he actually returns to Merseyside.

“Since leaving for Real Madrid, I’ve been back to Liverpool to visit family on a number of occasions,” he said.

“I’ve bumped into lots of fellow Scousers and Reds when I’ve been on my travels. Not a single interaction I’ve had in person reflects the sort of stuff you get online or via social media. So that helps me disassociate it.

‌



“This isn’t me saying everyone in Liverpool is fine with me leaving the club. Of course they aren’t. But that’s very different from the stuff that goes beyond the football. It’s why I don’t allow myself to get too down about it and I don’t dwell on it.”

The intensity of the reaction reflected Alexander-Arnold’s unique relationship with Liverpool. A local boy who joined the academy aged six, he rose through the ranks to play 259 times for the club. Yet for all the bitterness surrounding his departure, Alexander-Arnold’s own feelings towards Liverpool appear strikingly unchanged.

“I still watch every game,” he said. “I support them. I want to see them do well. I enjoy watching them, and there will always be a place in my heart for Liverpool, no matter what. It is home to me. It’s the place that gave me the opportunities to go and do what I’ve done and I will always love it. It’s always a place that I’ll call home.”

‌



View 3 Images Trent talks to the Mirror (Image: Daily Mirror)

Alexander-Arnold also spoke of his heartache after missing out on England’s World Cup squad as he remembers the day earlier this year when Thomas Tuchel broke the news to him.

“I was aware the calls were underway,” he said. “Other players I knew had had their call the day before. I’ll be honest, I was full of hope. When the call came, I was at home in Madrid. I had some family over visiting and I went to my bedroom to take the call. When I put the phone down, I was properly gutted. Absolutely gutted. I’d made no plans for my summer because I hoped I’d be in the squad.”

‌



Alexander-Arnold had continued pushing to force his way into Tuchel’s plans and felt his performances during the closing stages of the season had given him reason to believe he might make it.

The rejection left him not merely disappointed but furious too. “I hope the coaching staff would expect and understand that I was angry,” he said. “He wants players who are desperate to play for England. I am one of those. I think he would respect the fact that it really hurt me and prefer that to me not being bothered.”

That hurt is particularly acute given the fierce competition Alexander-Arnold has faced throughout his international career. “We’ve had a lot of really, really good right-backs in this generation that I’ve been playing in so far,” he said. “There’s been a lot of competition, and the managers choose who they feel is the best fit for the team. That’s never really been me so far. But I guess I use it as motivation to push.”

‌



And unlike players who have publicly aired their frustrations after being overlooked, Alexander-Arnold believes there was little to be gained by complaining in the immediate aftermath.

“Some things just don’t need to be said,” he said. “I think everybody would have known that I was disappointed. Speaking out in public is not going to change the manager’s decision. He’s made his mind up. He’s decided what he has. There’s no changing it. Life goes on.”

Alexander-Arnold watched England throughout the World Cup and insists his exclusion has done nothing to diminish his determination to represent his country.

‌



“Until I retire, I’m still an England player, whether I’m selected or not,” he said. “I’m always available if and when the manager needs me. There’s no bigger honour.”

And rather than allowing the rejection to consume him, he plans to use it to drive his attempt to force his way back into Tuchel’s thinking. “I’ll take those feelings into this season and turn them into a positive,” he said. “I want to use it as fuel to get back into England squads and then back in an England shirt. That’s an aim of mine and I hope to achieve it.”

Alexander-Arnold has told how he struggled in the aftermath of Liverpool forward Diogo Jota's death in a car crash, aged 28. The football star was in America at the Club World Cup with his new team Real Madrid when his former teammate was tragically killed.

‌



And he says how being so far away from Liverpool and his ex-colleagues in the US was a “very, very difficult time.”

He said: “I think that's what was difficult….going through it on your own. Everybody else who had known him for that amount of time were all grouped together. It was difficult, and then having to continue to play games and them being so far away was hard. But coming back to Anfield and being able to go to the stadium and put some flowers down really helped me get that closure.”

Opening up about Diogo, he said the two of them “spoke every day.” He added: “I was injured a couple of times when he was and we were doing our training to get back fit together, and we were both very competitive.

Article continues below

“So we would always, you know, have different competitions between ourselves. Those are the kind of memories that I'll hold close to me. He was just a really good guy. Like he was very honest. That's one of the best attributes that anybody can have. He was hardworking. He loved what he did, and was a massive family man. "

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hints at new role for Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd hold future talks
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hints at new role for Bruno Fernandes as Man Utd hold future talks

Turkish giants Galatasaray were plotting a €50million (£43m) bid for Bruno Fernandes, but Manchester United have moved to open talks with him over a new contract

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has touched on Bruno Fernandes' future (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has hinted that he'll rotate Bruno Fernandes this season in a bid to get the best out of the Manchester United star. Fernandes, 31, enjoyed his best individual season to date last term, breaking the Premier League assist record with 21 while helping United qualify for the Champions League.

‌



But there is some doubt over the Red Devils captain's long-term future, having entered the final year of his contract at Old Trafford. Turkish giants Galatasaray had planned to test United's resolve by offering €50million (£43m) for his signature.

‌



Now, though, United are in talks with Fernandes and his representatives over a new deal. The Portuguese wants to stay and Carrick has pledged to 'look after him' ahead of what could be a gruelling campaign for his side, as they prepare to fight on all fronts unlike the 2025-26 season.

‌



"I've said quite a lot about Bruno, he's been a big part of the team and the club over recent times and had a huge impact, so he'll continue to do that,' Carrick stated ahead of United's abject 2-0 defeat away to Hull on Saturday.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"In terms of the games and how it comes, hopefully he stays fit and he's in good shape. But yeah, there's the element talking about the squad and the depth, and as we go through the season and the waves and the momentum and keeping the boys in good form, but keeping them fresh as well.

"So Bruno's part of that. He's a big player for us, he's obviously our captain, but there's still elements where we need to look after him."

Part of why Fernandes has been so successful since joining the Red Devils in January 2020 has been his immaculate fitness record. The midfielder has only missed five games through injury in that time for both club and country.

‌



But with the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and soon Carlos Baleba, Carrick has more options in midfield. Mason Mount also enjoyed a promising pre-season before he suffered a small hamstring tear.

Should Manchester United give Bruno Fernandes a new contract? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is out of contract in 2027 (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

‌



"I know we've got a good midfield," Carrick added. "We've brought in some really top players and really good characters, which is important.

"We're trying to improve the squad all the time. As it stands now, we've got some very good, top midfielders to choose from. So I think we've improved that.

"You need a solid foundation through the middle of the team. I think if you look at all the great teams over the years, the spine is really strong. We're conscious of that, and I think we've got a good spine of the team right now."

Sports.title: Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid

Arsenal are still in the running alongside Barcelona to sign Julian Alvarez in the summer transfer window, with the Atletico Madrid striker increasingly unhappy and unsettled

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is unhappy at Atletico Madrid (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta have been in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez and haven't given up hope of signing the unsettled Atletico Madrid striker.

‌



The Gunners are determined to add a world-class forward to their squad before the summer transfer window closes. Alvarez has been focused on leaving Atletico Madrid for Barcelona, but hasn't ruled out a return to the Premier League.

‌



Things have got increasingly messy between Atleti and their star forward - and it could play into Arsenal's hands. Barca saw their €100million (£86m) bid rejected earlier this summer, with Atleti then reporting their La Liga rivals for allegedly tapping up the Argentina international.

‌



Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone wants to keep the 26-year-old, but tensions behind the scenes could trigger a transfer. Atleti chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín said on Friday that Alvarez "has not had the best advisors" this summer after saying he wanted to "fulfil his dream" of joining Barca.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Gil Marín's words prompted a not-so-subtle response from Alvarez's agent Fernando Hidalgo, who wrote on social media: "Never ask a liar why he lied. To explain himself, he would have to lie again."

‌



According to ESPN, Barcelona have given up on signing Alvarez, with Atleti refusing to engage in negotiations. They have turned their attention to his Argentina team-mate Lautaro Martinez, of Inter Milan.

AS reports that Alvarez doesn't understand his club's approach to the transfer saga and remains determined to leave before the window closes on September 1. He would still prefer to join Barcelona, but is conscious of not closing the door on Arsenal either.

View 2 Images Arsenal are still interested in a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez (Image: (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez))

‌



Arteta and Berta have been keeping in touch with Alvarez, who is said to appreciate their interest. A move to Arsenal is considered to be 'a welcome emergency solution' for Alvarez, even if he doesn't want to uproot his family from Madrid.

He is continuing to train for Atleti, but is expected to receive a frosty reception from the supporters when they host Villarreal on Sunday. Simeone has tried to cool the situation ahead of what should be his first appearance since the World Cup.

"There's no uncertainty. Miguel Ángel [Gil Marín] spoke clearly," he said. "For me he's a really important player to achieve our objectives. We'll be with him, we'll look after him on the sporting side, because he's our player... He'll be in the squad tomorrow."

Article continues below

"Atlético Madrid, like every big club, is built on great players, and Julián is one of them, as well as being a great professional," Gil Marín told EFE on Friday. "We have to compete with our values, with homegrown players and the best players we can bring in from outside.

"We are going to help Julián and continue to look after him, so he can reach his full potential... We must understand that Julián hasn't had the best advisors around him in recent months."

Sports.title: Saints keep Super League play-off hopes alive over 10-man Castleford
Sports.content:
St Helens built on a strong first half and relied on six different try-scorers to beat 10-man Castleford 36-12 at the Brewdog Stadium to keep their play-off hopes alive.

It has been a dramatic week for Castleford, whose former head coach Ryan Carr announced he was leaving the club for "personal reasons" on Friday.

Saints also announced a coaching change this week, with Kevin Walters due to join from next season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jackson Hastings was sent off for punching Tyler Dupree, then clashes continued off the pitch between St Helens and Castleford Tigers

The Australian's new side took an early lead, and tries from Jack Welsby, Shane Wright, Jacob Douglas, Tom Humphreys and Tristan Sailor made it 30-0 before the break.

Hastings had added five goals, but lost his cool and was sent off after an altercation with Tyler Dupree for violent conduct.

Dupree was sin-binned for the same incident, and tempers continued to flare as the teams disappeared down the tunnel for the break.

Nene McDonald added a sixth try for the hosts after the break, making a Castleford comeback look increasingly unlikely.

Louis Senior and Laulu-Togaga'e finally got them on the board, and Saints finished the game with 10 men after Alex Walmsley and Chris Matagi were both sent to the sin bin.

St Helens interim boss Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside: "I said I wanted to see the attitude of the players, and what better way to display that than when you go down to 10 men for 45 minutes?

"The players were fantastic. We simplified a few things, which probably helped, because everyone knew what the role was and their position."

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face.

"We'll let the disciplinary (match review panel) deal with those kinds of things. That's what they're there for."

Hull KR slump to another home defeat

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Hull KR and Toulouse Olympique

Hull KR slumped to a second home defeat of the week as Toulouse ran out deserved 32-12 winners following a ruthless second half at Craven Park.

The Robins were beaten at home by play-off rivals Warrington on Tuesday night, and head coach Willie Peters dropped both Tevita Pangai Junior and Mikey Lewis following their upcoming bans which were handed out in the wake of the 34-28 defeat against the Wolves.

It was a scrappy start - much to the frustration of the expectant Hull KR fans - as Toulouse dug in during the opening 20 minutes and then exerted some control before Mathieu Jussaume scored the opening try on the half-hour when he broke through down the right.

The defending champions, chasing a home play-off berth, finally sparked into life when substitute Elliot Minchella went over in the 35th minute after a surging run by Peta Hiku, with Rhyse Martin adding the extras to make it 6-6 heading into half-time.

Toulouse opted to kick for a penalty early in the second half after a late tackle from Tom Amone, but Cesar Rouge saw his 35-metre attempt bounce off the crossbar.

Hull KR continued to be pushed back and Toulouse deservedly did get themselves in front again after 57 minutes when Benjamin Laguerre burst down the left and fed Romeo Tropis to go on to touch down under the sticks.

Hull half-back Jake Arthur landed a late drop goal to seal his side's thrilling fightback as they beat Catalans Dragons 27-26 at the Gilbert Brutus Stadium.

Arthur coolly slotted over a match-winning one-pointer with six minutes left to clinch Hull victory over former boss John Cartwright's Catalans and just their second win in 10 Super League games.

Hull trailed 26-14 early in the second half, but came storming back through converted tries from Harvie Hill and Aidan Sezer to tie the scores before Arthur's match-winning effort.

The visitors led through early tries from Logan Moy and Lewis Martin and led 14-12 at half-time after Catalans had hit back through touchdowns from Charlie Staines and Kruise Leeming.

Catalans appeared to take control of the match when Edenn Rogers-Smith and Leo Darrelatour both went over early in the second period, either side of Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet's penalty, to put them 26-14 ahead.

But Hull launched their fightback as Hill and Sezer both went over for converted scores in the space of six minutes and Arthur had the final word.

Sports.title: McIlroy pulls himself back into contention at BMW Championship
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy pulled himself back into contention at the BMW Championship with a strong finish for a five-under par third round in St Louis.

McIlroy has been looking for a response after labouring to an eight-over finish at last week's St Jude Championship, and shot a fine six-under opening round for a share of the lead, before following that up with a 69 on Friday.

The back-to-back Masters champion again appeared in steady form during the front nine on Saturday, turning at one under after a birdie on the par-three second before another on 11.

World No 2 McIlroy then stepped things up with a run of four birdies from the 13th, sandwiched by a bogey at 14.

The Northern Irishman found both bunkers with his opening two shots on the 18th, but then almost chipped in with a fine recovery effort before saving par.

Image: Wyndham Clark remains the front-runner at Bellerive

McIlroy finished the day at 12 under, looking to keep pace with Wyndham Clark, whose own strong back nine was pulling him clear at 17 under.

Patrick Cantlay was alongside McIlroy at 12 under, with Gary Woodland and Chris Gotterup a shot further back.

JJ Spaun, though, saw his challenge fade fast after dropping to two over.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler - who had coasted to an impressive victory at last week's St Jude Championship, but was two over after a first-round 72 - sits in a group on five under after his 68.

Sports.title: Dundee claim derby bragging rights with victory over winless Dundee United
Sports.content:
Dundee enjoyed another memorable trip across the road as they secured a deserved 2-0 derby victory away to Dundee United to move joint-top of the fledgling Scottish Premiership table.

Drey Wright opened the scoring late in the first half before Owen Bevan notched after the break as the Dark Blues made it three wins in their last four visits to Tannadice.

Steven Pressley's side are now level with Celtic and St Mirren on the six-point mark, albeit having played a game more than most of their rivals, after making it two wins from their opening three league matches.

By contrast, United endured a demoralising evening as they went down to a third straight defeat in all competitions to remain second-bottom with just one point from their three Premiership matches.

Terrors boss Jim Goodwin made six changes to the side that lost 4-0 to Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup, including restoring influential left-back Will Ferry after a minor injury.

There was just one enforced tweak to the Dundee side that lost to Aberdeen in the same competition, with Alan Forrest replacing Simon Murray after the captain sustained anterior cruciate ligament damage at Pittodrie.

Image: Dundee's Joe Westley (L) and Dundee United's Pan Camara in derby action

Swiss striker Bradley Fink, who finalised a season-long loan move from Wycombe earlier in the day, was listed among the substitutes.

Despite being sidelined for the foreseeable future, veteran forward Murray joined his team-mates to make the traditional short pre-match walk from Dens Park to Tannadice.

The visitors had the first two notable attempts, with forwards Charlie Reilly and Joe Westley both going close with efforts from outside the box.

United's first chance came in the 28th minute when Vicko Sevelj's header from a Mehdi Merghem corner was pushed away by Owen Goodman.

Dee defender Ryan Astley then made a brilliant challenge in the six-yard box to stop Idjessi Metsoko turning in Merghem's low delivery from the right.

Image: Drey Wright made it 1-0 to Dundee

Dundee made the breakthrough in the 43rd minute when Wright seized on a loose pass from Abdoulaye Yoro just inside his own half and surged forward before unleashing a powerful shot into Jack Walton's bottom right-hand corner from 20 yards out.

Yoro had a chance to redeem himself early in the second half but his low effort from the angle of the six-yard box was superbly saved by Goodman. A couple of minutes later, the Dundee keeper appeared to be struck by a vape as he retrieved the ball to take a goal-kick in front of the United fans.

The Dark Blues doubled their lead in the 57th minute when Bevan inadvertently diverted the ball over the line from close range with his heel after team-mate Forrest drilled an angled shot across the face of goal from 10 yards following a corner from Fin Robertson that was not dealt with by the hosts.

United knocked on the door in the closing stages but Dundee rarely looked like relinquishing their sense of authority.

What the managers said...

Dundee manager Steven Pressley:

"I was probably a bit more animated than usual today because we obviously set out with a tactical game plan and we carried virtually none of it out.

"Truth be told, I didn't see evidence of hardly any of our detail today, but what it did show me is that derby games are not won on tactical detail.

"They're won on courage, they're won on determination, they're won on grit, all the things that my players served up today, so I couldn't be prouder.

"We've spoken in the week about how we find ways to win away from home, and I think that was a good example of it. You don't always need to play particularly well, but when you show that determination you've got a chance."

Dundee United boss Jim Goodwin:

"I know what this game is all about, at the end of the day, it's all about winning games, results are what matter most.

"I don't need to look at the stats from the game today to see that we've probably had more possession of the ball, more attempts on goal, more penalty box entries, more dangerous attacks.

"But it counts for nothing if we don't have the three points to show for it at the end of it."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Man Utd lack guts and fight, but can Leeds dare to dream?
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Manchester United

Hull nailed their set-up with a back five too physical for Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, and wing-backs in Lewie Coyle and Ryan Giles who served target man Oli McBurnie well.

But this was about fight and spirit over anything on Sergej Jakirovic's tactics board. Winning almost two thirds of both their duels and headers before the break was just reward for the intensity, energy and belief they brought to the game - and United did not match it.

It was inevitable that the Tigers would be fired up after riding the wave of promotion, but it felt as though Michael Carrick's side hadn't realised. They failed to do the basics right and were punished.

A video of McBurnie dribbling around a static Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans will rightly do the rounds on social media and only epitomised their performance on Humberside.

People may point to a lack of quality in the Man Utd side but without the hunger and desire to do those basics, it would have made little difference.

Ron Walker

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi spoke about creating a "team I have in my dream" after securing Premier League survival at the end of last season. Well, the new season has started in nightmare fashion.

In their 3-0 defeat at Brentford, Spurs were as bad as they were during that relegation dogfight last year.

After spending over £230m in the transfer window and fielding five debutants at the Gtech, that's hard to fathom. They should have been transformed. That was the expectation.

But it was not the quality of the players on the pitch that was the issue - it was, once again, the mentality.

"We were not ready to fight," admitted De Zerbi. "The first XI was able to compete."

New faces, a new captain but a familiar problem after Spurs' application was repeatedly criticised last season.

The stats reflected it on Saturday. In that shocking first half, Spurs striker Richarlison managed to win just two of his eight duels. At the other end of the pitch, new centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke won just two of his seven.

Spurs were repeatedly second to the ball, outmuscled in challenges and run over by an incredibly intense Brentford side. The second goal was the perfect illustration of that.

More signings look certain before the transfer window closes. But unless De Zerbi can shift the mentality of this group his ambitions at Spurs will remain an elusive dream.

Peter Smith

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Everton and Crystal Palace

Everton's performance in victory over Crystal Palace was symptomatic of a team maturing under the influence of wily David Moyes. He fielded the second-youngest XI of his second stint at the club, inviting questions over the suitability of his inexperienced midfield.

But young Harrison Armstrong and new signing Hayden Hackney dovetailed perfectly, unafraid of their elevated Premier League stage. And others shone, too.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall delivered a masterful display, scoring a wonderful opener to set the tone. Under-the-radar Iliman Ndiaye was equally impactful. He has more Premier League goal involvements for Everton than any other player since his debut in 2024-25 (15G, 4A).

Everton made big strides following the return of Moyes last term and now have the potential to double down on that progress. No doubt Moyes needs a bit of help from the decision-makers at the club to climb higher in the table. He wants a right-back before the transfer window closes. And talk of a reunion with Jack Grealish offers more hope of investment and improvement.

With a few more signings, there are plenty of reasons for optimism in the blue corner of Merseyside.

Laura Hunter

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United

Daniel Farke is keen to quash any prospect that anything but survival is possible this season, but Leeds have started the new campaign in the same way they ended the last one.

Only reigning champions Arsenal have picked up more points since the start of April than the Whites - who have lost just once in their last ten games. Leeds are still very hard to beat.

This win over Forest was about defensive solidity. The back five that transformed the last campaign is still going strong. The back three of Jaka Bijol, Joe Rodon and Tarik Muharemovic make 18 clearances between them, while James Justin and Anton Stach won a combined 21 duels on their own.

That solidity earned them a first win - and first clean sheet of the season. Last season, they had to wait until New Year's Day for their first shutout on the road. Advances are already being made on last season - how far above last season's 14th spot could this team go?

Sam Blitz

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry

Vinicius Jr this, Morgan Rogers that... Arsenal have shown that their transfer window was better than many made out.

Christos Tzolis looks like a gem, a real livewire down the left wing. After a stale opening five minutes on the pitch, he set it alight with two shots and two chances created in the space of four minutes.

It was no surprise to see him strongly involved in the two goals that put this game to bed, winning the ball high up for the first, then crossing for Bukayo Saka for the second.

But Martin Odegaard's start to the season cannot be overlooked either. He backed up the stunning Community Shield display with a first goal of the season here, equalling his league tally last season that saw him miss 30 matches in all competitions.

"When he plays better, the team's a lot better. So we're happy to have him in this level," said Saka about Odegaard after the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka joined us after the Coventry victory to talk fitness, attack, and Ezri Konsa joining Arsenal

In fact, this was just the second time since December 2024 that Saka, Odegaard and Kai Havertz started together. All three scored against Coventry.

That trio are like new signings. And with three open-play goals, Arsenal look like a new team.

Sam Blitz

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Ipswich's game against Sunderland in the Premier League

Gary O'Neil needed a fast start as Ipswich boss - to give everyone the chance to move on from Kieran McKenna and turn the next page.

McKenna had taken the club from League One to the Premier League, created an identity and, ultimately, made Ipswich believe they belonged at this level.

That is a difficult act to follow.

O'Neil, though, has now got his first significant result to put his name on.

There was an authority in flashes about Ipswich's performance that suggested they aren't simply going to be making up the numbers this season. They were aggressive without the ball, willing to commit bodies forward and, crucially, showed the character to respond when Sunderland threatened to wrestle control away from them.

There will inevitably be comparisons with McKenna for a while. That's natural. But the quickest way to silence those is to win football matches.

Ipswich have done exactly that.

Lewis Jones

Image: Igor Jesus missed a few big chances for Nottingham Forest vs Leeds

Igor Jesus could have won the game for Nottingham Forest against Leeds. He had two golden chance to score from two Ola Aina balls in - one was saved by James Trafford, the other header bounced over.

But despite the misses, there was a lot to like about the Brazilian forward. He was at the heart of everything good for Forest - especially in terms of shrugging players off. He won 11 duels - seven more than his opposite man Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and four more than the other two Forest starting forwards.

Oliver Glasner took Jean-Philippe Mateta to a different level at Crystal Palace and looking at the early signs of Jesus, there is no reason why the Brazilian cannot become a big player for both club and country.

Strikers will be judged on goals, but Jesus is showing a lot of potential and desire to make his own chances and get into the right areas. Don't sleep on him just yet.

Sam Blitz

Sports.title: De Zerbi admits 'we're not a team yet' as Redknapp labels Spurs 'strangers'
Sports.content:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi believes their dismal 3-0 opening-season defeat at Brentford shows his new-look side are "not a team yet" after a big summer of spending.

The Italian also admitted they lacked fight in the loss but felt they were undercooked for their opener, as Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp labelled them a "team of strangers".

Spurs' summer spending is set to surpass the £300m mark, with deals advancing for Manchester City pair Savinho and Omar Marmoush.



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur

But despite five of Tottenham's six summer arrivals featuring against Brentford, Spurs were stung badly by the Bees in a deserved defeat that epitomised their back-to-back 17th-place finishes after avoiding relegation on the final day last season.

De Zerbi said at his post-match press conference: "I think we are not a team yet, for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target when you become a team. Before (we) become a team, we can't say what we can do.

"We are not in the right point in physical condition for a lot of reasons. For the players, they came late after the World Cup because in Australia [pre-season tour] we couldn't work in the right way for the trip; we don't take risks for a lot of things.

"But (these) are not excuses, (this is) the normal situation when you are building a new project, a new process. I don't want time, but we have to pass through these problems.

"I believe in my players, I believe in my club, I believe in myself. After the Hoffenheim game [final pre-season game last weeked], I said we are not in the right point, we are late for the start of the Premier League, but it's a step; we have to improve quickly.

"We could fight stronger than we did today. We lost too many duels, we made too many mistakes in the timing when we wanted to push the pressure higher. We arrived second on the second ball; we didn't win one second ball, one duel, one tackle, and it's tough."

He added: "Now the focus and the target is to become a team because a team. You can't become a team for the transfer market window - the player on paper, no.

"You become a team with the players; they find the connection between them, they find the spirit, they find the soul - it's a process."

Redknapp: Spurs looked a 'team of strangers' Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:



"You'd say they were a team of strangers; they didn't have that extra know-how of when (Jan Paul) Van Hecke and (Marcos) Senesi become a partnership.



"They never really won enough duels. I never really liked the look of the team when I saw the XI. I don't like (Conor) Gallagher in the 10, I wondered where the creativity was going to be.



"The hope for Tottenham is that they won't be the same side in six weeks. But there were so many disappointing factors. They've got to be better than they were today - all the fundamentals you need to win a match, they didn't do."

De Zerbi's two 'big conditions' to become 'a team'

Tottenham will aim to earn their first victory of the new season on Wednesday as they host Championship side Charlton in the Carabao Cup second round, live on Sky Sports, before hosting Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday, also live on Sky Sports.

The ex-Brighton boss said: "We have to become a team, and to become a team, in my home, there are two big conditions: the soul and the style of play, and today, we didn't show the soul, and we didn't show the quality of the play with the ball and without the ball.

"When we find these two conditions, I think we can become dangerous for everyone.

"Until we reach these conditions, we have to suffer, and today, I think this defeat is important for us because maybe we woke up stronger than we thought."

He added: "We need time, but I think we are much better than we showed today. So, from Wednesday, we can show our qualities and who we are.

"But even if we win Wednesday or next Saturday, we need time to become a team."

De Zerbi admits starting Bergvall was a risk

Spurs conceded a soft second goal as Lucas Bergvall gave the ball to allow Mathias Jensen's saved shot that led to Vitaly Janelt's rebound strike.

Bergvall was substituted at half-time for Rodrigo Bentancur, and De Zerbi admitted he knew the 20-year-old would struggle with Brentford's physicality, but the experienced Bentancur was not fit enough to start.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Vitaly Janelt hit Brentford's second

He said: "Lucas Bergvall for the second goal. I think he didn't play badly today, even if I substituted at half-time.

"But Lucas Bergvall, in the next two years, he will not lose that ball in that moment of the game."

He added: "If you analyse last season, the defensive line is: (Pedro) Porro, (Kevin) Danso, Micky van de Ven and (Destiny) Udogie. And today, Archie Gray, JP Van Hecke, (Marcos) Senesi and (Andy) Robertson - four new players.

"Two midfielders [last season]: Rodrigo Bentancur and (Joao) Palhinha. Today, two midfielders: Bergvall (and Tonali). Why not Bentancur? Because he came late in the pre-season.

"In the pre-season, we worked with Lucas Bergvall. I think at the beginning of the season, the new project, it was right to play with Lucas Bergvall. But I knew before the game that Lucas Bergvall, in this type of game, maybe he could suffer more than Rodrigo Bentancur, who is 29 years old and Lucas is 20. I knew before the game, but at the end you have to think. We go and we try to build something good for the club.

Tottenham Hotspur

Newcastle United Saturday 29th August 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

"For the plan, for the project, what the club want and what we are in the direction we are working, I think is the normal process.

"Even if we are suffering for defeat, we are shocking for this defeat, especially for the way we lost the game, because they deserve to win and we played very, very bad."

Gray: Brentford outfought us

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Kayode added a third

Archie Gray became Spurs' youngest-ever captain in a competitive fixture as he took the armband in the absence of new skipper Micky van de Ven.

The 20-year-old, who played at right-back due to Pedro Porro's late return from Spain's World Cup win, admitted the team lacked fight in the defeat.

He told Sky Sports: "It was simple really: we lost too many duels. They just outfought us all over the park. We need to watch it back: that's the main thing we need to do better.

"For whatever reason, we weren't up for the fight as they were. That's on us. For the fans, they were incredible, for us to let them down like that in the first game, there are no words for it."

Sports.title: Sherrock claims first Women's Series title of 2026 in the absence of Greaves
Sports.content:
Lisa Ashton and Fallon Sherrock shared the spoils at Events 17-18 of the PDC Women’s Series on Saturday, as the duo scooped a title each to reinforce their positions of second and third in the rankings respectively.

Leicester's Mattioli Arena played host to a double-header of Women's Series action, with Ashton and Sherrock celebrating success in Event 17 and 18.

Ashton stormed to the Event 17 crown, breezing to the last 16 with a trio of whitewash victories, before conceding just a solitary leg against Lauren Hall to reach the quarter-finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool

The Lancaster-based arrowsmith then saw off Grace Ferridge 5-1, although she faced a stern test against Gemma Hayter in the semi-finals, edging through a last-leg decider to reach the showpiece.

Nevertheless, the 2025 Women's World Matchplay champion swept aside Lauryn Salter with ease, triumphing 5-0 to lift her third Women's Series title of 2026.

Although Salter fell short, she broke new ground by competing in her first final on the Women's Series after previously reaching the semi-finals at Event 12 earlier in the year.

Salter accounted for Emma Pearce and Jade Gofford in the quarter-finals and semi-finals respectively, shooting up to 16th in the Women's Series rankings as a result of her groundbreaking run to the final.

In Event 18, Sherrock denied Ashton a second title of the day with a rampant 5-0 win in the final to scoop her first Women's Series title in over 16 months.

After conceding just one leg in defeating Hollie McKain and Julie Whitehouse, the 32-year-old saw off Jody Hancock with a 93 average before easing past Leanne Topper to reach the last eight.

The 2022 Women's World Matchplay winner dispatched Aoife McCormack 5-0 before battling past Hayter 5-3 in the last four to reach her fourth final of the year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fallon Sherrock famously knocked out Mensur Suljovic in the second round of the World Darts Championship in 2019

In a rematch of July's Women's World Matchplay semi-final, Sherrock locked horns with Ashton, replicating the result courtesy of a 5-0 victory to take home her first title on the circuit in 2026.

Beau Greaves - absent from Saturday's action - remains on top of the Women's Series rankings, with Ashton and Sherrock bolstering their positions in second and third respectively.

The top three players from the final PDC Women's Series rankings will qualify to compete in the 2026/27 Paddy Power World Darts Championship, with the top-ranked player also qualifying for the 2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts.
