Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi says Tottenham are ‘not a team’ and hits out at lack of fight
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi said that Tottenham are “not a team” after they opened their season with a humiliating 3-0 defeat away to Brentford.

Spurs are looking to kick on after almost going down last season and are expected to spend more than £300m this summer but they were handed a rude awakening at the Gtech Community Stadium. Brentford outclassed the north Londoners and left De Zerbi rueing a lack of fight from his players, bemoaning his side’s physical conditioning and suggesting that the pre-season tour of Australia was less than ideal.

“We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons,” the Tottenham manager said. “Before you become a team you can’t say what you can do. We are not in the right physical condition for a lot of reasons. Some players came back late from the World Cup. In Australia we don’t work in the right way but it is not excuses. It is a normal situation when building a new project.

“I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems. I cannot lose confidence in my players. I believe in my players, my club, myself. We are working well. We have to improve quickly. We could fight stronger than we did today. We lost too many duels today. We arrived second in the second balls. We didn’t win one second ball, one duel, one tackle.”

Spurs handed debuts to Andy Robertson, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali. They are close to strengthening their attack by signing Omar Marmoush and Savinho from Manchester City but De Zerbi needs to build a collective.

“There are steps to become better,” he said. “Now the target is to become a team. You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul. It’s a project.”

De Zerbi pointed out that he was without Pedro Porro, Kevin Danso and Micky van de Ven. He said that Rodrigo Bentancur, who started on the bench, came back late in pre-season.

It was a fine way for Brentford to start their second year under Keith Andrews. Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode scored and there was an outstanding debut in midfield from Mamadou Sangaré, the £39m signing from Lens.

“The club deserve a lot of credit for getting that deal done,” Andrews said of Sangaré. “You’ve seen today what he’s capable of, the attributes he has. It adds to a talented midfield. I really enjoyed his performance today. He’s slotted in really well. He’s a humble young man who’s very, very hungry.”

Sports.title: Carrick tells Manchester United to keep calm and carry on after Hull humbling
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says he will not overreact, but has called for improvement after Manchester United started the season with a 2-0 defeat at Hull. United lost their opening game for the fourth time in the past seven years as Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy took advantage of poor defending from set-pieces.

The United head coach presented a professional exterior despite United’s performance not reaching the desired standard as they were deservedly beaten by Hull, who finished sixth in the Championship last season.

“I’m talking to you quite calmly, but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, so there’s a big difference,” he said. “I played [for United] for a long time. You don’t get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal.

“It’s 100% not that, and trust me, it’s not that. It just doesn’t mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it. Inside we’re hurting and we need to get better. But the calmness doesn’t mean there’s no emotion in it, for sure.”

He added: “The result’s the result. We got beat, we’re hurt and it’s not a nice feeling. It doesn’t mean it’s going to change the whole direction of how we’re going as a team or as a football club.

“It’s one game and results can happen in football, we all understand that. It’s not nice when they do, but it does happen.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes (left) looks dejected after the match against Hull City Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

United barely threatened throughout the 90 minutes. “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game,” Bruno Fernandes said. “We gave too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time. We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hull’s head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, said he and his backroom staff had spotted a weakness in the way United defended set-pieces, but would not divulge his “secret” that helped to expose it.

Hull are strongly tipped for relegation and their supporters sung “are you watching Joe Cole?” during the match after the pundit mocked their chances of survival. “I don’t have any problems with critics with opinions,” Jakirovic said. “We tried to prove them wrong and today we won the game. Now it’s 37 to go, so we will try to continue like this. I’m very, very happy because of all the people in the club.”

Sports.title: Infantino angers Concacaf nations by hijacking meeting in Caribbean
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has risked alienating numerous Concacaf nations, whose support he is seeking in his re-election campaign, by hijacking a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) to announce Fifa-funded development projects for the region with millions of dollars that had been delayed for months.

Multiple sources attending the CFU meeting in the Dominican Republic said many of the Concacaf members were infuriated by Infantino’s behaviour, particularly as he had been asked to stay away by their president, Victor Montagliani.

The Concacaf position echoes previous complaints about Fifa’s operations from the Jordan FA, whose president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, accused Infantino of bribery this month when he claimed they have not received prize money from last year’s Arab Cup due to the country’s failure to endorse the president.

Infantino appears to have seen the CFU meeting as an opportunity to lobby for election votes among Caribbean countries in the hope of causing a split within Concacaf, who have aligned with Uefa and the Asian Football Confederation in demanding his resignation after the World Cup sell-off debacle.

In a letter addressed to Infantino on Friday, Montagliani had asked the Fifa president “in the name of football to reconsider your attendance”, pointing out his presence would take the spotlight away from a regional under-14 tournament being held alongside the meeting.

Despite that entreaty, Infantino is understand to have turned up at the resort of Punta Cana with a large Fifa entourage including the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, and Elkhan Mammadov, a staunch ally who is responsible for maintaining good relations with the 211 members in his role as director of member associations.

Before making funding pledges in the CFU meeting, Infantino’s team are understood to have approached individual member associations lobbying for support. Mammadov has played a central role in attempts to keep them onside since the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal broke and his insistent approach has caused disquiet in some quarters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

One source said the official Fifa party had attempted to portray their governance crisis as a private dispute between Infantino and Montagliani. The Canadian businessman has not commented since news of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise emerged, but has been widely touted in Europe as a possible contender to replace Infantino.

The pair met briefly and shook hands before the CFU meeting in an exchange captured by Infantino’s personal camera crew.

While Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have all broken with Concacaf and declared their support for Infantino, the majority of their 41 members are understood to back the alliance with Uefa advocated by Montagliani.

The Uefa/Concacaf pact extends beyond attempts to unseat Infantino, with the two confederations in talks about setting up a joint Nations League in 2028 that could develop further into a new global competition.

Sports.title: José Mourinho marks Real Madrid return with late drama and touch of humility | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
José Mourinho says he is calmer now so when the rest of the bench emptied, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate the 90th-minute goal that finally delivered victory on his first game in charge of Real Madrid in 4,380 days, he didn’t set off with them. Instead, he clenched his fists, got to his feet and walked down the touchline behind the subs, watching them head, shouting, towards Carlos Espí. As they piled on down in the corner, he pulled over his captain Fede Valverde for a word. Which might just have been: phew.

For all those stars; for all that Mourinho’s main task might just have been been to find a way to fit Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham together; for all that he had introduced Yan Diomande, the most expensive player in the club’s history, it was a 21-year-old, unknown six months ago and unexpectedly signed from Levante, who got the goal that secured victory upon the coach’s second coming.

Espí, whose goals had rescued Levante from relegation last season and who is still living at Madrid’s Valdebebas training ground like his coach, the two of them sharing breakfast every morning, was signed for pretty much this: to be a different type of striker, an old-school No 9, with a presence in the area. And when a scrappy, broken-up move ended with Mbappé seeing the ball run away from him in the area, there he was to force it over the line. Perhaps even to pose a question: is his a profile they could do with and not just in reserve? This time, at least, it had worked.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Espí celebrates the late winner for Real Madrid. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Mourinho’s first game since a 4-2 win over Osasuna in May 2013 began with the photographers abandoning their places behind the goal to surround him on the bench, no doubt what the attraction was; it ended with him hugging the Espanyol coach Manolo González, high-fiving the referee and ducking down the tunnel. In between time, reality was revealed, which he surely always imagined it would be: it is early, solutions are never immediate, and he had said that Espanyol were a good side. At times, they showed it too. Madrid had more chances, but Manolo’s team had largely succeeded in limiting the visitors.

On a night where Madrid exhibited some of the old flaws, there were doubts still – it is the first day after all – but they were at least allayed for a little while. There will be other days, sterner tests of this team; there will also be sterner tests of Mourinho’s temperament, of course.

When Madrid faced Benfica in the spring, Mourinho had described his time there as “three hard, intense, sometimes violent years”. But the thing about nostalgia is that as the bad slips into the distance, only the good remains. Mourinho said that he is “not the kind of man who misses anything”, someone who has “regrets”; plenty though had missed him, the president Florentino Pérez first among them. In his world view, managers are mostly a necessary evil; the Portuguese is virtually the only coach he had ever truly liked.

There are those who had longed for exactly that intensity, violence even: for a hard man to lead them, some kind of iron surgeon to fix them and go to war with their rivals, someone with the personality to impose. For all that by the end they really could not go on, at some level Pérez had always been drawn to Mourinho’s return. He clung to the idea that their success after his departure – six Champions League wins in 11 years – was down to him, that he had made it possible. He had shown the way.

Mourinho told a story on the eve of this game revealing that after every trophy Madrid won he would have got a call from Pérez. “I always said no, no, no, it was nothing to do with me,” he said, which was a neat way of saying it kind of was. This was not a confidence betrayed: Pérez had said much the same. It took the president 13 years to attend to his urge, but now Mourinho was back.

And, perhaps, why not? The last returnees had done rather well, while all the others had failed. There was a moment at the end of that story when Mourinho said the trophies belonged to Zinedine Zidane and Carlo Ancelotti, not him, and innocently checked that they were the only men to have won anything. The diagnosis of their ills, the challenge before them, required his surgery too. Like in 2010, Madrid had fallen behind Barcelona. They have not won a major title in two years, and that was about culture as well as football.

View image in fullscreen A first look of Yan Diomande in action for Real Madrid against Espanyol. Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images

It may not be as simple as effort but that is a start. “We have to try not to negotiate things that are non-negotiable,” Mourinho said. “Commitment can’t be missing.” Mourinho has the authority to change that, or so it goes. He would be afforded it, anyway. That at least is the theory. Habits had been changed, demands made. Sessions had improved, or the attitude towards them. Diomande had said he was ready to “die” for his coach, who insisted that was just a phrase, but he could not help but be pleased with that.

There were other reasons to be optimistic. Vinícius’s future had been resolved at last, no lingering doubts over status or resentment. The World Cup is out the way, no other priority on the horizon. Mourinho noted that Brazil, France and England had found a way to get the best out of Vinícius, Mbappe and Bellingham, but that getting the best of all three is different. “I don’t think they’re incompatible,” he insisted; last year it often looked like they were, Bellingham, admitting that they find themselves occupying the same spaces at times.

Here, they all started. Bellingham was at No 10, Vinícius tight to the touchline. “For me this is his [Jude’s] position: the connection with the forwards, he can score goals. He has to play close to the goal. Playing at 6 or 8 we’re losing his closeness to the goal,” said Mourinho.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellingham had an immediate impact, the first goal of this new era coming from a dead ball and after nine minutes. Vinícius was fouled, which was already looking like becoming a pattern – Alex Calatrava had already given him a kick in the back, prompting Mourinho to raise his arms – and from the left, Arda Guler delivered a superb cross. Bellingham leapt highest to head past Marko Dimitrovic.

View image in fullscreen Jude Bellingham celebrates after giving Real the lead. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

This time, sitting on the left end of the bench, Mourinho barely flinched. He got up, put his hands in his pockets and walked along the touchline to the other end where the rest of his sizeable staff sat in the overspill in the stand beyond the other end. There, he shook hands with Sami Khedira, the in-house assistant Madrid have provided him, and Roberto Merella, the analyst.

And that, it was tempting to assume, was that. The gap between the teams looked insurmountable. Madrid were pressing high, Espanyol barely able to find a way out. Here was a glimpse, they might have hoped, of the future. Instead, the intensity dropped again and that was an invitation for Espanyol.

When Dean Huijsen needed attention for a cut, Madrid’s players came to Mourinho for instructions but the game started to slip from them a little. Espanyol took a step forward and soon had an equaliser. Thibaut Courtois saved from Riedel, Roberto Fernández unable to keep down the follow-up. Then a lovely move concluded with Tuy Dolan and Javi Hernández setting up Calatrava to score. Mourinho sat almost motionless.

Twice Mbappé escaped to force saves from Dimitrovic, one on each side of the area, but it was Espanyol who should have led at the break. Again, the ball was worked into position. From the right, Omar El Hilali provided a superb cross. Dolan couldn’t quite get to it, inside the six-yard box, and Fernández headed it straight at his own feet. Mbappé may wonder how he didn’t put Madrid into the lead just after the break. From Guler’s corner, Bellingham headed against the bar, via Dimitrovic’s hand, and the ball dropped to the Frenchman right by the post. Somehow, it went wide.

Valverde hit the post, Mbappé shot wide, but there was no way through. Mourinho turned to the men behind him – Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Alexander-Arnold, Espí – until, at last, he saw them dash past him, given a reprieve on his return.

“I think we deserved to win, but Espanyol didn’t deserve to lose,” Mourinho said as he ended the night with a touch of humility.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca searches for ‘new Rodri’ and expects Manchester City reaction
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has brushed off the loss of Rodri to Barcelona for £65m by stating Manchester City will search for the “new Rodri” in the same way Sergio Agüero was replaced by Erling Haaland.

Rodri’s departure is a sizable blow to the club’s new manager as he embarks on a first season in charge. Yet the Italian is not fazed by the absence of a player considered one of the world’s best No 6s.

“How do we solve that problem? We try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is. [Before] Rodri arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. He joined the club, then he achieved many important things.

“Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri. I was thinking on Thursday night, when David Silva was here, everyone was worried and Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio [Agüero] was here, everyone was worried [when he was going to leave] and Erling [Haaland] arrived. Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this. When they leave, you need to be good at recruiting the next one.

“They are all similar, David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling – it is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.”

Rodri had expressed his desire to leave City and Maresca said – as did his predecessor, Pep Guardiola – he would not stand in the way of any player who wishes to leave. “He can go, absolutely. If he is not happy, he is not going to perform in the right way,” he said.

City lost 3-0 to Arsenal in last Sunday’s Community Shield in Cardiff and before Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth for their Premier League opener, Maresca said the critical reaction to the loss had been expected.

“It was good, and normal. It is normal that you are upset straight after the game. We were all upset,” said the manager. “We wanted to win, we didn’t win so it’s a normal reaction but after Tuesday we started to prepare for Bournemouth, you have to switch off one thing and focus on the next one. It was two days where we were not happy and now the focus has to be Bournemouth.”

Maresca has been pleased with how the players are training now he is in charge and not Guardiola. “Since day one the attitude has been very good,” he said. “For them it is not easy. When you work with the same person every day then change, it changes everything.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I am an actor and I work with the same director, and we make movies for 10 years. Suddenly the director changes, me as the actor I’m still thinking in the same way as I was with the previous director but now the director is new so I need to adapt. It’s complicated, it’s not easy. It’s not an excuse but it requires a little bit of time, but we need to compete as soon as possible.”

Maresca has an ideal size for his squad. “We have three or four academy players that will stay with us because they impressed me in pre-season. Kaden [Braithwaite], [Floyd] Samba and Ryan McAidoo. Then, for me personally we need around 21-22 players. Around 20 players plus these three young players full of energy – we are happy.”

Sports.title: Burnham’s boys enjoy visit from Palace as Everton ease to victory in opener
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham was in the posh seats to see how his beloved Everton would fare without the key additions that even the prime minister has voiced an opinion on. No right-back, no new centre-forward, no problem: Everton contained enough quality to overcome a wasteful Crystal Palace.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Iliman Ndiaye delivered a timely reminder that, despite the missing pieces in the squad, there is pedigree and Premier League knowhow available to David Moyes as he attempts to sustain a challenge for European qualification this season.

Dewsbury-Hall swept home an outstanding finish to give Everton the lead and sweep away any lingering resentment over how last season flatlined. Ndiaye supplied the superb cross that invited Thierno Barry to seal Everton’s first opening game win since 2021. It was a brutal introduction for the new Palace manager, Pierre Sage, who lost defender Chadi Riad to a potentially serious knee injury late on.

“I spoke to the prime minister on the phone,” Moyes said. “Andy Gray came down into the office [before the game] and his assistant Peter Reid phoned down.”

Reid was Burnham’s chaperone for the day – along with a phalanx of security – and put the prime minister on the phone during his call to Moyes. His good luck message was answered, thanks in part to Palace’s profligacy.

There were no radical changes in formation or personnel from Sage for his first Premier League outing. A lack of cutting edge was familiar from the Oliver Glasner era, too. The visitors created three clear opportunities before Everton took the lead and failed to take any. Misfortune played its part in two of the chances, with Jordan Pickford’s left post struck twice, but that did not diminish the torment for Sage and the travelling support. A sense of the inevitable from Everton increased with each one.

Palace denied reports that Ismaïla Sarr had refused to play because of a desire to join Galatasaray – the Senegal international was absent due to a groin injury, according to his manager – and the disruption had no effect on their start. Eddie Nketiah created an early opportunity for Jean-Philippe Mateta, but his strike partner volleyed over at the near post.

View image in fullscreen Moved from his usual seat into the directors’ box by prime pinisterial security logistics, Andy Burnham celebrated with the Everton legend, and his good friend, Peter Reid. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Chance number two came from a sublime pass by Adam Wharton, the midfielder who Sage has insisted is going nowhere despite interest from Manchester City. Wharton found Nketiah free inside the area with a perfectly weighted ball over Merlin Röhl, forced to deputise at right-back in the absence of a conclusion to Everton’s almost farcical search for Séamus Coleman’s successor.

Nketiah had time to pick his spot but Pickford produced a superb save to tip the shot on to a post. Mateta struck the same post from another Nketiah cross and Everton took full advantage of their reprieves.

Everton grew into their opening game, with the summer signings Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Röhl all impressing. Creativity was initially in short supply from the home side, despite George’s constant probing on the left, until Dewsbury-Hall and Ndiaye imposed themselves on proceedings.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Dewsbury-Hall’s impact was worth the wait. The midfielder burst into life with a mazy run that ended with an appeal for handball when his shot hit Chris Richards. Play continued through Daniel Muñoz, a possible Everton right-back target, who was dispossessed by the industrious Harrison Armstrong and left a void for Dewsbury-Hall to exploit. Receiving Armstrong’s pass, the 27-year-old swept an unstoppable, angled drive into Dean Henderson’s far corner to open the season in style for Everton.

View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry outjumped Chris Richards to head Everton into a two-goal lead just after half-time. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

Muñoz should have made amends when stealing in ahead of George to meet an inviting delivery from Daichi Kamada. Palace’s end product did not match the buildup yet again, however, and the Colombian defender guided his header wide of the far post.

Everton found the comfort of a two-goal lead when Ndiaye delivered a peach of a cross from the right. Barry, on a self-confessed mission to improve after a difficult debut season in the Premier League, rose between Richards and Jaydee Canvot to head past Henderson at close range. The departure of the unfortunate Riad on a stretcher compounded Palace’s deflating afternoon.

Sports.title: Aston Villa upheaval is a risk but Emery can release v2.0 and reap rewards | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Last season was the greatest Aston Villa have enjoyed since they won the European Cup in 1982. They claimed their second European trophy by lifting the Europa League, but even without that would have secured Champions League qualification by finishing fourth in the Premier League.

Despite a miserable start during which they failed to win any of their first five league games, there was even a spell around Christmas when it looked as though Villa might be challengers for the title. The question after a season like that is always: where next?

The answer is probably less clear now than it was amid the delirium of Istanbul in May. A reasonable consideration, even a couple of weeks ago, would have been: was that a one-off high, the limit of the club’s ambitions, or was there more? The danger for any team, but particularly one relatively unfamiliar with success, is to rest on its laurels, to be too loyal to those who have brought the long-awaited silverware.

It’s an understandable enough impulse: any transfer comes with a risk, so why make changes when what was there before worked? Why offload players to whom there is a sense of gratitude? Villa have not rested on their laurels.

Three major players – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa – have left, Emí Martínez seems likely to join them and Ollie Watkins might go as well. This is not a fire sale. Nor is it a club cashing in while it still can. But it probably wasn’t quite planned this way either. The exodus is a combination of accepting that certain players are ready to fly the nest and trying to make as much money from them as possible for a rejuvenation of the squad. The danger is that too much is being changed too quickly.

Those changes have not just been among the playing staff. Two physios and the head of the medical team went to Arsenal. Jaime Arias Galán, a technical assistant, has left. The individual development coach, Rodri, went to Como. Most significantly, Unai Emery’s assistant, Pako Ayestarán, departed, while the set-piece coach, Austin MacPhee, went to Chelsea. There are always changes among backroom staff and the impact is hard for outsiders to assess but, still, the departures add to the sense of flux and uncertainty.

There is logic in the changes to playing personnel, though. Rogers is 24 and had been at the club for two and a half seasons. He scored 14 goals in all competitions in each of the past two seasons, many of them spectacular. He squeezed in the third goal in the Europa League final and will be remembered with great affection by Villa fans but he wanted to go for the better salary and perceived better opportunities (a risk, frankly) at Chelsea.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi was a flowing sight for Switzerland at the World Cup this summer. Photograph: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images

Once a player’s mind is set on leaving, there is rarely much point in standing in their way. An Alexander Isak at Newcastle situation helps nobody. Far better to accept the cash and reinvest it. For a player who cost £15m, a fee of £117m, less the 20% owed to Middlesbrough, represents excellent business.

Konsa is 28 but had two years left on his contract. A fee of £51m feels reasonable. Tielemans went after Manchester United triggered his £35m release clause. There was nothing Villa could have done but, given the Belgian is 29, they can at least console themselves that they’re selling a player they picked up on a free in summer 2023 for a reasonable price before any decline has begun. While no club enjoys losing high-class players, trading is a necessary part of squad development – and there is reason to be excited about Villa’s recruitment.

Johan Manzambi is a hugely gifted young attacking midfielder, Zion Suzuki is recognised as one of the most promising young goalkeepers in the world, João Gomes has already shown signs of the tenacity he can bring to the midfield and Matteo Ruggeri probably represents an upgrade on Lucas Digne at left-back. Alejandro Garnacho is a loan signing with potential. The Argentinian winger clearly has talent; the issue is releasing it consistently. Aaron Wan-Bissaka, reliable cover at right-back, has joined from relegated West Ham.

And all that with a net surplus of £160m, plus whatever they may get for Watkins should he leave. More signings will arrive. There is need of a defender to replace Konsa. Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson represents an obvious option to replace Watkins, given his capacity to exploit the space behind opposing defensive lines. The thought of him and Manzambi linking with Brian Madjo, the 17-year-old centre-forward who made such an impression in the Uefa Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, is undeniably enticing.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another central midfielder looks essential, particularly after Amadou Onana tore his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup. There will probably be at least one and possible two more creative players, one to operate centrally and one in the left.

View image in fullscreen Villa’s teenage forward Brian Madjo gave Paris Saint-German a torrid time in this month’s Super Cup. Photograph: Joao Bravo/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

That means potentially seven or eight major arrivals over the summer, and that is a lot. It hasn’t always been easy for new signings to adapt themselves to Emery’s methods. The Spaniard has insisted there are “six or seven contenders” who are better equipped than Villa this season.

Managers habitually try to play down expectation and, given the changes, it’s understandable Emery should take that stance. It may even be accurate. But it’s also true that a lot of sides have undergone a lot of change this season – and Villa at least have retained the same manager.

It may even be that this is a necessary stage of development, of rejuvenation and of the accumulation of capital before a renewed assault on the heights. Certainly the shift from Profitability and Sustainability Rules to squad cost ratio should suit Villa. But in an ideal world, all three of Rogers, Konsa and Tielemans would not have gone in the same summer; to undergo this much change at once is an enormous risk.

It is, though, risk with a potential upside, whereas sitting back and relishing the memory of last season would have led inevitably to decline. One phase is ending, a new one beginning and, while it might go wrong, Emery 2.0 may, in time, be even better for Villa than the first version.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Nuno admits West Ham ‘let down’ fans with Charlton defeat
Sports.content:
Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham in a pulsating London derby to pile more pressure on the Hammers manager, Nuno Espírito Santo.

Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell put Charlton 2-0 ahead before Joel Piroe, signed on loan from Leeds, marked his first appearance for the home side with a goal that set up a frantic finish. Taty Castellanos then missed a stoppage-time penalty for West Ham that would have salvaged a point.

West Ham have not won their past 10 derbies, losing nine of them, but Hammers head coach Nuno defended the decision for Castellanos to take the spot-kick instead of Jarrod Bowen.

He said: “We trust Taty to take the penalties. I don’t know [if he will take the next one], we will have to decide. We started badly again. We got punished from a situation where we know Charlton create problems. It became much harder but we still created a lot of situations but were not accurate enough in the boxes. Football is this – to be accurate in the offensive box and we have to defend much better.

“We had a lot of possession and tried to break them, which is not easy. We should have finished better. Of course, I feel under pressure. West Ham is pressure every day – it is a big club. You see that with 62,000 fans in the stands and we let them down. This is the more disappointing feeling. The boys tried until the end. We are going to repeat, repeat and repeat in training, in the final third, to create situations that allow us to score. We will keep the belief and the process.”

Fer López bagged a double as Wolves secured their first victory of the season with a convincing 3-1 success over Preston at Deepdale. The Spaniard put Wanderers ahead with an eighth-minute rocket and substitute Adam Armstrong tucked home a 71st-minute second, just four minutes after stepping on to the pitch.

López put a cherry on top of the cake with a poacher’s finish in the 82nd minute as César Peixoto’s men flexed their muscles, but substitute Jordan Thompson bagged a 25-yard consolation in the first minute of stoppage time to give the home faithful something to cheer.

View image in fullscreen Fer López scores Wolves’s third of the match to kill off Preston. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

It was a much-needed victory for the relegated Premier League side but Preston are now without a win in their opening two Championship matches.

Blackburn stunned Middlesbrough with two goals in the space of six second-half minutes to earn a 2-1 victory at Ewood Park which continues their impressive start to the season. After conceding late against Wolves, the early signs pointed to more misery for Rovers as Kim Hellberg’s side smothered them early and were rewarded through Jeremy Sarmiento’s composed 12th-minute finish.

Rovers created enough in that first half to give their fans encouragement and pounced after the break through Andri Gudjohnsen’s 49th-minute header – his second goal in as many games – and Todd Cantwell’s diving header six minutes later to complete the turnaround.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Skipp off as Leicester woe continues Show Leicester’s poor start to the League One season continued with a 2-1 defeat by Burton at the King Power Stadium, where Oliver Skipp was sent off (pictured). Russell Martin’s side – held 1-1 at Notts County in their opening league game following relegation – were behind to an early goal from Matthew Dennis, with Kgaogelo Chauke adding another for the Brewers in the 25th minute. Skipp was then shown a straight red card for a late challenge by the Foxes’ midfielder on Curtis Tilt, before Wes Burns reduced the deficit ahead of the break. Despite Leicester dominating possession in the second half, they could not find an equaliser. Jack Wilshere was happy his Luton players were disappointed to only claim a point from their 2-2 draw with Notts County at Kenilworth Road. The hosts had led through Nahki Wells’ 42nd-minute penalty but then found themselves 2-1 down with just over an hour gone, Cal Roberts netting before the break and Ollie Cooper also on target. Callum Marshall came off the bench to earn a point and Wilshere said: “I’m happy they’re disappointed we didn’t take all three points, we want that. However, my message to them was we’re not going to win every single game. We want to and we prepare every game like we want to win, however this league is demanding." Oxford beat Stevenage 2-1 at the Sporta Arena to secure a first league win under Aaron Ramsey. Huddersfield also continued their unbeaten start with a 1-1 draw at MK Dons, which puts them second. Victor Adeboyejo’s late goal gave Bromley a 1-1 draw with Cambridge, in what was the Ravens’ first home match in the third tier. Wigan sit bottom without a point after a 2-0 home defeat by Leyton Orient. Doncaster and Barnsley registered their first points of the season but were still searching for wins after a goalless stalemate. AFC Wimbledon and Reading ground out a 0-0 stalemate at Plough Lane in a game of few chances. Wycombe drew 1-1 at home to Plymouth, while Blackpool won 2-1 at Stockport. Peterborough won 2-1 at home to Mansfield. PA Media Photograph: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Divin Mubama scored a dramatic late goal on his home debut to help Southampton to a 3-1 victory over his former club Stoke. Almost a year ago, the Manchester City loan striker was sent off for Stoke at St Mary’s for diving.

Here, he was the hero as Saints dug deep to preserve an unbeaten home run which stretches back to January. Ryan Manning also scored a stoppage-time penalty after Svante Ingelsson was sent off for bringing down Samuel Edozie.

Cyle Larin bagged his third goal in as many games to give Tonda Eckert’s side an early lead but Stoke hit back through Ethan Galbraith and looked good value for a point until late on.

Wrexham were kept waiting for their first Championship win of the season as they drew 1-1 with Watford in front of Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac.

Both goals at the Racecourse Ground came in the opening quarter with Luca Kjerrumgaard’s header cancelled out by Danny Imray’s first Wrexham goal. It meant another draw for Wrexham after the Red Dragons were denied by a last-gasp Cardiff equaliser on Monday.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac watch Wrexham draw 1-1 with Watford. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

Cardiff remain unbeaten two games into their return to the second tier after goals by Cian Ashford and Yousef Salech earned a 2-2 draw at Derby.

The Bluebirds were good value for their point, having twice taken the lead in front of a raucous Pride Park crowd of 28,926. But the Rams, unconvincing for large periods, capitalised on defensive mishaps to earn their first point of the new campaign through Carlton Morris and Bobby Clark.

Taïryk Arconte scored his first two goals for Millwall as they breezed past 10-man Norwich 3-0 to make it two wins from two this season. Having been tipped to challenge for the playoffs, Norwich have lost both of their opening games and had defender José Córdoba sent off in the second half at The Den.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Millwall were rewarded for their lively start in the 18th minute when Mark Sykes’ ball found Josh Coburn, whose shot was pushed out by Vladan Kovacevic for Arconte to tap in the rebound on his home debut. They deservedly went 2-0 ahead after 58 minutes when Zak Sturge’s ball into the box was headed back by Jake Cooper for Arconte to steer a volley into the bottom corner.

Córdoba was sent off for a second yellow card after bundling over Arconte as he charged towards the area.

Victory was sealed with six minutes remaining when a slick counterattack ended with Luke Cundle sliding in Millwall’s third.

View image in fullscreen Tairyk Arconte celebrates scoring Millwall’s second goal of the game against Norwich City. Photograph: George Tewkesbury/Shutterstock

Alex Neil, the Millwall manager, said: “I thought it was a complete performance from us, probably the most complete performance we’ve had in the nearly 20 months I’ve been here.”

Portsmouth claimed their first win of the season with a comprehensive 3-1 success at Lincoln. Portsmouth found themselves under the cosh early on but a seventh-minute goal from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen put them in the driving seat.

Adrian Segecic doubled the lead nine minutes later before Reeco Hackett-Fairchild pulled one back from the spot just past the half-hour mark. Substitute Ebrima Adams made the game safe with a superb strike after 69 minutes to leave Lincoln still searching for their first win back in the second tier for more than 60 years.

Demarai Gray rescued a point for Birmingham with a late penalty in a 2-2 draw at home to Bristol City. Scott Twine’s 33rd-minute effort gave the visitors the advantage before they conceded a 42nd-minute equaliser to Carlos Vicente. Dom Ballard converted Rio Cardines’ cross with a superb flick with his back to goal after 85 minutes to restore Bristol City’s lead but they could not hold on.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Barnet and Crewe share 100% starts Show Barnet maintained their 100% with a 3-1 win at Shrewsbury, who are bottom after two defeats. Crewe also have six points after Josh March’s second-half goal secured a 1-0 victory over Northampton. Danny Cowley admitted Oldham’s red card changed the game after his Colchester side secured a last-gasp 2-1 win. Lewis Temple’s own goal in stoppage time handed United victory but Gus Scott-Morriss’s dismissal in the first half ultimately proved costly for Latics. Cowley said: “It’s always the best way to win [in stoppage time]. I’m not sure it’s good for the blood pressure but it was a great performance. I genuinely thought at XI v XI that we were the better team. Oldham are a really good team, but I really liked the way that we played. The sending-off naturally changed the game, so we made tactical tweaks. We were super young at the end, but we had enough energy and enthusiasm.” On the sending-off, Cowley added: “I’ll have to have another look. It looked high, and I did think that the ball was high as well.” Early goals earned Exeter a 2-0 win against Accrington Stanley. After a Devon derby defeat by Plymouth in the Carabao Cup and losing 1-0 at Grimsby last week, there was a bit of anxiety around St James Park, but captain Fitzwater settled any nerves inside two minutes with a terrific bicycle kick finish. Ten minutes later, it was 2-0 as a Gwion Edwards shot took a wicked deflection of Accrington skipper Seamus Conneely before ending up in the net. Rochdale’s first home game since promotion back to the EFL ended in a 2-1 defeat by Crawley, which was a second straight loss. York, though, are still unbeaten after coming from behind to draw 1-1 at Rotherham. Port Vale continued their winless start to the season with an entertaining 1-1 home draw with Tranmere. The centre-back Bobby Faulkner was forced to fill in as an emergency goalkeeper for Tranmere after Harrison Male was injured, before Tom Ince’s strike cancelled out George Byers’ first-half penalty to extend Rovers’ unbeaten start under Darrell Clarke. Bobby Kamwa scored against his former club as Bristol Rovers beat Newport 5-3 at the Memorial Stadium – where they had fallen behind after just 15 seconds. Swindon saw off their West Country rivals Cheltenham 2-1 at the County Ground, while Salford lost 1-0 at home to Chesterfield and are also still pointless. Fleetwood were held 0-0 at home by Gillingham, with Walsall v Grimsby also finishing goalless. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

QPR’s Richard Kone missed several chances in a goalless draw with Bolton at Loftus Road. Kone, left out for last weekend’s win at Portsmouth, was restored to the Rangers side but missed four clear-cut opportunities during a first half largely dominated by the hosts.

Callum O’Hare came closest to netting a winner but Sheffield United had to be content with a goalless draw at Swansea City.

West Brom have said they are “devastated” after the death of former midfielder Quevin Castro, aged 25.

Castro, who made two senior appearances for the Baggies during a two-year spell at the Hawthorns, collapsed during a friendly between his current club, third-tier Portuguese side Real Sport Clube, and Estrela da Amadora on Saturday and later died in hospital.

West Brom said: “West Brom are devastated to learn of the untimely passing of Quevin Castro, aged just 25. Albion will pay tribute to Quevin on Sunday, with a period of applause in the 25th minute of the fixture against Burnley. James Morrison’s men will also wear black armbands.”

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso backs 'world class' Cole Palmer to return to form this season and refuses to confirm if Robert Sanchez will be his starting keeper
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is determined to unlock the 'world class' side of Cole Palmer after Chelsea's playmaker suffered his first injury-plagued season to the detriment of his club.

The 2025-26 campaign saw Palmer struggle with a groin problem in particular but he also had other issues, including fracturing his little toe after stubbing it on a door at home. His limited influence contributed to Chelsea finishing 10th in the Premier League.

Before opening their campaign away at Fulham, Alonso spoke of how Palmer is pushing to avoid a recurrence of his previous injuries. 'Cole is determined to enjoy his football,' Chelsea's manager said. 'He wants to be fit. He wants to feel healthy.

'He wants to have a good connection with the players around him. We have this goal. If we are able to reach him and he feels that flow in the game and connects well with the players, I'm sure his level is top class, world class, and that he will have a great season.

Xabi Alonso is desperate to get the best out of Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer this season

'Sometimes you need to go through a moment with an injury or whatever to learn from that.

'Cole has gone through a difficult period with an injury and now he's working really hard to have the prevention to not feel those symptoms back. Since the first day, he's been working really hard to avoid that.'

Chelsea's trip to Fulham last season saw Marc Cucurella dismissed after 22 minutes as the 10-man visitors lost 2-1. The Blues received eight red cards in 2025-26 – the most of any club in the Premier League as their campaign was plagued by poor discipline.

Alonso has fined players before at previous clubs and said when asked how he will respond to reds at Chelsea: 'It depends on the context. You can have a red card. It's football. It can happen. There is always a context for everything but I don't have written rules for this kind of thing.

'We need to assess the particular cases. But for sure, having emotional control gives you the game control that we want to avoid these kinds of situations.'

Robert Sanchez is expected to start in goal versus Fulham over Mike Penders, though Xabi Alonso refused to confirm that. 'We want healthy competition in all the positions,' Alonso said. 'We will see. The pitch is the boss of everything. I don't decide. The players need to show me.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City urgently need to find a 'new Rodri' this summer - as race to complete deals before Deadline Day heats up
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca believes Manchester City can find ‘the new Rodri’ this month as they move on without their linchpin.

The Spain captain left for Barcelona last week, with City expected to wrap up a deal for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi during the transfer window.

With Elliot Anderson already signed, Maresca is confident that the new recruits can fill the void left by Rodri.

And Maresca pointed to the fact that the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner had never lifted major silverware before joining City in 2019 – underlining that they can mould signings into becoming the best in class.

‘Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri,’ Maresca said. ‘How do we solve the problem? Try to find the new Rodri.

‘Before he arrived, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. He joined the club then he achieved many important things.’

Enzo Maresca believes Man City can find their successor to Rodri by the end of this month

The Man City boss believes new recruits can fill the void left by the Spanish star

Rodri had made it clear that he wanted to leave the Etihad Stadium and Maresca has been unequivocal that any player eying a move away can depart, mirroring the principles of predecessor Pep Guardiola.

And the Italian claimed that life will move on, reeling off how City replaced previous big-name stars.

‘When Sergio [Aguero] was here, everyone was worried and Erling [Haaland] arrived,’ he added. ‘Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this.

‘When they leave, you need to be good in recruiting the next one. They are all similar, David [Silva], Kevin [De Bruyne], Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling. It is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.’

Meanwhile, Maresca confirmed that he is looking for a squad of around 20 outfield players. City currently have 19 senior players, excluding summer signing Jeremy Monga, but the number includes the likes of Tottenham target Omar Marmoush, Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez and Jack Grealish.

‘It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, that is for sure,’ Maresca added. ‘But we need to adapt. There are 10 days to go, hopefully we can do the things that we need to do.

‘The normal thing in the transfer window is that you have to wait until the last week, because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money. At the end, we’ll have all the squad here for sure it will be different.’

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Aston Villa agree terms with free agent Leon Goretzka: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Villa agree terms for Goretzka Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer. Pending a medical, the 31-year-old is expected to sign a three-year deal this week. Taylor Harwood-Bellis was left out of Southampton's squad to face Stoke City amid Villa's interest in the defender. Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer Villa have had an enquiry for Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Crystal Palace. Unai Emery's team are hunting a centre-forward with Al-Hilal pushing hard to sign Ollie Watkins. Villa are also ready to bid for Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea. Watkins has also been offered a new deal at Villa. Napoli sign Chelsea star on loan Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy. The loan fee is worth £2.5million and could rise to £3.4m with add-ons. The option price is around £23m. Chelsea could receive more than £26m from the deal if Badiashile moves permanently. They valued him at £30m in this window. Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy Napoli are also one of the clubs keen on Chelsea's Marc Guiu. He is weighing up options from Spain and Germany too. Hull City are exploring a loan for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo who is also wanted at Strasbourg. Wrexham eye up move for Millwall's Azeez Wrexham are exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez. The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City. The Robins are hoping the Nigeria international will be attracted by their ambitious project despite Millwall being rival promotion contenders. Wrexham are also looking at Ipswich Town attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti. The 25-year-old Albania international only joined in January from Bristol City for £3.5m and scored his first goal for the club against Wrexham. The move would mean him giving up the opportunity of Premier League football now though Wrexham hope to be there in a year's time. Meanwhile, Wrexham's move for free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe looks to be off. The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City Brighton enquire about Hull target Hernandez Brighton have asked about Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also. Hull owner Acun Ilicali said: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. 'This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' Brighton remain in talks with Liverpool over the sale of winger Yankuba Minteh. Though the 22-year-old wants the move, the clubs are some distance apart on valuation with Brighton wanting over £70m to reflect market prices. The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also Blues keep tabs on Conceicao amid interest in Neto Juventus winger Francisco Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto. Conceicao was bought from Porto for £36million and Juventus would want some profit on their outlay for the 23-year-old Portugal international. Neto has interest from Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea are asking £100m. They also have an offer from Roma for Jamie Gittens but so far that's too low, as a loan with option. Conceicao is quick, technically good and robust for his diminutive stature. Juventus would look to utilise any money from Conceicao for targets such as Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus winger Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto, with Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City all interested in Neto Magpies reignite interest in Spurs' Gray Newcastle United have rekindled interest in Tottenham's versatile midfielder Archie Gray. Sports.title: Jean-Philippe Mateta goes to war with Crystal Palace: Wantaway striker takes his club to FIFA over claims the final months of his contract should be void
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta is arguing that the final months of his Crystal Palace contract are invalid and has taken his challenge to FIFA.

Palace activated the option year in Mateta's contract in 2024 and his current deal is due to expire at the end of this season.

But the 29-year-old is arguing that the contract should be void and that he should have been a free agent this summer.

Mateta's case was heard by an independent tribunal under the Premier League's rules and he subsequently went to FIFA, but they ruled earlier this week that overruling the contract is not within their jurisdiction.

Jean-Philippe Mateta is arguing that the final months of his Crystal Palace contract are invalid

Palace this week rebuffed an enquiry from Aston Villa for Mateta and more clubs are expected to try in the final days of the window.

Mateta, who started Palace's Premier League opener at Everton on Saturday, signed for the club from Mainz 05, initially on an 18-month loan.

He signed a four-and-a-half year contract when joining permanently in January 2022, in a deal that also included the option of a 12-month extension.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi warns big-spending Tottenham need time and must improve 'physical condition' and 'organisation' - as boss apologises after crushing loss to Brentford
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi apologised as Tottenham started the season with a crushing defeat at Brentford.

De Zerbi admitted Spurs did not 'fight in the right way', 'lost too many duels' and 'made a lot of mistakes'.

He also claimed they must improve in their 'physical condition' and 'organisation' but insisted he believed in his players and needed time for them to become a team.

'I am sorry for the defeat,' said De Zerbi. 'We didn't play well. We played very bad. We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We are not in the right physical condition, but these are not excuses, this is a normal situation when you are building a new project.

'It's part of our journey. Yes, I am surprised and I am suffering for this defeat. I expected for sure. I didn't expect this result, but I knew the problems we would find today.'

Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andrew Robertson all made their debuts for Spurs.

Roberto De Zerbi apologised after Tottenham were beaten 3-0 on the opening day by Brentford

De Zerbi admitted his new look side made 'a lot of mistakes' and will need time to become a team

'We are trying to build something good,' said De Zerbi. 'There are steps to become better. Now, the target is to become a team. You become a team when players find a connection, find the spirit, and the soul.

'Before this game, when people asked me about targets, I said first we have to fight to become a team and the two biggest conditions are the soul and the style of play.

'We didn't show the soul or the quality of play, with or without the ball.

'When we find these, we can become dangerous against every team. Until we reach them, we have to suffer and today can be an important defeat. Maybe we will wake up stronger.'

Lucas Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were replaced at half time. Bergvall after losing a vital tackle in the build-up to the second Brentford goal.

'Lucas didn't play badly even though he was substituted,' said De Zerbi. 'In two years' time he will not lose that ball in that moment of the game.'

Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode scored the goals, and Igor Thiago missed a penalty for Brentford.

Mamadou Sangare starred on his Brentford debut with Keith Andrews praising the club for securing his signature

'Pretty impressive on a lot of fronts,' said proud Bees boss Keith Andrews. 'You never truly know what you're going to get because intensity of Premier League is different to most friendlies, but I felt we were in good spot and the cohesion of the team was coming together nicely.'

On Mamadou Sangare's starring debut, Andrews said: 'The club deserve a lot of credit for getting that deal done. There were a lot of clubs looking at Mamadou and we were keen to get that done.

'He has slotted in really well, adapted really well. You never know coming from a different league. He's a humble young man, and very hungry. You can see his attributes. Great energy and quality. I enjoyed his performance.'

Sports.title: Defiant David Sullivan continues to ignore calls to stay away from West Ham matches after allegations of sexual misconduct
Sports.content:
Defiant David Sullivan continues to ignore calls to stay away from West Ham matches after allegations of sexual misconduct

Do YOU have a story? Email William.G.Hallowell@dailymail.co.uk

Get your news delivered straight to you by 7am - sign up to our new Morning Mail newsletter for FREE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

David Sullivan has continued to ignore calls to stay away from West Ham matches despite allegations of sexual misconduct by seven women.

The defiant West Ham owner, 77, was the subject of a BBC Panorama and Times newspaper investigation earlier this year, which accused him of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour against the alleged victims.

However, despite fears of fan unrest following the investigation, Sullivan, who has denied any wrongdoing, continues to attend the Hammers' games.

The 77-year-old was spotted in the crowd watching West Ham's match against Charlton Athletic at the London Stadium on Saturday, which saw the home team lose 2-1.

Sporting a dark grey suit and tie, Sullivan was pictured in the stands with his fiancé, 45-year-old model Ampika Pickston, who was wearing a blue dress.

It comes after London Stadium bosses had 'recommended' to West Ham that Sullivan does not attend home matches over concerns of fan unrest following the investigation into alleged sexual misconduct.

Earlier this month it was also reported that the stadium had asked for advance notice of any planned visits so as to implement further safety and operational measures.

However the billionaire businessman has continued to defy calls not to attend the club's home games.

West Ham owner David Sullivan, 77, continues to ignore calls to stay away from the London Stadium after he turned up to see the Hammers lose 2-1 to Charlton Athletic on Saturday

The billionaire businessman was pictured with his fiancé, 45-year-old model Ampika Pickston

Sullivan, who denies any wrongdoing, is West Ham's largest shareholder

Sullivan stepped down as joint chairman of West Ham shortly before Panorama's investigation went to air, insisting he wanted to focus on fighting 'factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life'.

The 77-year-old is the Championship club's largest shareholder.

The investigation found that Sullivan has been banned from contact with the club's women's and youth teams for the past three years due to safeguarding concerns after a historical allegation into his alleged conduct was raised with the FA in 2023.

Sullivan has denied the allegation and says he has never met any academy or women's player 'one-to-one' during his 16-year tenure at West Ham.

A spokesman for London Stadium previously said that 'following media reports at the end of the season regarding a safeguarding matter being managed by the club, London Stadium sought further information to ensure it could fulfil its own safeguarding responsibilities'.

The spokesman added that West Ham had responded, saying the 'matter was investigated and that the club does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Mr Sullivan attending the stadium'.

West Ham co-owner David Sullivan has been accused of abusing a number of women and preying on them for sex, but denies the allegations

London Stadium upheld its recommendation that Sullivan stay away from games due to the risk of 'potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators'.

Daily Mail Sport previously revealed that Sullivan felt he was being 'bullied' by 'keyboard warriors' into staying away.

He was concerned about the lack of transfer activity, now that he's no longer the man signing the cheques.

This newspaper was outside the directors' entrance in September when thousands gathered outside to protest against Sullivan's ownership.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino defies FIFA vice-president request to stay away from youth tournament amid backlash to World Cup sell off plan
Sports.content:
Under-pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino was asked to stay away from a youth tournament in the Caribbean after being told his presence would 'undermine' the event.

According to reports, Concacaf president Victor Montagliani told Infantino to reconsider attending the Caribbean Football Union's Under-14 Series event.

The letter from Montagliani, who is also a FIFA vice-president, comes with Infantino still coming under fire over his now scrapped plans to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

'The media will focus on this situation, which will unfortunately significantly take away from the technical nature of the CFU youth competition,' Montagliani wrote.

'As such, I respectfully ask you in the name of football to reconsider your attendance as it will unfortunately undermine the technical nature of this important youth development activity.'

Concacaf had previously joined UEFA and the Asian Football Confederation in accusing Infantino of breaking trust ‘through deception’ over the World Cup sell off plan.

Gianni Infantino was reportedly told to stay away from a youth tournament in the Caribbean

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani wrote to Infantino to ask him to 'reconsider' his attendance

Gianni Infantino brushed off questions from reporters about his future with a series of bald jokes when attending the event

Despite the plea, Infantino arrived in the Dominican Republic for the event, which is funded by the FIFA Forward programme. His presence is believed to have angered Concacaf nations.

Infantino was asked at the event by a Sky reporter whether he has betrayed football and why he won't resign

'You have a nice haircut, thank you so much. See you at the hairdressers,’ Infantino told the reporter, who is also bald.

In July, news broke Infantino was considering selling parts of the World Cup to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could have been worth around £15billion.

The Times' report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest could pay him more than $50million-a-year.

Infantino's blueprint for the potential selling of stakes had been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could have included Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared – and they signed non-disclosure agreements.

Bank JPMorgan was said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

Earlier this month, Infantino was given the ‘full support’ of FIFA’s top brass after summoning executives to crisis talks in Morocco.

The Swiss football administrator has since scrapped the proposals after widespread opposition – including an internal rebellion at FIFA.

Earlier this week, Kevin Lamour, the FIFA chief operating officer who broke ranks and criticised Infantino over the World Cup sell-off plan, was sacked.

Sports.title: Brentford 3-0 Tottenham: This was as comprehensive as defeats come. Roberto De Zerbi's men were outplayed and unable to cope with their slick hosts, writes MATT BARLOW
Sports.content:
Amid so much change, some things remain the same. And there is still nothing quite like a trip to Brentford in the Premier League to bring the lofty expectations of the self-appointed elite crashing back to earth.

Tottenham, having escaped the ignominy of relegation, settled upon a head coach to their liking and spent a couple of hundred million in the transfer market, took a hiding at the hands of the Bees and should be flattered by the scoreline.

Roberto De Zerbi saw his team outplayed in every department. Unable to cope with the intensity and physicality in midfield. Unable to handle Brentford's aerial presence up at the back. Unable to get a hold of the ball and offer any threat in attack

This was as comprehensive as defeats come. Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode scored the goals, and Igor Thiago missed a penalty.

Spurs barely stirred. Apart from a late effort by Mikey Moore, superbly saved by Caoimhin Kelleher, they did not look like scoring. Perhaps most worrying of all, they appeared reluctant to engage in the battle they faced.

De Zerbi might add Savinho and Omar Marmoush next week and but there is still work to be done on the fundamentals of competing at this level, what he called 'the soul of the team' on the eve of this season.

Roberto De Zerbi cut a forlorn figure as Tottenham sank to a 3-0 defeat opening-day defeat at Brentford

The Italian cut a forlorn figure on the touchline with hands in pockets as the jubilant home crowd taunted him with songs about Thomas Frank, relegation and wasted money.

Brentford, we should note, were excellent. Slick and cohesive. They know what they are and what they are trying to achieve and in Mamadou Sangare had the most influential of all the big-money summer singings on display.

Sangare, signed for a club record £41million from Lens, eclipsed £100m Sandro Tonali. In the second half, he eclipsed £85m Mateus Fernandes, too. The new central defensive pairing Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi had no answer for the aerial assault led by Thiago.

The Bees, having been written off following a summer upheaval last year, have basked in a summer of serenity this year under Keith Andrews. They scored seven on their final pre-season outing against Eintracht Frankfurt and were again in fluent attacking mood again.

Sangare created the opening goal, carrying the ball forward, bouncing a one-two off Thiago and cutting a low cross square for Lewis-Potter to convert.

Lewis-Potter has matured into an excellent left back. His strength is going forward but he has become capable in defence and deceptively strong in the air. He had already seen one sweet volley blocked from a corner and Nathan Collins had turned a good chance wide with a near post header. Thiago headed another against the bar but there was a flag up for offside.

James Maddison and his Tottenham team-mates applaud the fans after this bruising defeat

Keane Lewis-Potter put Brentford in just the 12th minute as they made a fast start on Saturday

Home fans were buoyant. Thrilled by the attacking vibrancy of their own team and perhaps enjoying further disorder in the ranks of the visitors on behalf of Frank, their popular former boss who was given short shrift when he left for Spurs.

When the teams met here on New Year's Day, the 0-0 draw unfolded to the stinging soundtrack of 'Boring Boring Tottenham' from the away end. It proved the beginning of the end for Frank, sacked 41 days later with relegation fears taking a grip.

De Zerbi's rescue mission lifted spirits, and investment in new players fuelled hope of a better season ahead. The Spurs boss named four debutants to start. Fernandes from the bench made it five. They were led out by Archie Gray, the club's youngest captain the club in a competitive match at 20 years, 163 days but it was not an occasion he will cherish.

Subbed before the end, Gray was serenaded by Bees supporters who have not forgotten he snubbed them for Spurs. 'Should've signed for a big club,' they crowed.

Janelt scored Brentford's second before the interval. Mathias Jensen beat Lucas Bergvall in a tackle and tested goalkeeper Toni Kinsky with a skidding shot from the edge of the penalty area.

Kinsky made a mess of the save and spilled it into a dangerous area, and Janelt was quickest to the rebound, an all-encompassing defensive shambles with familiar echoes for Spurs.

Brentford's new £41m signing Mamadou Sangare played a starring role against Tottenham

Going forward, they offered very little. Mathys Tel had a tame free kick easily gathered by Kelleher and Tonali lashed a hopeful shot over from distance and high into the top tier of the stand and greeted by chants of, 'what a waste of money'.

De Zerbi's made half-time changes to his midfield. Off came Bergvall and Conor Gallagher. On came Fernandes and Rodrigo Bentancur. It gave them a little more control but not before Brentford grabbed a third via a smooth corner routine.

Collins, unmarked in the deep, headed the ball down to Sangare's whose fierce strike from the edge of the penalty box was saved by Kinsky. Michael Kayode pounced to fire the loose ball high into the net.

From the Spurs angle, there were maddening similarities to the previous goal. Bees were first to the header, first to the knock-down and first to the rebound. They should have made it 4-0 from the spot when Bentancur was ruled by referee Michael Oliver to have pushed on Kevin Schade.

Thiago hit a post having sent Kinsky the wrong way. It was perhaps the only real mistake made by Brentford. Alas, for Spurs there were many.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly update emerges as club makes early transfer approach
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly update emerges as club makes early transfer approach

Manchester United news as the need for fresh blood is summed by the dire opening-day defeat at Hull City

The need for new signings was laid bare as Manchester United made the worst possible start to the new season

United have so far bolstered their midfield with the signings of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa, while Carlos Baleba is on the way from Brighton. However, the shocking 2-0 defeat against newly promoted Hull underlined how much more work there is to do before the transfer window slams shut on September 1.

‌



A new left-back is desirable, with United being linked with a move for Arsenal youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly and Newcastle's Lewis Hall.

‌



With the Champions League now on the schedule, it is imperative that United strengthen in several positions. Ahead of a crucial fortnight for the club, here's a round-up of the latest United transfer news.

United priced out

United's reason for not pressing ahead with a move for Lewis-Skelly has emerged. The versatile Gunners man, who can also operate in midfield, was subject of interest from both United and Chelsea.

‌

Amad absence from Man Utd squad vs Hull explained after training ground blow READ MORE :

Arsenal were open about the fact he could move, but their valuation ultimately saw United walk away from talks. That's according to The Athletic's David Ornstein, who said the price quoted was "too high" for United, who then switched their attention to long-time target Baleba.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has since said he is "100 per cent" certain Lewis-Skelly will stay put. Hall is another left-back on United's wish-list, but again, they have been put off by the asking price.

Hall is now said to be in talks over a new Newcastle contract and a place in the players' leadership team under new boss Matthias Jaissle.

‌

A host of new signings have arrived, including former United pair Alejandro Garnacho and Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Romano said Villa had recently "made a call" about Zirkzee, while adding that their interest is in its early stages.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher fires early Man Utd dig as 'carried away' remark comes full cricle
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher fires early Man Utd dig as 'carried away' remark comes full cricle

Jamie Carragher claimed on Friday night that the predictions for Manchester United this season were potentially over the top with the Red Devils then going down to Hull

View Image Jamie Carragher has revelled in Man Utd's opening loss (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher was quick to reference his Manchester United comments after their loss to Hull on Saturday with a witty post on his social media.

‌



Michael Carrick enjoyed an impressive interim spell last season, which saw United rise up to third and secure a Champions League spot. Among his landmark results was a win over Liverpool at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils' renaissance last term, coupled with some of their midfield signings in the form of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, has seen plenty tip United to secure another top four finish. Some have gone as far as to back them to finish second behind Arsenal.

‌



Carragher felt some of the fanfare was over the top and claimed: "People are getting very carried away with Man United. People are putting them second and third, honestly. Man United's back four is the same back four they had five years ago."

The former Liverpool man had his usual back and forth with Sky Sports colleague Gary Neville but, in the aftermath of United's loss at the MKM Stadium to newly promoted Hull, Carragher used a GIF to highlight his comments from Friday night.

‌



Neville had claimed that United were in a better place than Liverpool, but Carragher suggested that Liverpool's starting XI would still be better than their rivals. Both Neville and Carragher will have to give their Premier League predictions on Monday Night Football, which they do annually, but the latter will likely poke fun at Neville over the result.

United were heavy favourites going into Saturday's lunchtime kick-off by were 2-0 down by half-time. They struggled to offer anything in the second-half and returned to Manchester with no points and no goals after a thoroughly underwhelming performance.

Carrick said on their performance: "It was never going to be perfect today but I think going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult, probably a typical one of those games of a newly promoted team at home.

"You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to, and then after that, we had moments, we had opportunities, we just didn't have that spark to then put the chances away or create any more. Listen, we're bitterly disappointed with the result today but it won't knock us.”
