Sports.title: McLaren’s car is “terrible” in low-speed corners – Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
McLaren’s performance in Zandvoort highlights their car’s weakness in slow corners, says Lando Norris.

The reigning world champion won the previous round at the Hungaroring, a circuit which has several low-to-medium-speed corners, but he believes the slower mix of corners at Zandvoort is a problem for the MCL40.

“We knew in Budapest we’re very good in high-speed corners and we’re pretty terrible in slow speed, but we still managed to win,” he said. “Here there’s a lot more of the very, very slow speed and more of our problems show. So [it’s] not a surprise at all. It’s exactly what we expected.”

McLaren have brought further upgrades for their car in Zandvoort. Norris said these have performed as expected but the team still has a significant deficit to its rivals at some circuits.

“They’ve done exactly as they should, so I’m very happy,” he said. “We still managed to progress.

“It’s just [in] certain areas we’re just nowhere near quick enough. The slow speed, we’ve just struggled the whole weekend and seems clearly the weakness we have in the car at the minute. I feel if we still went back to Monaco now, we’re going to be shocking, as we were.

“So I think we’ve clearly progressed a lot, and especially in medium and high-speed, which is why we’re quick here, why we were so quick in Budapest. It wasn’t like we were quick everywhere in Budapest, and that’s why we won. The slow speed, we were still slower than Ferrari and matching Mercedes just about.

“So we still have weaknesses, even though we managed to win one race. It’s just the strengths really shone there, and here it’s just the deficit is too big in the slow speed.”

Norris qualified second on the grid for today’s sprint race alongside George Russell but fell to third behind Charles Leclerc. He doubts McLaren can make any significant changes to the car’s poor performance in low-speed corners for the time being.

“There’s just nothing we can do about it now. It’s just how the car is for the time being.

“That’s where we still have to focus as a team. We’ll try and get everything out of it. I feel like I still did a good job today, even with the P3.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Defeats Rolly Romero, Captures WBA Title
Sports.content:
That was Romero’s best stretch of the fight. Lopez recovered in the sixth and resumed moving forward behind his jab while attacking the body. Although the cut began bleeding again late in the contest, he continued outworking a champion who spent too much time waiting for isolated counterpunching opportunities.

Needing a strong finish, Romero remained cautious during the 12th. Lopez stayed on the front foot and completed the fight as the busier boxer. The victory raised his record to 23-2 with 13 knockouts, while Romero dropped to 17-3 with 13 stoppages.

Gary Antonio Russell Takes Santillan’s Interim Belt

A dominant unanimous decision over Victor Santillan gave Gary Antonio Russell the interim WBA super bantamweight title. Scores were 119-108 twice and 118-109.

Superior speed, a sharp jab and faster combinations allowed Russell to control the fight. The matchup between two southpaws produced frequent clinches, but Russell consistently landed the cleaner punches whenever space opened between them.

A right hook to the top of the head dropped Santillan during the 12th round. He beat referee Robert Hoyle’s count and held repeatedly to survive until the final bell. Russell moved to 22-1 with 13 knockouts, while Santillan fell to 16-3 with seven stoppages.

Hernandez Receives Majority Decision Over Veron

A majority decision over Francisco Daniel Veron gave Yoenli “El Diablo” Hernandez the victory in their 10-round middleweight bout. Two judges scored it widely for Hernandez at 99-91 and 98-92, while the third returned a surprising 95-95 card.

Heavier and more accurate punches gave Hernandez control during the opening rounds, while Veron tried to compensate with pressure and a high work rate. Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes.

The Cuban regained control by attacking the body and landing right hands and uppercuts. Veron continued advancing and throwing through the final bell, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Utria Edges Mercado By Split Decision

A disputed split decision over Israel “Bad Ways” Mercado kept Carlos Utria’s perfect record intact after their 10-round light welterweight fight. Scores were 96-94 for Utria, 96-94 for Mercado and 97-93 for Utria.

Much of the early action belonged to Utria before Mercado closed the fourth with a combination. The fight remained close through the middle rounds, with neither boxer establishing a lasting advantage.

Strong work during the ninth carried Mercado into a decisive final round. He believed he had done enough to win, and sections of the crowd expressed their displeasure when Utria was announced as the victor.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell In First

A sustained attack from Marco Romero forced a first-round stoppage against Kahlil “Killa” Mitchell in their scheduled eight-round bout.

Unable to defend himself, Mitchell was trapped as Romero unloaded a combination during the final minute. Referee Allen Huggins stopped the contest at 2:33.

Johnson Decisions Rodriguez

A six-round decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez gave Benjamin Johnson another welterweight victory. Johnson moved to 8-0 with seven knockouts, while Rodriguez dropped to 4-4-1.

Tony Weeks served as the referee.

Brown Sweeps Wiggins Over Six Rounds

Every round went to Joseph “The Prodigy” Brown in a slow six-round middleweight contest against Alton Wiggins. All three judges scored the fight 60-54.

Cleaner punches separated Brown from Wiggins, whose frequent holding prevented the exchanges from developing. The same pattern continued through the sixth.

Blancas Drops Mamone, Wins Decision

A knockdown helped Aldo Blancas secure a unanimous decision over Ricky Mamone in their four-round light welterweight bout. Scores were 39-36 twice and 40-35.

A left hook to the body from Blancas produced a delayed knockdown late in the second. Mamone beat referee John McCarthy’s count and continued despite bleeding from the nose during the third.

Unable to secure the stoppage, Blancas settled for the decision after Mamone survived the final round.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Wins Third Belt As Rolando Romero Barely Fights
Sports.content:
Romero’s strategy depended almost entirely on catching Lopez as he moved inside. That opportunity arrived in the fifth round when a left hand opened a cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow and hurt him. Romero followed with a flurry and had the challenger under pressure as “Rolly” chants spread through the arena.

It should have changed the fight. Instead, Romero returned to waiting.

Lopez recovered in the sixth, reestablished his jab and resumed attacking the body. Blood continued leaking from the cut during the later rounds, but it never prevented him from moving forward or maintaining his output. Romero landed isolated counters without putting enough punches behind them to take control.

The champion’s corner urged him to hold the center of the ring before the final round. He continued moving away and never produced the desperate attack required from a fighter in danger of losing his belt. By then, the crowd had grown restless after repeatedly waiting for Romero to open up.

Lopez deserves credit for remaining disciplined after being hurt. He avoided turning the fight into the reckless exchange Romero needed, kept scoring with straightforward work and closed the championship rounds on the front foot. The performance was controlled rather than destructive, with Lopez winning through activity, positioning and better decision-making.

His welterweight debut also raised a question about his punching power at 147 pounds. Lopez landed plenty of clean shots but never seriously hurt Romero. That may become important against the stronger and more active fighters in the division.

Still, Lopez accomplished what he came to Las Vegas to do. He won a title in a third weight class, while Romero surrendered his belt through passivity after finding the punch that briefly gave him a chance to take over the fight.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Beats Franciso Veron, But Draw Card Stuns
Sports.content:
Early confidence led the Cuban to lower his hands, pose and attack with wide power shots. He controlled the distance when he used his jab and footwork, then punished Veron with right hands, uppercuts and combinations to the body whenever the Argentine moved inside.

Veron’s persistence created one dangerous moment. A check hook late in the fifth round caught Hernandez cleanly, briefly wobbling him and forcing him toward the ropes. It was the clearest round for Veron and a reminder that Hernandez was taking unnecessary chances against an opponent who refused to retreat.

The favorite responded by tightening his defense and resuming his body attack. Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the eighth, followed with uppercuts and continued landing the stronger punches through the championship rounds. Veron absorbed the punishment and kept throwing, but his aggression rarely produced clean scoring shots.

That inability to secure the stoppage will give Hernandez something to study. He had the size, power and technical advantage, yet spent too much time looking for single explosive punches instead of breaking Veron down with sustained combinations. His performance was convincing without being the destructive statement his team likely wanted.

None of that explains the draw score. Hernandez clearly won more than five rounds, and the 95-95 card turned an otherwise straightforward result into an unnecessary controversy. The two wide scores properly reflected a fight controlled by Hernandez, even if Veron’s toughness forced him to work until the final bell.

Sports.title: Rolando Romero vs Teofimo Lopez Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Live results

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 12

An unusual embrace opened the final round as the challenger whispered something to Romero before being pushed away. Lopez then resumed pressing forward and kept the champion from producing the desperate attack he needed.

Romero’s corner instructed him to hold the center of the ring, but he continued moving away and never forced a sustained exchange. Lopez closed the fight with greater activity and control, completing what should be a wide decision victory.

10-9 Lopez, 118-110 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 11

The challenger continued pressing behind his jab despite blood dripping from the cut over his right eye. Romero opened with a right to the body, added a shovel hook and later connected with another clean right hand.

Those isolated punches were not accompanied by enough urgency. Romero spent much of the round circling away before both fighters traded near the bell. Lopez’s higher output and forward pressure earned him another round, leaving the champion needing a knockout in the 12th.

10-9 Lopez, 108-101 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 10

Another slow round favored the challenger, who continued attacking the body and landed a clean right hand upstairs. He remained busier and controlled the range despite the cut over his right eye beginning to bleed again.

Romero increased his jab slightly but continued retreating and failed to apply the pressure needed to change the fight. The champion’s cautious approach cost him another round despite having much of the crowd behind him.

10-9 Lopez, 98-92 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 9

An early attempt by the champion to move forward produced little offense. Lopez quickly resumed control behind his jab, worked the body and maintained the distance while operating comfortably from the front foot.

Long stretches passed without a meaningful exchange as Romero kept his hands low and waited for counters that never developed. The earlier “Rolly” chants faded, and the crowd became restless with the champion’s passive approach.

10-9 Lopez, 88-83 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 8

Greater activity allowed the challenger to control another round. He moved forward behind combinations, landed clean hooks upstairs and blocked many of Romero’s counters before answering with punches of his own.

Romero continued picking isolated moments to exchange but remained too cautious to match Lopez’s output. The cut over Lopez’s right eye stayed under control as he extended his lead with cleaner and more consistent work.

10-9 Lopez, 78-74 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 7

Steady pressure from the challenger forced Romero to spend much of the round moving laterally and looking for counters. Both landed right hands early before Lopez attacked the body with a flurry. One punch strayed low and brought a warning from the referee.

Romero connected with a left hook at the bell that appeared to wobble Lopez. The late punch gave the champion another dangerous moment, but Lopez’s activity and control over most of the round narrowly earned it.

10-9 Lopez, 68-65 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 6

The challenger regained his composure after being hurt in the fifth and returned to applying pressure behind the jab. Working patiently from long range allowed him to control the distance and slow the pace.

Romero looked for counters but could not build on his success from the previous round. Lopez’s disciplined boxing and greater activity steadied the fight and secured the sixth.

10-9 Lopez, 58-56 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 5

The champion produced his strongest round yet, hurting Lopez with a left hand that opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Romero followed with a flurry and hurt him again with about a minute remaining.

Lopez answered late as the fighters exchanged punches and words, but Romero’s power and increased activity created the first major change in the fight. Chants of “Rolly” spread through T-Mobile Arena as the challenger finished the round under pressure.

10-9 Romero, 48-47 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 4

A stronger stand from the champion produced his best round of the fight. Several left hands connected cleanly, including one that briefly disrupted Lopez’s balance. The challenger continued pressing forward, but the sharper counters interrupted his rhythm and prevented him from controlling the exchanges.

Lopez’s activity kept the round competitive, although the more meaningful punches came from Romero.

10-9 Romero, 39-37 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 3

Teo continued moving forward, although Romero showed more willingness to hold his position and engage. Neither fighter landed a damaging punch as much of the action consisted of tentative jabs, feints and missed attempts from long range.

Romero remained focused on finding a counter, but Lopez’s greater activity and control of the distance narrowly gave him another quiet round.

10-9 Lopez, 30-27 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 2

Lopez continued setting the pace behind an active jab while forcing Romero to give ground. A clean right hand and several body shots helped Lopez establish his rhythm. Romero remained patient and looked for counters, including a check left hook, but spent too much of the round waiting for openings.

Both fighters missed during a wild exchange near the bell. Lopez’s higher output, effective jab and cleaner punches secured another round.

10-9 Lopez, 20-18 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 1

Both fighters opened cautiously at long range, using their jabs to measure distance without committing to extended combinations. Lopez applied more forward pressure and landed the cleaner jabs, while Romero remained patient and looked for counterpunching opportunities.

A counter right from Lopez connected late as Romero moved forward. Romero answered with a right hand before the bell, but Lopez’s greater activity and sharper work gave him the close opening round.

10-9 Lopez

Yoenli Hernandez defeats Francisco Veron

A surprisingly wide disagreement among the judges ended with Yoenli Hernandez defeating Francisco Daniel Veron by majority decision in their 10-round middleweight co-feature. Hernandez won by scores of 99-91 and 98-92, while the third judge produced a questionable 95-95 card.

Cleaner and heavier punches allowed Hernandez to control most of the fight. The Cuban attacked the body, landed sharp right hands and repeatedly caught Veron with uppercuts at close range. Veron pressed forward and maintained a high output, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes. Hernandez recovered and regained control, hurting Veron with a right hand early in the eighth before dominating the final two rounds.

The challenger’s chin carried him to the final bell despite absorbing numerous power punches. Hernandez never found the stoppage he wanted, but his accurate work made the 95-95 score difficult to explain.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 9

Hernandez continued landing the cleaner punches, although some of his shots lacked full force. Veron walked directly into a right hand but absorbed it well and kept pressing forward. His toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not produce enough accurate offense to take the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 89-82 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 8

Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the round and moved in for the finish, but Veron avoided the follow-up attack. Hernandez returned to the body before landing a combination upstairs and two uppercuts that lifted Veron’s chin. Veron answered once again, although Hernandez’s cleaner and harder punches secured the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 79-73 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 7

Hernandez landed a right hand at close range before partially connecting with an uppercut and following with another right. The Cuban then increased his body attack and struck Veron with clubbing punches on the inside. Veron absorbed everything without going down, but Hernandez controlled another round with the heavier work.

10-9 Hernandez, 69-64 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 6

Hernandez connected with several chopping punches, but Veron continued answering with a high volume of shots. Most of Veron’s punches missed or struck the guard, while Hernandez landed the cleaner work during the exchanges. CompuBox credited Veron with only 24 connects from 171 punches across rounds five and six. Hernandez landed 42 of 128 during the same stretch.

10-9 Hernandez, 59-55 Hernandez

After Five Rounds: Hernandez Remains in Control

Hernandez has controlled most of the fight, but Veron’s check hook at the end of the fifth showed that he remains dangerous. Hernandez needs to continue attacking the body without becoming careless while pressing for a stoppage. A convincing victory would place him near a world-title opportunity, but getting reckless against Veron could undo an otherwise strong performance.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 5

Hernandez landed a heavy right hand during the opening minute, but Veron absorbed it and immediately answered. Hernandez avoided the return before attacking the body and connecting with a right uppercut, a two-punch combination and a left hook. Just when Hernandez seemed to be taking full control, Veron caught him with a check hook that badly wobbled him and stole the round.

10-9 Veron, 49-46 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 4

An overhand right from Hernandez shook Veron at close range before a body shot and two more power punches disrupted his balance. Hernandez continued working downstairs and found the target with a left hook. Veron landed a late flurry, but Hernandez took the punches without showing any effect.

10-9 Hernandez, 40-36 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 3

Hernandez briefly lost his balance after taking a right hand, then answered with a long right and a hard one-two that forced Veron backward. Hernandez continued applying pressure, although many of his heavier punches struck Veron’s guard rather than landing cleanly. Veron’s responsible defense kept him competitive.

10-9 Hernandez, 30-27 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 2

Hernandez pushed Veron backward with power punches, but much of his work landed on the guard. An uppercut-left hook combination came close before Hernandez connected with a sharp right hook at close range. He continued closing the distance and controlling the exchanges.

10-9 Hernandez, 20-18 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 1

Hernandez attacked immediately, landing an overhand right that knocked Veron slightly off balance. A straight left split the guard before Hernandez went to the body and followed with punches upstairs. Veron answered with a double left at close range, but Hernandez’s right uppercut and cleaner power shots gave him the round.

10-9 Hernandez

Russell Dominates Santillan

Gary Antonio Russell captured the interim WBA super bantamweight title with a one-sided unanimous decision over Victor Santillan. The judges scored the 12-round bout 119-108, 119-108 and 118-109.

Russell (22-1, 13 KOs) controlled the distance with his faster hands, accurate jab and sharp combinations. Santillan (16-3, 7 KOs) struggled to deal with Russell’s movement and spent much of the fight being beaten to the punch. Russell completed the dominant performance by dropping Santillan during the final round and nearly forcing a stoppage before the bell.

Carlos Utria Edges Israel Mercado by Split Decision

A difficult U.S. debut ended with Carlos Utria narrowly defeating Israel Mercado by split decision after 10 competitive light welterweight rounds. Mercado disrupted the Colombian prospect’s rhythm, pressed forward and made the heavy favorite work harder than anticipated. Utria found success with body punches and short combinations, but he never gained complete control of the fight. Scores were 96-94 and 97-93 for Utria, while the third judge gave Mercado a 96-94 card.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell in First Round

A fast start allowed Marco Romero to overwhelm Kahlil Mitchell and force a stoppage at 2:33 of the opening round. The 20-year-old middleweight landed hard combinations almost immediately, giving Mitchell little time to settle into the fight. Referee intervention ended the scheduled eight-round bout before the first bell.

Benjamin Johnson Decisions Jose Gabriel Rodriguez

The opening fight of the evening ended with Benjamin Johnson earning a unanimous decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez after six welterweight rounds. Johnson used his 6-foot-2 frame and 76-inch reach to control the distance against the shorter Ecuadorian. Rodriguez remained durable and became the first opponent to take the 21-year-old prospect to the final bell. Johnson had stopped each of his first seven opponents before Saturday night.

Joseph Brown Sweeps Alton Wiggins

A six-round shutout gave Joseph Brown a unanimous decision over Alton Wiggins in their junior middleweight bout. The 19-year-old controlled the distance with his height and reach, winning each round without scoring a knockdown. All three judges returned scores of 60-54.

Aldo Blancas Decisions Ricky Mamone

Aldo Blancas used his height, reach and strong left hand to defeat Ricky Mamone by unanimous decision in a four-round light welterweight bout. Blancas dropped Mamone with a left to the body in the second round and controlled most of the action from distance. Mamone recovered and made it to the final bell, but he could not overcome the early knockdown or Blancas’ higher output. The judges scored it 39-36, 39-36 and 40-35.

Sports.title: Marco Romero Destroys Kahlil Mitchell in First Round
Sports.content:
Mitchell never had an opportunity to settle into the scheduled eight-round fight. Romero closed the distance quickly, landed clean punches and continued firing combinations once he had his opponent near the ropes. The pressure became too much for Mitchell before the first round ended.

“I’m not getting paid for overtime,” Romero said after the fight.

That line matched the performance. Romero did not rush forward, throwing wild punches in search of an early finish. His shots were short and accurate, and he remained balanced while attacking. Those qualities separate him from young punchers who rely almost entirely on physical strength.

Although Mitchell was not a major test, Romero handled him exactly as a highly regarded prospect should. There was no prolonged feeling-out period and no opportunity for the underdog to gain confidence.

Romero (15-0, 13 KOs) recently signed with Premier Boxing Champions, giving the company another young middleweight with the potential to move quickly. His power will attract attention, but his composure is just as important. He fights like someone who already understands how to create openings rather than waiting for an opponent to make an obvious mistake.

Stronger opposition will be needed before Romero can be judged against the leading fighters at 160 pounds. Saturday’s performance still provided an impressive introduction for viewers watching him for the first time.

Mitchell came to Las Vegas with six professional wins and four knockouts. Romero made that experience look insignificant, finishing him before the fight had a chance to develop.

Sports.title: George Liddard Stops Dario Morello After Eight Rounds
Sports.content:
The 24-year-old Liddard moved to 15-0 with nine knockouts after adding the European championship to the British, Commonwealth, and IBF Intercontinental belts he previously held.

Morello struggled to land consistently against the quicker champion. Many of his wider punches missed, allowing Liddard to score with straighter combinations before moving out of range. The Italian never found a way to slow him down and lost each completed round.

Officials recorded a retirement after eight rounds. Morello fell to 26-2 with four knockouts.

Jimmy Sains Defeats Tom Cowling

Jimmy Sains claimed the vacant Commonwealth middleweight title with a 12-round unanimous decision over Tom Cowling.

Much of the opening half belonged to Sains, although Cowling landed a solid right hand late in the first round and enjoyed his best stretch during rounds six and seven. A sustained attack in the sixth briefly forced Sains onto the defensive.

The southpaw regained command from the eighth and swept most of the remaining rounds with his higher output. Cowling rocked him with another right hand during the final minute, but the late success was not enough to change the outcome.

The judges scored the contest 119-109, 119-109, and 118-110 for Sains, who raised his record to 13-0 with 10 knockouts. Cowling dropped to 15-2.

Buttigieg And Gordon Fight To Split Draw

Emmanuel Buttigieg and P A Gordon fought to a 10-round split draw, leaving the vacant English middleweight title unclaimed.

Gordon had the stronger start and held the advantage through much of the opening four rounds. Buttigieg increased his output in the fifth and sixth before Gordon answered during a series of closely contested later rounds.

Both men fought aggressively in the tenth with the decision still unsettled. Gordon bloodied Buttigieg’s nose during an entertaining finish, but the judges were unable to agree on a winner.

One card favored Gordon 97-93, another had Buttigieg ahead 96-94, and the third was level at 95-95. Buttigieg is now 12-0-1, while Gordon moved to 9-0-1.

Tiah Mai Ayton Stops Ellie Hellewell

Tiah Mai Ayton won the vacant Commonwealth featherweight title when Ellie Hellewell retired after the sixth round.

A combination near the end of the opening round began creating separation for Ayton. She continued landing the cleaner punches over the following rounds and hurt Hellewell again late in the fifth.

Hellewell completed the sixth, but her corner ended the contest before round seven. Officials recorded a sixth-round retirement, advancing Ayton to 7-0 with six knockouts.

Copper Box Undercard Results

Connor Mitchell defeated Caine Singh on points over four rounds in a featherweight bout. A left hand from Mitchell dropped Singh in the opening round, and referee Lewis Van Poetsch scored the contest 39-37. The victory moved Mitchell to 4-0 with two knockouts.

Louie Ward knocked out Jon Martinez at 2:36 of the third round. A right-left combination sent Martinez down for the full count.

Ioan Croft stopped Tomas Andres Reynoso at 1:50 of the sixth round. A left hand dropped Reynoso in the second before another sustained attack forced the stoppage four rounds later.

Harley Burrows needed only 65 seconds to stop Carlos Miguel Ronner. A series of unanswered punches led referee Kieran McCann to end the middleweight contest.

The official results are confirmed by the British Boxing Board of Control.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Nobody Can Stop Fury-Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
“The update is quite simple. We’ve signed the contract. We’re waiting for a date. You saw Tyson Fury on the elliptical trainer, shouting and screaming. There’s nothing to shout about. The fight’s done, the fight’s signed,” Hearn told DAZN Boxing. “No one can pull out of the fight. You can’t just pull out of a contract. So, we’re waiting on the date.”

The dispute remains tied to the location. Joshua’s agreement calls for the fight to take place in the UK, while Sela, Netflix and the other parties involved favor New York. Hearn has submitted separate terms that would allow Joshua to accept Madison Square Garden, but he made clear that his preference remains a British stadium.

If Sela rejects those changes, Hearn expects the company to follow the existing contract and deliver the event in the UK.

“If they deliver on the contract, which they have to legally, the fight’s happening in the UK, and we’ll be very, very happy,” Hearn said. “The only way it can stop from happening is if they actually breach the contract.”

That line leaves Sela with two direct options: honor the UK agreement or meet Joshua’s terms for America. Sela can still abandon the event in practice, but doing so may expose the company to a costly legal claim. The possible damages cannot be calculated without seeing the cancellation and breach provisions.

Hearn’s claim is legally forceful but practically overstated. Sela cannot withdraw without risking financial penalties, but it can still refuse to finance the event. A contract creates legal consequences for breaking an agreement; it does not guarantee that a boxing match reaches the ring.

The greater issue may come after the lawyers finish. Joshua has received some of his largest purses through Turki Alalshikh and Sela. Hearn can use the UK clause to secure better terms for New York, but pushing too far risks damaging the relationship that makes paydays of this size possible. Few other backers can offer Joshua comparable money at this stage of his career.

Sports.title: Jake Paul Admits Amanda Serrano Needed Championship Rounds
Sports.content:
“I had Manzur leading for the first half of the fight as that overhand right was finding its target,” Jake posted on X. “But you figured it out and started controlling the fight on your terms…body shots, mid-range, reading what the young challenger was giving you. If that fight was 10 rounds, a different outcome, but the championship rounds made the difference.”

That was a revealing admission from Serrano’s promoter. Manzur’s aggression, right hand, and willingness to remain in punching range gave Serrano trouble through much of the contest. The champion eventually created separation with her body attack and higher output during the later rounds.

Unlike the standard 10-round limit for women’s title fights, Serrano and Manzur competed over 12 two-minute rounds. The format gave Serrano six more minutes to recover from her slow start and strengthen her position on the scorecards.

Serrano has spent years pushing for women to receive the same 12 three-minute rounds used in men’s championship fights. Friday’s contest retained two-minute rounds, but the longer fight still worked in her favor and helped her overcome Manzur’s early success.

Paul also left Serrano’s future open after praising the influence she has had on women’s boxing during her 17-year career.

“You have used it every step of the way to lift others and push women’s boxing,” he said. “The most impactful in many ways. Whatever you decide to do next, I am in your corner.”

That closing message sounded less like the immediate promotion of another fight and more like Paul giving Serrano control over the next decision. At 37, she has won titles across seven weight divisions, completed three fights with Katie Taylor, and now reached 50 professional victories.

Serrano can continue defending her featherweight belts, but Manzur showed that those assignments are no longer routine. Paul’s comments also showed how close MVP believed its biggest star came to losing her milestone fight.

Ghana News.title: 9 Blue Water Guards arrested over alleged bribery, impersonation
Ghana News.content:
Nine members of the Blue Water Guards (BWG) have reportedly been arrested at Manso Adubia in the Ashanti Region over allegations of bribery and impersonation.

The personnel were reportedly picked up on Friday, August 21, 2026, by the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) following claims that they collected money from individuals while allegedly posing as officials of the anti-illegal mining body.

The development has triggered an internal warning to members of the Blue Water Guards, with authorities cautioning personnel against conduct that could undermine public confidence in ongoing efforts to combat illegal mining.

An internal notice circulated among members of the group described the alleged conduct as a serious breach of professional standards and warned that such actions could tarnish the reputation of the anti-illegal mining programme.

The notice made it clear that Blue Water Guards personnel were not authorised to assume the identity or functions of NAIMOS officials.

“All guards are hereby cautioned to desist from such acts and remain professional. No BWG is authorised to act as NAIMOS,” the notice stated.

The arrests come amid collaboration between NAIMOS and the Blue Water Guards in the fight against illegal mining, particularly activities along water bodies and river corridors.

The two groups have previously operated from the Manso Adubia operational base, conducting joint enforcement exercises aimed at curbing illegal mining activities in parts of the Ashanti Region.

The alleged impersonation has, however, raised concerns about the need for personnel participating in such operations to clearly distinguish their respective mandates and maintain professional standards.

Ghana News.title: Wildlife guard shot dead during Kakum patrol
Ghana News.content:
A routine patrol in the Kakum Forest Reserve ended in tragedy on Saturday, August 22, 2026, after a wildlife resource guard was allegedly shot dead by a suspected poacher in the Assin Kruwa area of the Central Region.

The deceased, identified as 58-year-old Richard Otwey, was attached to the Kakum Wildlife Division of the Forestry Commission and was on patrol with two other guards when the incident occurred.

According to the Central North Police Command, the patrol team encountered two men allegedly engaged in illegal hunting inside the protected forest.

The guards reportedly attempted to apprehend the men, identified as Bukari Abudu and John Mensah, but Abudu allegedly pulled out a single-barrel gun and fired at the officers.

Otwey was hit in the chest and died at the scene.

After the shooting, the patrol team pursued the suspects through the forest, managing to apprehend Mensah.

He was subsequently handed over to the police and is assisting with investigations.

Abudu, however, managed to escape into the forest and was still at large as of the latest update.

The police and forestry authorities have since intensified efforts to locate him.

Investigators who visited the scene, located about 60 metres from the reserve boundary and beneath a wawa tree, reportedly recovered a spent cartridge, footprints and the single-barrel firearm allegedly used in the attack.

The Central North Regional Crime Officer, Chief Superintendent Edmund Agyemang Badu, confirmed the incident but declined to disclose further details because of the ongoing investigation.

"The Police can confirm the killing, but we cannot comment further as investigations are ongoing," Chief Superintendent Agyemang Badu stated.

Otwey's remains have been conveyed to the Abura Dunkwa Government Hospital Mortuary, where they have been deposited for preservation and post-mortem examination.

The incident has raised fresh concerns about the risks faced by personnel who patrol Ghana's forest reserves, particularly in areas where illegal hunting and other activities continue to pose threats to protected wildlife and those tasked with safeguarding the forests.

The police have appealed to residents and others with information that could lead to the arrest of Abudu to assist the investigation.

Authorities are particularly interested in information on his whereabouts as the manhunt continues.

Ghana News.title: ‘I reject them without qualification’ — Afenyo-Markin hits back over Sammy Gyamfi’s claims
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader in Parliament and Member of Parliament for Effutu, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, has rejected allegations questioning his motives for demanding accountability for losses associated with the Bank of Ghana’s (BoG) Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), calling them "false and defamatory”.

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the controversy surrounding the programme should not be allowed to shift attention from the substantive financial questions raised by the Minority, particularly concerning the reported US$1.7 billion loss under the programme in 2025 and the role of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) in the transactions.

In a social media post on Saturday, August 22, the Minority Leader said he had faced sustained personal attacks over the past week after his decision to question the programme's financial implications.

“Over the past week, all manner of insults and personal attacks have been directed at me, apparently in an attempt to impugn my character and divert attention from the substantive questions I have raised,” he stated.

He said attempts had also been made to attribute improper motives to his scrutiny of the programme.

“False and defamatory allegations have also been made about my motives for questioning the losses incurred under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme and the role of GoldBod in those transactions,” he revealed.

Mr Afenyo-Markin was emphatic in his rejection of the allegations.

“These allegations are entirely false, and I reject them without qualification,” he emphasised. ‘My duty is oversight’

The Minority Leader said his intervention was rooted in Parliament’s constitutional responsibility to scrutinise public institutions and demand explanations where questions arose over the use and management of public resources.

“As Minority Leader in Parliament, my responsibility is to help Parliament discharge its constitutional oversight function.”

He maintained that his questions were not driven by personal interests or any improper agenda.

“My actions have been guided solely by that responsibility. I have neither acted from any improper motive nor conducted myself inappropriately in the performance of my duties.”

The comments come against the backdrop of a public exchange between Mr Afenyo-Markin and the Chief Executive Officer of GoldBod, Sammy Gyamfi, following the Minority’s concerns about the reported loss under the DGPP.

The dispute centres on the interpretation of the reported US$1.7 billion loss and the extent of GoldBod’s involvement in the transactions.

The IMF has raised concerns about losses associated with the BoG’s domestic gold purchasing operations, putting the programme under renewed scrutiny and prompting questions about its financial implications.

GoldBod, which plays a central role in Ghana’s gold purchasing and aggregation arrangements, has meanwhile been the subject of questions over its role in the transactions and the extent to which the reported losses should be attributed to it.

Substantive issues

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the personal attacks against him appeared intended to divert public attention from the issues requiring scrutiny.

He acknowledged that public officials and institutions subjected to oversight could resist questioning but said that should not undermine Parliament’s role.

“I recognise that, in public life, those who are uncomfortable with legitimate scrutiny may push back.”

He added: “In some cases, they may resort to false allegations, personal attacks and ridicule in an effort to shift attention from the substantive issues and make the person asking the questions the subject of controversy.”

The Minority has maintained that the reported loss warrants closer examination to establish how it occurred, the institutions involved, the financial implications for the state and whether adequate safeguards were in place.

The development has also revived broader questions about the financial risks associated with the government's gold purchasing strategy and the mechanisms used to manage the transactions.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod must appear before a parliamentary inquiry to answer for gold-trade losses — Appiagyei
Ghana News.content:
The Minority in Parliament has stepped up its demand for accountability over the financial consequences of the Bank of Ghana’s (BoG) Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), insisting that the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) cannot distance itself from questions surrounding billions of dollars in gold transactions undertaken on behalf of the central bank.

Deputy Minority Leader Patricia Appiagyei said in a statement on Saturday, August 22, that the Minority’s concerns were not an attempt to undermine GoldBod but a legitimate parliamentary demand for transparency over the management of public resources.

Her comments come amid an increasingly heated exchange between the Minority Caucus and the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of GoldBod, Sammy Gyamfi, over the interpretation of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) findings on the programme.

The dispute centres on the financial cost of the DGPP, under which the BoG dramatically expanded its domestic gold purchases in 2025 as part of efforts to rebuild Ghana’s international reserves and support the foreign exchange market.

The IMF reported that the BoG purchased US$7.6 billion worth of gold through the programme up to August 2025, including about US$5 billion of doré gold from artisanal and small-scale miners. GoldBod was involved in the purchasing and related activities under the arrangement.

The Minority has interpreted the latest IMF findings as pointing to approximately US$1.7 billion in under-recoveries associated with the programme, equivalent to about GH¢22 billion at the exchange rate used in the current public debate.

Mrs Appiagyei said the sheer scale of the figures demanded more than political exchanges and denials.

She said the central issue was whether the public received value for the resources committed to the programme and whether the institutions involved had exercised adequate financial discipline, risk management and oversight.

According to her, the Minority would not be distracted by what she described as personal attacks and exchanges between the Caucus and the GoldBod CEO.

“The issue before us is accountability. It is about public money, public gold and the management of a programme that involved billions of dollars. Ghanaians deserve clear answers,” she said.

GoldBod's defence

Mr Gyamfi has rejected the Minority’s characterisation of the figures, describing claims that GoldBod incurred a US$1.7 billion loss as false.

He has argued that GoldBod’s audited 2025 financial statements show an operational surplus of GH¢907 million and an overall surplus of GH¢5.4 billion.

The CEO has also maintained that GoldBod’s role in the 2025 arrangement was primarily to purchase, assay and export gold on behalf of the BoG, while the central bank retained responsibility for the trading and sale of the gold to off-takers.

Mr Gyamfi has, consequently, challenged the Minority to identify where, in the IMF report, GoldBod itself is accused of causing the US$1.7 billion figure being cited.

But the Minority says the argument over which institution technically booked the loss should not become an excuse for avoiding scrutiny of the operations that generated the financial exposure.

Who bears responsibility?

Mrs Appiagyei said GoldBod’s status as an agent or intermediary did not, in the Minority’s view, remove the need to account for how the transactions were executed.

The Minority has argued that GoldBod occupied a central position in the domestic gold market, with responsibility for buying, weighing, grading, assaying, valuing and exporting gold.

The Caucus therefore wants greater disclosure of the pricing mechanisms, discounts, premiums, fees, off-taker arrangements and other commercial terms underpinning the transactions.

It is also demanding clarity on the relationship between GoldBod and the BoG, particularly why the central bank should bear the financial risk where GoldBod was involved in the operational chain.

The Minority says those questions are especially important because the programme was undertaken with public resources and was presented as a key instrument for strengthening Ghana’s reserves and stabilising the cedi.

Beyond the politics

The controversy has now moved beyond the original dispute over the figures to a wider debate about the governance of Ghana’s gold reserves and the role of the central bank in commercial transactions.

The IMF itself has said that the DGPP helped rebuild Ghana’s external buffers. By the end of 2025, Ghana’s gross international reserves had nearly doubled to about US$11.9 billion, supported in part by strong gold receipts.

But the Fund has simultaneously urged Ghana to end quasi-fiscal activities and strengthen the institutional framework surrounding domestic gold purchases.

For the Minority, Mrs Appiagyei said that was precisely why the matter should not be reduced to a political quarrel between Mr Gyamfi and the opposition.

She said Parliament had a constitutional responsibility to scrutinise the use of public resources and ensure that institutions entrusted with national assets operated transparently.

The Minority, she added, would continue to pursue the matter through the appropriate parliamentary processes.

“The personalities may change, governments may change, but accountability remains. We owe it to the Ghanaian people to establish what happened to their resources and who must answer for it,” she said.

Ghana News.title: GH¢22bn gold loss: Afenyo-Markin pushes for full parliamentary inquiry
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, says the Minority Caucus will pursue the necessary parliamentary processes to secure a full inquiry into the reported GH¢22 billion loss associated with the Bank of Ghana’s (BoG) Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP).

Mr Afenyo-Markin, who is also the Member of Parliament for Effutu, said the Minority would focus on establishing how the reported US$1.7 billion loss arose, the institutions and individuals involved in the transactions, and the financial decisions that resulted in the loss.

The comments follow an escalating war of words between the Minority Leader and the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, over the IMF-reported loss and GoldBod’s role in the transactions.

In a Facebook post on Saturday, August 22, Mr Afenyo-Markin said regardless of which institution's balance sheet ultimately carried the loss, the money involved was public funds and, therefore, subject to parliamentary scrutiny.

“I remain focused. I will continue working with the Minority Caucus to initiate the necessary parliamentary processes for a full inquiry into the reported GH¢22 billion loss arising from the trading done by the GoldBod and reflected in the books of the Bank of Ghana.” ‘Ghanaians deserve answers’

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the IMF's reported figure raised a number of questions that, in his view, required answers in the public interest.

“The International Monetary Fund has reported a loss of approximately US$1.7 billion under this programme in 2025.”

He said the Minority wanted details of the transactions, including the identities of the off-takers, discounts applied to gold purchases and the authority under which such discounts were approved.

“Whichever institution’s balance sheet carries that figure, it represents public money.”

He added:

“Ghanaians are, therefore, entitled to know who the off-takers were, what discounts were applied to their purchases, on whose authority those discounts were approved, and what fees were earned from the transactions.”

According to him, the Minority also wants the reported loss broken down to establish the specific factors that contributed to it.

“They are equally entitled to a full disaggregation of the US$1.7 billion: how much arose from foreign-exchange differentials; how much resulted from the prices at which GoldBod bought and sold the gold; and what considerations informed the management decisions behind those transactions.” ‘Put evidence in public domain’

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Minority intended to put the questions and supporting evidence before Parliament and the public rather than rely on political claims or personal assertions.

“These questions belong in the public record.”

He said the Minority would publish its sources and place the information before the public to enable Ghanaians to assess the evidence for themselves.

“The Minority will continue to place them there, in writing and with our sources published, so that every Ghanaian can examine the evidence and arrive at an informed judgment, rather than merely take my word or anyone else’s.”

The statement comes amid a broader debate over the financial performance and structure of the DGPP, under which the central bank purchased gold domestically as part of efforts to build reserves and support the country's foreign exchange position.

GoldBod has played a significant role in Ghana's domestic gold purchasing arrangements, making its operations a key part of the political and public debate surrounding the programme.

The dispute has centred partly on whether the reported loss should be attributed to GoldBod or the Bank of Ghana and how the transactions were structured.

Mr Afenyo-Markin, however, said the identity of the institution recording the loss should not prevent Parliament from investigating the underlying transactions.

Legal action

The Minority Leader also disclosed that he intended to pursue legal remedies over statements he described as defamatory.

“On the defamatory statements made against me personally, I intend to pursue the appropriate legal remedies.”

He, however, sought to distinguish the personal dispute from the Minority's substantive concerns about the gold programme.

“Meanwhile, my attention, and that of the Caucus I lead, remains firmly focused on the programme, the decisions taken and the public funds involved.”

The latest development is likely to intensify calls for greater disclosure around the DGPP, particularly concerning the pricing of gold, off-take arrangements, foreign exchange exposures, fees and the decision-making processes behind the transactions.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod row: Afenyo-Markin refuses to back down
Ghana News.content:
The Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, has defended the Minority’s scrutiny of the Bank of Ghana’s (BoG) Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP), insisting that attempts to subject him to personal attacks will not distract him from demanding accountability over the programme’s reported losses.

Mr Afenyo-Markin said his questioning of the programme and the role of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) was part of Parliament’s constitutional oversight responsibility and was not motivated by any personal or political agenda.

In a statement posted on social media on Saturday, August 22, the Effutu MP said the controversy had shifted from the substantive financial issues to attacks on his character following questions he had raised about the reported US$1.7 billion loss, equivalent to about GH¢22 billion, associated with the DGPP in 2025.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its recent assessment of the programme, said the rapid scaling-up of the DGPP had generated substantial losses for the Bank of Ghana and exposed the central bank to significant quasi-fiscal risks.

Mr Afenyo-Markin said he would not be deterred by the backlash.

“Over the past week, all manner of insults and personal attacks have been directed at me, apparently in an attempt to impugn my character and divert attention from the substantive questions I have raised,” he stated.

He said the attacks followed concerns raised by the Minority over the financial implications of the gold purchasing programme and GoldBod’s involvement in the transactions.

“False and defamatory allegations have also been made about my motives for questioning the losses incurred under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme and the role of GoldBod in those transactions,” he noted.

“These allegations are entirely false, and I reject them without qualification,” he insisted. ‘My duty is oversight’

The Minority Leader said his position was anchored in Parliament’s constitutional mandate to scrutinise public expenditure and hold institutions exercising public authority accountable.

“As Minority Leader in Parliament, my responsibility is to help Parliament discharge its constitutional oversight function,” he stressed. “My actions have been guided solely by that responsibility. I have neither acted from any improper motive nor conducted myself inappropriately in the performance of my duties.”

The comments come amid an increasingly heated public exchange between the Minority Leader and the Chief Executive Officer of GoldBod, Sammy Gyamfi, over the interpretation of the IMF’s reported loss.

Mr Gyamfi has rejected the characterisation of the US$1.7 billion figure as a loss incurred by GoldBod, arguing that the amount relates to the Bank of Ghana’s DGPP and should not be attributed to GoldBod’s own financial performance.

He has pointed to GoldBod’s audited 2025 financial statements, which show an operational surplus of GH¢907 million and an overall surplus of more than GH¢5.4 billion.

Mr Gyamfi has also maintained that GoldBod’s role under the 2025 DGPP was primarily to purchase and aggregate gold on behalf of the central bank and that it was not involved in the subsequent sale of the gold, determination of selling prices or negotiation of off-take agreements.

The IMF, however, has identified the DGPP as a source of significant financial risk to the Bank of Ghana and said losses associated with the programme and GoldBod-related activities should ultimately be transparently brought onto the national budget.

‘Questions will not disappear’

Mr Afenyo-Markin said the intensity of the response to his concerns reinforced the need for continued scrutiny rather than weakening the case for accountability.

“I recognise that, in public life, those who are uncomfortable with legitimate scrutiny may push back.”

He accused unnamed persons of attempting to change the subject of the debate by making the person raising the questions the focus of public controversy.

“In some cases, they may resort to false allegations, personal attacks and ridicule in an effort to shift attention from the substantive issues and make the person asking the questions the subject of controversy.”

The Minority’s position is that regardless of which state institution ultimately carries the accounting loss, Parliament must establish how the loss arose, the role played by the various institutions involved, whether the transactions represented value for money and what measures are being taken to prevent similar exposure.

The dispute has therefore widened into a broader debate about the financial cost of the country’s gold-for-reserves strategy, the role of GoldBod and the extent to which the economic benefits of the programme justify the losses recorded by the central bank.

For Mr Afenyo-Markin, however, the immediate issue remains accountability.

His latest response signals that the Minority intends to continue pursuing the matter despite the escalating political exchanges surrounding it.

Ghana News.title: Swedish sword attack victim was 17-year-old girl, police say
Ghana News.content:
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson visit the makeshift memorial.

The victim of a deadly sword attack at a high school in central Sweden was a 17-year-old girl, police have confirmed.

Two boys aged 12 and 17 were also seriously injured in the attack at Brinell School in Fagersta on Friday afternoon, according to local authorities, while a third person sustained minor injuries.

An 18-year-old man, who has not been named, was arrested and police said they were treating the case as murder and attempted murder.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson visited the school, where flower tributes have been laid to honour the victims, on Saturday morning.

Students at the school had only just returned to the classroom following the summer break when the deadly attack unfolded on Friday afternoon.

The police later confirmed they fired shots after being called to the scene but did not say whether the alleged attacker was hit before he was detained.

Sweden's public broadcaster reported that the suspect was wearing a helmet. Local media also said he was a former student.

The region went into a state of emergency on Friday, but it had ended by Saturday.

The school has just under 500 students on its roster, according to SVT, and is located 170km (105 miles) north-west of the capital, Stockholm.

Investigators have already carried out two house searches in connection with the suspect, police said.

On Friday, Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson described the attack as a "serious incident," and said "we do not know what lies behind the act, but we know that police are working very intensively", in a post on X.

Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf said he received the news "with dismay and sadness".

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
