World.title: New official tasked with promoting Poland criticised over error-strewn, potentially AI-generated report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A government official appointed last month to promote Poland abroad has been hit by a wave of criticism after it emerged that she authored a report containing errors and which shows signs of being generated by artificial intelligence. The document mislocated major Polish cities and included bizarre language mixing Polish and English. It was marked as being part of a project financed by the sport and tourism ministry, though the ministry itself has denied that claim. The opposition has called on prosecutors to investigate potential misuse of public funds. ⁉️ Czy “Markę Polska” ma nam wygenerować sztuczna inteligencja? ⁉️ Czy Ministerstwo Sportu i Turystyki zapłaciło 200 000 złotych w ramach zadania publicznego za raport wygenerowany przez AI? ⁉️ Czy mogę prosić Panią Minister prof. @b_mroz_gorgon o odniesienie się do tych pytań… pic.twitter.com/lM2AY88oAh — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 The official in question, Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, is a professor at Wrocław University of Economics who was appointed three weeks ago as the government’s plenipotentiary for the promotion of Poland’s brand, a newly created position. She was presented at a press conference by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. However, this week, journalists and commentators began highlighting cases of bizarre errors from a report, titled A Self-Portrait of the Poles (Polaków Portret Własny), published last year with Mróz-Gorgoń named as the author, in her position as president of a think tank called Marka Polska (Brand Poland). The report contained some glaring errors, such as describing the city of Katowice as being in “north central” Poland (whereas in fact it is in the south) and Wrocław as being in the “northwest” (when it is actually in the southwest). Geografia – czyli gdzie leżą Katowice A propos miast jest też ciekawy chochlik lub też, jakby to powiedział ktoś złośliwy, klasyczna halucynacja AI. Przy opisie badań FGI miasta opisane są w następujący sposób (zdjęcie poniżej): 👉 Olsztyn – północny wschód 👉 Szczecin -… pic.twitter.com/SF6XBRfhWS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 Other parts contain strange analysis, such as noting that “after World War Two, Germany did not build its brand on the Holocaust”. The text also features unusual language, including random use of words in English, some of which have been turned into Polish ones. It is also regularly features words written in capital letters. One sentence, for example, refers to “INSTABILNOŚĆ” and “REZILIENCE”, presumably meaning “instability” and “resilience”, but neither of which is a Polish word. Another section claims that 95% of Poles born after 1990 are “polilingwalni” (an invented Polonised version of “polylingual”) who speak “angielski fluent”, a strange linguistic mix that means they speak English fluently. As well as the unusual language, the very claim that 95% of young Poles speak fluent English, as well as that many additionally speak Mandarin, has been questioned by many commentators. The report also contains bizarre errors in footnotes, which are numbered randomly (on one page, three consecutive footnotes are numbered “41, 517, 6”) and some of which are completely empty. A number of expert commentators have suggested that the text contains clear indications that it was generated by AI, a claim supported by evidence from programmes that check texts for AI-generated content. AI czy nie AI, oto jest pytanie Czytając ten raport kilkukrotnie, trudno mi było pozbyć się wrażenia, że nikt poważny, a szczególnie naukowiec z tytułem doktora habilitowanego, nie wygenerowałby dużych części raportu, za który zapłacili podatnicy, w jakimś LLM. No bo przecież… pic.twitter.com/jyTexgmeXS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 As well as bearing Mróz-Gorgoń’s name as author, the report also features on its front cover the logo of the sport and tourism ministry. The first page then includes a note saying that the project was carried out under an initiative co-financed by the ministry. After the issue began to draw attention and criticism on Thursday, the ministry issued a statement saying that the report was not ordered by them, was not part of any agreement to which the ministry was a party, and that no request to use the ministry’s logo was submitted. However, a social media post last November by deputy sport and tourism minister Piotr Borys shows him attending an event to present the report. He thanked Mróz-Gorgoń for coordinating the project and inviting him to the presentation. 📚W Akademii Leona Koźmińskiego odbyła się prezentacja raportu „Polaków Portret Własny”, przygotowanego Think Tank Marka Polska. To wyjątkowe wydarzenie poświęcone premierze badań dotyczących DNA Marki Polska. 🧬To pierwsze tak kompleksowe badanie, które pokazuje, kim jesteśmy… pic.twitter.com/jb7KdCJTPM — Piotr Borys (@piotr_borys) November 26, 2025 On Thursday evening, Mróz-Gorgoń herself addressed the controversy in an interview with Polsat News. She said that the report was actually a “work in progress” that “should never have appeared in the public space”. However, she still defended the work, saying that “the research was conducted reliably” and “the conclusions stand up to scrutiny”. But she also admitted that the writing of the report had been “aided by artificial intelligence”. In separate remarks to the Polish Press Agency (PAP), she said that “we used AI tools solely for transcription, summarising and text editing; they did not design research content or draw conclusions…We worked according to social science methodology, diligently and without cutting corners”. Meanwhile, on the Marka Polska think tank’s website, where the report had been published, it was initially changed on Thursday to being marked as a “draft version” before later being deleted entirely. Od raportu i deklaracji, że “praca badawcza [została] przeprowadzona zgodnie z zasadami nauk społecznych, rzetelnie i merytorycznie, w oparciu o opisaną metodologię”, przez “work in progress”, aż do “Oops! That page can’t be found”. Myślę, że to słowo “Oops!” jest najlepszym… pic.twitter.com/OaSTxkwKwa — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 On Thursday evening, the main opposition party, Law and Justice (PiS), announced that it was submitting requests to both prosecutors and the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (ABW) to investigate the use of around 200,000 zloty (€46,380) in state funds for the project that the report was allegedly part of. PiS has also called on Mróz-Gorgoń to resign or to be fired. On Friday, a deputy digital affairs minister, Dariusz Standerski, told the Wirtualna Polska news website that “all the circumstances surrounding the creation of this report will be clarified”. The controversy around Mróz-Gorgoń comes just days after the sport and tourism ministry was involved in the launch of a new advertising campaign designed to encourage tourism to Poland, but which many commentators have argued was poorly conceived and executed. A speed of 253 km/h (157 mph) has been reached by a Pendolino train during tests carried out as part of preparations to speed up rail connections between Poland’s major cities from next year. The plans will see the journey time between Warsaw and Kraków cut to well under two hours. “Polish rail is accelerating – and 250 km/h is just the beginning,” declared the infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak, alluding to plans for Poland to later begin running trains at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Osiągnęliśmy 250 km/h na Centralnej Magistrali Kolejowej❗🚅 Dzisiejsze nocne testy systemu GSM-R na linii nr 4 zakończyły się pełnym sukcesem. Oznacza to, że pociągi pojadą tą trasą z rozkładową prędkością 250 km/h już w przyszłym roku❗ Pozwoli to znacznie skrócić czas… pic.twitter.com/ndXvePZP4t — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) August 18, 2026 The tests on the GSM-R data transmission system, a communication standard designed to be used at very high speeds, were carried out on Monday night. Trains will be able to run on Poland’s Central Main Line (CMK), which connects Warsaw with Kraków and Katowice, at a scheduled speed of 250 km/h from December 2027. That will cut the expected journey time between Warsaw and Kraków, the country’s two largest cities, by around half an hour to 1 hour and 52 minutes, reports rail news service Portal Kolejowy. It will also be possible to travel from the capital to Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, in around three hours. The fastest current connection is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Reaching the target speed of 250 km/h was a “very important moment for Polish rail”, said Maciej Kaczorek, a board member of PKP Polskie Linie Kolejowe, the state railway infrastructure manager, quoted by news website Money.pl. Poland has been operating Pendolinos, built by France’s Alstom, since 2014. The trains are designed to run at speeds of up to 250 km/h, but currently operate at a maximum of 200 km/h in Poland and run on routes connecting Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the Tricity area. However, this week’s tests are not a record rail speed in Poland. In 2013, a Pendolino reached 293 km/h during a test on the CMK a year before the high-speed trains commenced passenger services in the country. A Polish Pendolino high-speed train has begun running in the Czech Republic for the first time. The Prague-Bohumín service will run until June as part of a certification process that Polish operator PKP Intercity hopes will lead to a Warsaw-Prague route https://t.co/hmUNd7ft0E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 10, 2026 Speaking to Rynek Kolejowy, deputy infrastructure minister Piotr Malepszak said that it had “taken too long” for the network to be adapted to allow regular speeds of 250 km/h. The current government, which took power in December 2023, has much broader plans for expanding high-speed rail travel in Poland, including building 2,700 km of tracks capable of carrying trains at 320 km/h. In December 2025, state rail operator PKP Intercity launched a tender for 20 such trains. They would cut the journey time between Warsaw and Gdańsk, on Poland’s Baltic coast, to around 100 minutes – from 2 hours 25 minutes currently – by 2040, Malepszak told the Polish Press Agency in June. Passenger numbers on Poland’s rail network have been booming in recent years. In the first half of 2026, a record 44.7 million passengers travelled with PKP Intercity, more than 10% up on the previous year’s record and some 45% higher than three years earlier. Poland has launched a tender to buy 20 trains that can reach speeds of 320 km/h (199 mph), making them the fastest ever to travel on Polish tracks. World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: More Czech Companies Test Four-Day Work Weeks Despite Political Resistance
World.content:
A growing number of companies in the Czech Republic are experimenting with a four-day working week, with some reporting higher productivity and greater employee satisfaction.

But politicians remain reluctant to make the arrangement a standard option across the country.

Under the model, employees work four days instead of five while keeping their full salaries. Companies that have introduced the system say workers can maintain their output while having more time to rest.



At Trinity Group, the arrangement has been in place for five years. Jan Hanulík, the company’s product and marketing director, said productivity had risen despite employees working one day less each week.

“Although we have one working day less, productivity has increased,” Hanulík said, adding that the company’s results have roughly doubled since the system was introduced.

A survey cited in the report found that around 70 percent of employees in the Czech Republic would welcome a four-day working week.

Politicians remain cautious

The idea has already been adopted in different forms elsewhere in Europe. In Belgium, for example, employees can request to work their weekly hours over four days rather than five. The system therefore does not necessarily mean fewer working hours.

Czech politicians, however, argue that a single system would not work across all sectors.

Labor and Social Affairs Minister Aleš Juchelka of ANO said a legally mandated four-day week could create problems in areas already facing staff shortages, including social services and health care.

SPD lawmaker Lucie Šafránková also said the working week should reflect the conditions of individual professions and employers rather than follow one nationwide rule.

Czech companies are already experimenting

Several companies have introduced or tested four-day schedules, including SAB Finance, Phonexia, Sherpas, Digiskills and Café Eternity.

Not every experiment has lasted. The Cognito agency eventually returned to a traditional five-day working week after testing the shorter schedule.

World.title: Foreign Workers Now Make Up 22% of Czech Employees
World.content:
Foreign workers accounted for around 22% of all employees in the Czech Republic at the end of 2025, according to data from the Czech National Bank (ČNB).

Their number has nearly tripled over the past decade, rising from about 323,000 in 2015 to 935,000 last year.

The increase has significantly changed the makeup of the Czech labor market. Foreign workers represented roughly 8% of all employees in 2015. By the end of 2025, their share had reached 22%.

Ukrainians made up the largest group of foreign employees, with approximately 358,000 working in Czechia at the end of last year. Slovaks were the second-largest group, numbering almost 230,000.



The Czech labor market has also seen increasing numbers of workers from other countries outside the European Union, including the Philippines and India.

Foreign workers are particularly important in several sectors, including manufacturing, construction, retail, transport and hospitality.

Their presence is most pronounced in accommodation, food services and hospitality. Foreign nationals accounted for more than half of all employees in the sector at the end of 2025.

The figures should, however, be interpreted with some caution when comparing individual industries. The CNB notes that employment agencies can distort the sectoral breakdown.

Workers employed through agencies are recorded in official statistics under administrative and support services, even when their actual jobs are in manufacturing, construction, logistics or other industries.

World.title: Tesco Teams Up With Wolt. Can Express Delivery Save Its Czech Business?
World.content:
Tesco will launch a new express delivery service in Prague in September, working with Wolt to deliver orders within 40 minutes.

The service, called Tesco Hned, will initially be available from selected Tesco stores in the Czech capital.

The launch comes as speculation continues over a possible sale of Tesco’s Central European operations and the British retailer’s future in the Czech Republic.



Tesco Hned is designed for customers who need groceries and other everyday products quickly rather than as part of a larger planned shop. Orders will include food, drinks, cosmetics, household products, pet supplies and other goods.

The company says its standard online shopping service will continue to focus on larger orders, while the new option is aimed at customers who need a few items immediately.

Tesco has already tested the service at six Prague stores. It plans to extend Tesco Hned to another 22 locations in the coming weeks.

Delivery will be provided through Wolt, giving customers access to Tesco products through the courier company’s platform.

Tesco faces questions over its future

The new service comes at a difficult time for Tesco in Central Europe.

According to the Financial Times, Tesco’s British owners are considering selling their operations in the region, including the Czech Republic. The Schwarz Group, which owns Lidl and Kaufland, and Polish retailer Biedronka have reportedly been mentioned among potential buyers.

Tesco has not announced plans to leave the Czech market, and the launch of Tesco Hned suggests the company continues to invest in its services.

World.title: New Budget Airline to Launch Direct Flights from Prague to Santiago de Compostela
World.content:
A new budget airline is set to launch direct flights between Prague and Santiago de Compostela in Spain, giving travellers from the Czech capital a new low-cost option for visiting Galicia and the famous Camino de Santiago.

Fly2Galicia plans to begin operating flights from Santiago–Rosalía de Castro Airport to eight European destinations from December 1, 2026.



Prague is among the international destinations, alongside Brussels, Munich, Venice and Milan.

Tickets are already on sale, with fares from Prague to Santiago de Compostela starting at €51.

The new route could be particularly attractive in 2027, when Santiago de Compostela will celebrate a Holy Year. The occasion is expected to bring increased numbers of pilgrims completing the Camino de Santiago, one of Europe’s best-known pilgrimage routes.

There is, however, one detail to note: Fly2Galicia will not operate the initial flights itself. The airline says the routes will be operated by another European carrier, which has not yet been named.

The new service comes as airlines continue to expand connections between Central Europe and Spain. Wizz Air has also announced new flights to Santiago from Rome and Warsaw starting this December.

What to see in Santiago de Compostela

For travellers arriving from Prague, Santiago’s historic centre is the main attraction. Its UNESCO-listed Old Town combines Romanesque, Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical architecture, with the Cathedral of Santiago at the heart of the city.

The Mercado de Abastos is another popular stop, offering fresh seafood and local produce. Galicia is also known for Albariño, a white wine that pairs particularly well with the region’s seafood.

Santiago can also serve as a base for exploring Galicia, with trips to A Coruña, Vigo and the Rías Baixas wine region, as well as the area’s beaches and islands.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: Students in Czech Republic Face Higher Rents as Housing Costs Rise
World.content:
Students looking for private accommodation in Czech university cities this year are facing higher rents, with prices for some types of housing up by as much as 14 percent compared with 2025.

The increase comes as demand for student accommodation reaches its annual peak ahead of the winter semester.

Data from several Czech property platforms show that the busiest period started earlier this year, meaning students who have not yet found accommodation may face a more limited and expensive selection in September.

Those unable to secure a place in a student dormitory generally have three alternatives: renting a small apartment alone, taking a private room in a shared apartment, or renting a bed in shared accommodation.



The most expensive option is usually a small one-bedroom apartment with a kitchenette, typically around 30 square meters. According to the REMAX network, monthly rents for these apartments range from more than CZK 7,000 in Ústí nad Labem to around CZK 14,000 in Prague.

Prices have not increased evenly across the country. Brno recorded the sharpest rise, with rents for small apartments increasing by 12 percent year on year.

Prague saw a 4 percent increase, while rents in Hradec Králové and Pardubice rose by almost 9 percent. Olomouc was one of the few exceptions, with prices falling by slightly more than 2 percent.

Rent is not the only expense students need to consider. Utilities, water and maintenance charges can add another CZK 1,000 to CZK 2,000 a month, according to property platforms.

Private rooms offer a cheaper alternative

Many students instead rent individual rooms in shared apartments, with properties ranging from smaller 2+kk and 2+1 layouts to larger 4+kk and 4+1 apartments. Czech property portal Sreality.cz puts the average cost of a private room in university cities at between approximately CZK 5,700 in Opava and CZK 11,500 in Prague.

In Prague, private rooms listed on Sreality.cz were around 10 percent more expensive than during the same period last year. Prices in Brno, meanwhile, remained roughly unchanged.

Shared housing remains the cheapest option

For students on a tighter budget, sharing an apartment and renting a bed rather than an entire room remains the least expensive choice. The more people share a property, the lower the individual housing costs tend to be.

Even this option, however, has become more expensive. According to UlovDomov.cz, the cost of renting a bed has increased by several hundred Czech crowns compared with last year.

Prague remains considerably more expensive. A bed in a two-bedroom apartment costs almost CZK 5,500, about CZK 1,200 more than a bed in a three-bedroom apartment.

World.title: 58 Years Since Warsaw Pact Troops Invaded Czechoslovakia
World.content:
On August 21, 1968, Soviet troops and their Warsaw Pact allies invaded Czechoslovakia to bring an end to that country’s brief period of political liberalization, called the Prague Spring.

People still recall waking up on that fateful morning to find that Soviet-led Warsaw Pact tanks had rolled into the country, crushing all hope of implementing the democratic reforms of the Prague Spring. Shocked citizens took to the streets in protest of the invasion.

About 500,000 troops were involved in the invasion and occupation, during which 137 Czechoslovaks died and some 500 were wounded.

One of the key battles was for the control of Czech Radio, similar to the one that took place at the end of the Second World War.

The invasion ended the political and economic reforms led by Alexander Dubcek and reasserted dominant Soviet and Communist authority in Czechoslovakia.

It also helped establish the Brezhnev Doctrine, which Moscow said allowed the U.S.S.R. to intervene in any country where a communist government was under threat.

Within the following year, resistance faded, Dubček was removed from office, his reforms were undone, and a more Soviet-controlled government was installed.

World.title: Prague’s Groovy Market Fest Returns After a Successful Debut
World.content:
A new urban festival is aiming to become a regular fixture on Prague’s cultural calendar after attracting 1,200 visitors to its first edition in Riegrovy sady.

Groovy Market Fest, held on August 1, brought together food, design, music and local brands in a format inspired by European city markets.

According to the organizers, around 85% of visitors were tourists or foreign residents of Prague, highlighting the event’s appeal beyond the Czech-speaking audience.



The festival will return to Riegrovy sady on September 5, with further editions planned for October, November and December.

From Barcelona to Prague

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food culture.

Their interest in international gastronomy also led them to compete in Spain. In 2025, they won first place in the Cooking The Street competition, where their dish was judged by a professional panel that included chefs Beñat Ormaetxea and Jon Kepa Aurrecoetxea.

After returning to Prague, they decided to develop their own event, drawing inspiration from markets such as Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market.

The First Edition

Food Garden focused on gastronomy, while Palm Street featured local products and handmade goods. The Design Zone presented Czech brands working in fashion, design and art.

Rather than filling the site with as many vendors as possible, the organizers selected a smaller number of participants. They say the approach was intended to create a more coherent experience for visitors.

Music was another part of the programme, with live performances and DJ sets throughout the event. Visitors could also attend a masterclass focused on preparing the festival’s signature Groovy cocktail.

Additional editions are scheduled for October 3, November 7 and December 5, all at the same location.

Tickets for upcoming editions are available through GoOut.

World.title: Paks nuclear plant begins turbine restart as Hungary races towards full capacity
World.content:
Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant has begun the process of restarting its third turbine, marking another major step towards restoring the facility to full capacity after the Danube’s record-low water levels forced several units offline.

The restart of the 6th turbine in Unit 3 began on Friday evening and entered its final, most critical stage on Saturday night, Prime Minister Péter Magyar said during a live broadcast from the nuclear power plant.

Two turbines are currently operating at Paks. Once the third turbine is successfully connected to the electricity grid, the plant will gradually increase its output, with full capacity of around 2,000 megawatts expected to be reached by Wednesday.

A 49-hour process is nearing its final stage

According to Magyar, restarting a turbine takes around 49 hours, meaning preparations for the third turbine began almost two days before the live broadcast. By Saturday evening, the process had reached its final three hours. This is the most critical phase, as engineers begin bringing the turbine up to its operating speed.

Károly Vigh, the plant’s director of operations, explained that the turbine is initially kept turning at just 3–4 revolutions per minute. This prevents the turbine shaft from bending and ensures that heat is distributed evenly throughout the machinery.

If you missed it: PM Magyar announces earlier restart of Paks 3rd reactor block

The restart is carried out in several stages. The turbine is first brought up to 600 revolutions per minute, followed by a technical inspection. It is then increased to 900 rpm and checked again before eventually reaching its operating speed of 3,000 rpm.

The final acceleration is particularly critical, with the turbine’s speed increasing by 600 revolutions per minute at a time. Once the turbine reaches 3,000 rpm, it can be connected to the electricity grid. However, it can take a further hour and a half to two hours before the turbine’s output appears on the grid operated by Hungary’s transmission system operator MAVIR.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Another turbine is expected to follow

The restart of the third turbine is only part of the wider process to restore Paks to full operation. According to the latest schedule, the second turbine of Unit 1 could be ready for parallel connection to the grid from around 8 AM on Sunday.

Preparations have also begun for restarting Unit 4. The 7th and 8th turbines are expected to be the last ones to enter the restart process, with their restart scheduled to begin around midnight. Plant officials said that restarting turbines is not an unusual procedure for Paks: between six and ten planned turbine restarts are carried out each year as part of maintenance and repair work.

However, the current situation is highly unusual. Vigh said that three reactors have to be brought back into operation at the same time – something that has never happened before in Hungary. Around 20–25 people have been working continuously to restart an individual unit, while approximately 75 workers are involved in restarting three turbines simultaneously.

Emergency Danube works made the restart possible

The restart would not have been possible without the emergency measures introduced after the Danube fell to exceptionally low levels during the summer heatwave. The river’s water level dropped so dramatically that Paks was unable to draw enough cooling water for normal operation. Unit 3 was shut down on 29 July, while from 2 August only the two turbines of Unit 2 were operating at full capacity.

The government subsequently ordered the construction of a bottom sill in the Danube near the power plant, designed to raise and stabilise the water level at the cooling-water intake. Two barges were also temporarily sunk in the riverbed, while additional water was released through the Ráckeve lock system.

The emergency works have significantly improved conditions at Paks. The bottom sill currently has an estimated lifting capacity of around 20 centimetres, while more than 6,200 tonnes of rock have already been incorporated into the structure. Around 231 metres of the construction has been completed along the left bank.

Danube level has risen significantly

Magyar said the Danube at Paks was around -100 centimetres on Saturday, compared with approximately -140 centimetres earlier in the crisis. Forecasts suggest that the level could rise to around -74 centimetres by Thursday before beginning to fall again if no significant rainfall arrives. The forecast does not include the additional effect of the bottom sill.

The government therefore intends to continue construction despite the improving water level, in order to provide greater protection against another decline.

Earlier this month, the exceptionally low river level raised fears that Paks could face a complete shutdown, potentially creating a serious challenge for Hungary’s electricity supply. The emergency measures ultimately meant that a total shutdown could be avoided.

Full capacity now within sight

Magyar said the aim is for the Paks Nuclear Power Plant to return to its full 2,000 MW capacity by Wednesday. The gradual restart represents a dramatic turnaround from the situation earlier this month, when Hungary’s largest nuclear power plant was operating at only a fraction of its normal capacity because of the Danube’s record-low water level.

World.title: Tisza MP shared when Hungary’s asset recovery office could start investigating high-profile cases
World.content:
Hungary’s newly established National Office for Asset Recovery and Asset Protection could begin investigating high-profile cases within months, with the institution expected to employ around 200 people, according to István Hantosi, chair of Parliament’s Justice and Constitutional Affairs Committee.

The office, which, according to Hungary’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar, will be “the strongest anti-corruption institute in Europe”, is expected to be established alongside the prosecution service, with its president holding a position at the same level as the Prosecutor General. Parliament could elect the president and four deputies as early as the second half of next week.

New institution to have broad powers

The office was created under legislation recently approved by Hungary’s Parliament. Its supporters, including the Tisza Party, have presented it as a major anti-corruption institution intended to recover public assets and investigate suspected abuses. The leadership structure will include four deputy presidents responsible for public finances, investigations, prosecution and appeals.

Candidates must meet strict eligibility requirements. They must have no criminal record, while recent political office can also disqualify applicants. The president does not necessarily have to be a lawyer, but must have at least 15 years of professional experience in their field, or a relevant academic degree combined with at least 10 years of professional experience, writes 444.

The deputy responsible for public finances faces similar requirements, including professional experience in areas covered by the tax or customs authorities. The investigation, prosecution and appeals deputies must be practising prosecutors. A total of 96 people applied for the president’s position, while 68 applications were submitted for the deputy posts.

Hungary’s new office will work alongside prosecutors

The new institution will not be a superior body to the prosecution service. Hantosi stressed that its president will not be able to instruct prosecutors directly. However, the prosecution service will not be able to refuse requests from the new office to hand over relevant cases or documents, according to Hantosi. The two organisations will therefore need to coordinate closely, while retaining their separate institutional roles.

The Tisza Party expects the beginning of autumn to be largely devoted to establishing the new office and recruiting its staff. Hantosi said he would be disappointed if the first high-profile accountability cases had not begun by the end of the year.

More on the Tisza government: PM Magyar’s first 100 days — Success or failure for Hungary?

Focus on suspected abuses linked to the NER

Asset recovery and accountability have been presented as key elements of the Tisza Party’s political programme. Hantosi said Parliament would not provide the office with a formal list of cases to prioritise, but argued that the major alleged abuses connected to Hungary’s National Cooperation System (NER) are already well known.

He said it was unclear which cases would be examined first, pointing to a wide range of controversial economic affairs involving major business groups and public institutions. The new office could therefore become a significant part of the incoming government’s promised efforts to investigate suspected corruption and recover public funds, provided it becomes fully operational as planned.

World.title: Huge vegetation fire threatened residential homes in Hungary
World.content:
A fire has broken out in dry grass and leaf litter near Bányász Street in Szolnok, eastern Hungary, with flames spreading in several directions and threatening nearby homes. The National Directorate General for Disaster Management reported the blaze on Saturday, saying local firefighters were working to contain and prevent it from reaching residential buildings.

Firefighters use five water jets

Professional first responders from Szolnok tackled the flames with six water jets. Additional crews from Cegléd have been dispatched to assist, while the disaster management operations service also travelled to the scene. The dry vegetation allowed the flames to spread, making the proximity of residential properties a particular concern.

However, Tamás Kisnémet, deputy spokesperson for the Jász-Nagykun-Szolnok County Disaster Management Directorate, told the Hungarian news agency MTI that no measures to protect or evacuate residents have been necessary so far. They have managed to bring it under control and prevent further spread.

Recent large vegetation blazes in Hungary

The Szolnok incident comes just days after a much larger incident near Polgár, where around 100 hectares of land were affected. The blaze, which broke out near the Route 35 main road, also destroyed around 2,000 bales of straw and four buildings. Firefighters have since managed to contain those flames as well.

World.title: Mysterious alkaline pollution found in the Danube in Hungary as authorities start investigation
World.content:
An investigation is under way after a dark brown liquid was observed flowing into the significantly receded bed of the Danube near Almásfüzitő, in northern Hungary. Measurements by investigative news outlet Átlátszó indicated that the liquid has a pH of 10, meaning it is strongly alkaline.

The substance was visible along roughly a one-kilometre stretch of the riverbank below the former red mud reservoirs. Its exact composition has not yet been established, and authorities are awaiting laboratory results.

Authorities launch investigation

The Győr-Moson-Sopron County Government Office, which is responsible for water and water-protection matters in the case, said it had received three reports concerning the suspected pollution. Officials began an investigation and carried out an on-site inspection on 12 August. They said the findings are still being evaluated and that no legal violation has been established so far. The authority added that it would take appropriate action if the assessment finds grounds for intervention.

Continuous environmental monitoring is also taking place in the area, including checks on both surface and groundwater. The North Transdanubian Water Directorate said it is not a regulatory authority and therefore cannot take enforcement action itself. However, it has reported the conditions around the red mud reservoirs, including those associated with the low water level, to the competent water authority.

The operator, Tatai Környezetvédelmi Zrt. (TKV), did not respond to Átlátszó’s questions, although reports indicate that the company has also taken samples from the affected area. Almásfüzitő’s independent mayor, Gergely Szabó, said the municipality was aware of the pollution and had also reported it. The town is now waiting for the laboratory results to establish exactly what is entering the Danube.

Residents report unusual smell

Local residents and anglers have reportedly complained about the phenomenon. Some residents described a strong, medicinal-like odour, saying it had at times irritated their airways. Átlátszó reported that the dark brown substance could be clearly seen entering the exposed riverbed over approximately one kilometre, with the strip along the riverbank appearing affected.

The low water level of the Danube has made the phenomenon particularly visible, but the source and environmental impact of the liquid remain unclear until laboratory testing is completed.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Former red mud reservoirs now used for waste

The Almásfüzitő site contains former red mud storage cells and is reportedly the country’s second-largest red mud reservoir after the disaster site at Kolontár. Areas classified as Natura 2000 sites are located nearby.

The reservoirs are now managed by TKV and have been subject to a reclamation process involving the covering of the former red mud cells with hazardous and non-hazardous waste and biological treatment. The company is authorised to deposit up to 315,000 tonnes of waste a year in Cell VII, including 280,000 tonnes of non-hazardous waste.

Environmental organisation Greenpeace has raised concerns about the site for years, arguing that pollutants could enter groundwater and the Danube from the unlined reservoirs. The organisation previously cited measurements showing elevated levels of fluoride, arsenic and molybdenum in groundwater.

More on river Danube: Key deal secured for new Danube bridge at Mohács, with new photos

Concerns raised, but the company just renewed their permits

The operator and authorities, however, have maintained that the site’s activities comply with the relevant regulations. The facility received renewed environmental permits in 2020 and 2025, with the latest permit reportedly containing stricter conditions than previous authorisations.

The TKV is owned by Envirotis Holding, which has been linked to the Mészáros Group through the Status Next environmental private equity fund. For now, the key question remains unanswered: what exactly is flowing into the Danube? Authorities and local officials are awaiting laboratory results before determining whether further measures are necessary.

World.title: Breaking: PM Magyar announces earlier restart of Paks 3rd reactor block
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar says electricity generation at Unit 3 of Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant could resume as early as Saturday evening, following a rise in the Danube’s water level and emergency works carried out near the plant.

Third reactor block could restart ahead of schedule

“Thanks to the construction works at Paks and the rising water level of the Danube, production in Unit 3 could resume today, earlier than planned,” Magyar said in a Saturday Facebook post. The prime minister added that the reconnection of the unit would be shown live from Paks on Saturday evening.

The announcement comes after weeks of concern over the exceptionally low water level of the Danube, which threatened the cooling capacity of the nuclear power plant. The facility relies on water from the river for cooling, and the record-low levels reached earlier this month forced several units to be taken offline.

Emergency measures raised the river level

The Hungarian government responded by ordering the construction of a submerged weir, or bottom sill, near the plant and deploying barges in the riverbed to help raise the water level at the facility’s intake.

According to Magyar, the measures have already increased the water level by around 15 centimetres. Construction of the bottom sill is also progressing rapidly, with 231 metres reportedly completed along the left bank.

The two barges placed in the Danube on 15 August have since been removed from their submerged position after the operation successfully increased the water level above them. The intervention has allowed the two turbines that remained in operation to continue generating electricity, avoiding a complete shutdown of the plant.

Barges at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

If you missed it: PM Magyar: Hungary begins sinking two huge barges to raise Danube water levels near Paks

Paks gradually returning to full capacity

The nuclear power plant was severely affected by the Danube’s low water level at the beginning of August. From 2 August, only the turbines of Unit 2 were operating at full capacity, although two turbines were able to return to operation on 10 August as water levels improved.

Magyar previously said that the remaining inactive units would be gradually reconnected from midnight on Sunday, with the entire facility potentially returning to full capacity by Thursday or Friday next week.

The latest announcement suggests that the restart of Unit 3 could now come earlier than that timetable.

The development follows a prolonged period of extreme heat and exceptionally low Danube water levels, which had raised concerns over Hungary’s electricity supply and the operation of one of the country’s most important power-generating facilities.

The Danube at Paks. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Emergency river works continue

The rapid construction of the bottom sill and the use of barges have become a key part of efforts to secure sufficient cooling water for the Paks plant.

The government approved the construction of the bottom sill on 12 August, with work beginning shortly afterwards. The emergency intervention is intended to provide a more stable water level at the plant’s cooling-water intake while the Danube remains unusually low.

Minister: Construction of Danube riverbed sill is progressing faster than planned

Construction of the Danube riverbed sill is progressing faster than planned, and the water level is rising, the defense minister wrote in a brief update posted on his Facebook page on Saturday from Dunaszentbenedek. Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi reported that all water had been pumped out of the barges and that the process of sinking them had been completed.

“The pumps are currently being dismantled; until this work is completed, the barges will remain at their original anchorage points. Afterwards, they are scheduled to begin construction of the riverbed sill on the right bank, as the water flow and the already constructed riverbed sill ensure the water level necessary for the safe operation of the nuclear power plant,” the minister added.

The minister noted that construction of the riverbed sill is also continuing on the left bank of the Danube. He added that work on the left bank has been completed over a 231-meter stretch, reaching the concrete blocks that had been previously placed in the river. He noted that nearly 4,000 cubic meters of stone had been installed, weighing a total of 6,200 metric tons.

Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi emphasised that a continuous supply of stone is being ensured for the work, and that five civilian vehicles are being driven by soldiers between the quarry and the depot.

“People, machines, and materials are working around the clock,” the minister stated. He added that the task remains to construct, reinforce, and complete the work.

“We are working to ensure that Hungarian households have electricity, that water flows from the taps, and that Hungary’s nuclear safety is guaranteed under all circumstances,” the minister emphasised in his post, noting that this is not simply a technical task, but a matter of the country’s functioning and security.

World.title: Major Hungarian banks announce service outages: Here’s what you need to know
World.content:
Customers of OTP, MBH and Erste should prepare for several scheduled IT maintenance periods over the coming weeks. Depending on the institute and the time of the work, card payments, bank transfers, online and mobile banking services may temporarily be unavailable.

Customers planning important payments are advised to check the relevant maintenance periods in advance.

OTP: card payments to be suspended

OTP will carry out maintenance on its card payment system from 1 AM on 25 August, with the disruption expected to last around 90 minutes. During this period, transactions will not be possible through either POS terminals or online payment platforms. OTP-branded cards will also be unavailable for payments and cash withdrawals.

A separate maintenance period will affect the bank’s Persely savings service on 30 August, when the service is expected to be unavailable throughout the day.

MBH announces several maintenance periods

MBH customers face a series of disruptions affecting different services. On 27 August from 7.30 PM to 10 PM, functions related to applying for and managing personal loans will be unavailable in the MBH Bank mobile app.

Later that evening, from 10 PM on 27 August until 2 AM on 28 August, SMS messages required for two-factor authentication on the MBH Netbroker and Mobilbroker platforms may be affected. Further maintenance will take place from 10 PM on 28 August until 2 AM on 29 August, when MBH’s Netbroker and Mobilbroker investment platforms may only be available with limited functionality.

On 5 September between 4 AM and 11 AM, the former Budapest Bank Netbank service will operate with reduced functionality, while securities-related features will be unavailable. The most extensive MBH disruption currently scheduled will run from 10 PM on 28 September until 3.59 AM on 29 September.

During these periods, several important services will be unavailable, including George App and Web, TeleBank, corporate online banking services, Electra and Erste Business MobilBank. Customers will also be unable to initiate instant transfers.

During the first maintenance period, online shopping will also be unavailable from 10 PM on 18 September until 10 AM the following day. The receipt of instant transfers will be interrupted between midnight and 4 AM on 19 September. However, according to Erste’s notice, card payments at Point of Sale terminals and domestic ATM cash withdrawals and deposits will remain available during the maintenance.

With several disruptions scheduled across three major Hungarian financial establishments, customers should consider completing important transfers or other banking tasks outside the affected periods and ensure they have alternative payment options available where necessary.

World.title: Tropical fever disease has appeared in Hungary
World.content:
An imported case of the disease called chikungunya fever has been confirmed in Bács-Kiskun County, Hungary after a 53-year-old woman returned from Mauritius, according to Hungary’s latest weekly epidemiological report.

The National Public Health and Pharmaceutical Centre (NNGYK) recorded the laboratory-confirmed case during the 32nd epidemiological week, covering 3–9 August 2026. The woman was in Mauritius during the infection’s incubation period and is believed to have contracted the virus there.

What kind of disease is chikungunya fever?

Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted primarily through the bites of infected mosquitoes. The main vectors are the Aedes aegypti, or yellow fever mosquito, and the Aedes albopictus, commonly known as the Asian tiger mosquito.

The infection does not spread directly from person to person without a mosquito acting as an intermediary. Around one-third of infected people may remain symptom-free. In those who develop symptoms, the incubation period is generally several days, after which the illness can cause:

sudden, high fever;

severe joint pain;

headaches;

muscle pain; and

an occasional skin rash.

Most patients begin to recover within a week, and the fatality rate is extremely low. However, more serious complications can pose a greater risk to older people, newborn babies and those with weakened immune systems, according to the NNGYK.

Imported chikungunya cases remain uncommon in Hungary, with only a small number of travel-related infections generally recorded each year.

Your story. Your perspective. Our readers. Write for Daily News Hungary!

Malaria case also linked to overseas travel

The same weekly report recorded another imported tropical infection. An 18-year-old man living in Pest County was diagnosed with malaria after spending time in Tanzania during the disease’s incubation period.

Laboratory testing identified Plasmodium falciparum as the causative parasite. This species is responsible for the most severe form of malaria and can require urgent medical treatment.

This might interest you: How to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest — a tourist’s guide

Gastroenteritis outbreak affects 54 people

The NNGYK report also documented a larger outbreak unrelated to overseas travel. An enteric outbreak occurred at a hotel in Zala County, where 54 of 640 exposed people became ill between 1 August and the publication of the report. Those affected included 50 hotel guests and four members of staff.

Vomiting and diarrhoea were the main symptoms. They reportedly disappeared within a short period, and most of those affected did not require medical attention.

Hungary’s public health authorities publish weekly epidemiological reports to monitor infectious diseases across the country and identify outbreaks and imported infections. The latest figures highlight how international travel can occasionally introduce diseases that are otherwise rarely encountered in Hungary.

World.title: Less than half of Romanians manage to save regularly, survey finds
World.content:
Roughly 48% of Romanians are able to put away money every month or most months, while a quarter manage to put money aside only occasionally, when they have funds left, according to a survey conducted at the initiative of tbi bank on a sample of 1,223 employees nationwide.

The survey, published on Friday, August 21, shows that Romanians’ real savings capacity remains limited and vulnerable to increasing pressures on the monthly budget.

Roughly 22% of respondents currently do not save at all or are forced to draw on previously accumulated reserves. Moreover, about 46% manage to save no more than RON 500 in a typical month, and 16% are unable to set aside any money at all.

The ability to save remains moderate even among those who manage to put money aside: almost 22% save between 11% and 20% of income, and just over 22% manage to keep between 6% and 10%.

“For many Romanians, saving remains the result of a fragile balance at the end of the month rather than a consistent financial plan. The increase in essential costs limits the amounts available, and this makes financial discipline, access to simple and safe products and the formation of savings habits increasingly important,” said Gergana Staykova, Market Leader, tbi bank Romania.

The ability to save has deteriorated for an important part of Romanians in the last period. Almost 42% say they save less than last year, and over 9% managed to put money aside previously, but currently they can no longer do so. At the same time, more than 29% save primarily for unforeseen situations or emergencies, and about 20% aim to build more security and financial independence.

Over 36% say they save only what they have left after covering expenses, while only about 15% set aside a fixed percentage of their monthly income. At the same time, almost 23% could cover their expenses for less than a month if they lost their main source of income, and about 22% could cover their expenses for between one and three months.

Romanians keep their savings mainly in forms perceived as safe and easy to access. Over 23% keep most of their savings in their current account, and almost 22% choose bank deposits. At the same time, more than 26% point to the increase in the price of food and basic products as the main obstacle to saving, and almost 25% say that income is too low in relation to expenses.

Savings are used both for planned experiences and needs, and as a reserve for unforeseen expenses. Almost 19% of Romanians have used or would have liked to use their savings for vacations and personal experiences, and over 14% for home or car repairs. The financial targets for 2026 are mainly geared towards strengthening reserves and protecting personal stability, amid fears related in particular to health and income. Almost 20% of Romanians aim to save more than last year, and almost 15% want to protect their existing savings. At the same time, more than 30% point to health problems as their biggest financial fear, and 21% primarily fear losing their job.

The tbi bank survey on how Romanians manage their money in 2026 was conducted online in July this year, on a total sample of 1,223 internet users in Romania, of which over 53% are men, 68% work in the private sector, and over 31% have a net income of over RON 6,000.

World.title: Romania’s real estate investment volume falls to EUR 300 million in H1 2026 - report
World.content:
Romania’s real estate investment market recorded transactions worth approximately EUR 300 million in the first half of 2026, down from around EUR 400 million in the same period last year, according to a Colliers report. The consultancy estimates that the full-year volume could approach EUR 1 billion if several large transactions currently underway are completed.

Romania accounted for roughly 5% of the EUR 5.8 billion invested across the six largest Central and Eastern European economies: Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia.

Regional investment increased by 7% year-on-year and exceeded both the five-year average of EUR 4.6 billion and the ten-year average of EUR 5.1 billion. Colliers expects the regional total to reach EUR 12.5-13 billion in 2026, compared with EUR 11.6 billion last year.

“The decline in transaction volumes in Romania during the period under review should be seen in a broader context,” said Robert Miklo, partner and head of capital markets at Colliers.

He noted that several deals are in progress, while the sale of a MAS retail portfolio to AFI Europe was completed shortly after the end of the reporting period, shifting the transaction into the third quarter.

“If other large transactions currently in progress are also completed, 2026 has the potential to close with investment volumes of close to EUR 1 billion, which would make it only the second year since 2007 in which the market has reached this threshold,” Miklo said.

Office properties generated approximately 60% of Romania’s transaction volume during the first half, their highest share since 2022. Colliers expects that percentage to decline as major deals in other sectors are completed during the remainder of the year.

“Influenced by the limited supply of properties available for sale, investment volumes remain below the level suggested by both investor appetite and the size of the local economy. In the first half of the year, Romania attracted just 5.4% of the investment volume recorded across the six largest economies in the region, despite accounting for almost 18% of their combined GDP. This gap shows that the local market still has substantial room for growth,” added Robert Miklo.

In Bucharest, prime yields stood at approximately 7.5% for offices, 7.75% for industrial and logistics properties, and 7.25% for shopping centers. These levels remained above those recorded in Warsaw, Prague, and Bratislava.

Colliers said investors are increasingly prioritizing assets with stable income, good energy performance, and clear long-term value prospects. Properties with weaker energy performance face tighter lending standards and lower demand.

“Financing conditions are favorable, but the advantage lies with high-quality properties with stable income, credible sponsors, and clear sustainability strategies,” Miklo said.

Across Central and Eastern Europe, Poland led the market with more than EUR 3 billion in transactions, representing 52% of the regional total. The Czech Republic followed with more than EUR 1.4 billion, while Hungary recorded close to EUR 600 million.

Offices accounted for 29% of regional investment, followed by retail at 27%, residential at 19%, and industrial and logistics assets at 17%.

World.title: Romanian animated short film selected in UK’s Official Encounters Competition
World.content:
Happy New Year, the Romanian animated short film directed by Radu Gaciu and produced by Adriana Bumbeș through Ariadna Films, has been selected for the Official Competition of the Encounters Film Festival. The film will have its world premiere on September 23, 2026, at Watershed in Bristol.

The film, set in 2009 in Romania, follows a woman who returns home on her birthday to the isolated cabin in the mountains where she spent part of her youth with her twin sister. She rediscovers a space where memory and dreams intertwine and where echoes of the past speak of the pain of separation.

With a running time of 25 minutes, Happy New Year is a fantasy drama made using a mixed 2D digital animation technique.

Encounters is a qualifying festival for the BAFTA, BIFA and European Film Awards and also gives filmmakers the chance to enter the race for the Academy Awards, in the Best Animated Short Film category. The film is eligible for the Animated Encounters Grand Prix and the Audience Award.

The movie was built over five years of work, two years of pre-production and three years of production. The animation was based on more than 60,000 reference photographs, used to build the characters and backgrounds. The project brought together a team of more than 25 people, from actresses and screenwriters to production, sound and image specialists. The film’s visual universe was created from several thousand digitally made elements, characters and backgrounds, complemented by almost 100 unique watercolor paintings.

“The film’s animation technique is mixed, a combination of digital drawing, rotoscoping and collage, in which both the characters and the settings are stylistically rendered realistically. The characters are predominantly digital drawings that were later animated or, in a few cases, rotoscoped, also digitally. The backgrounds are complex collages of adjusted photographs composed with the help of additional graphic elements,” director Radu Gaciu said.

The lead role is voiced by Ana Ularu, one of the Romanian actresses with the most solid and visible international career. The voice cast is completed by Ana-Maria Guran, Clara Angela Roman and Oana Rotaru.

The project’s journey began at the Animest International Festival, where Happy New Year won the 2020 edition of the Pitch, Please! competition. The award took the project to the CEE Animation Forum 2021. The project continued its development and production in Romania, received production support from the National Cinematography Center, and was completed on January 31, 2026.

The film is produced by Ariadna Films. The screenplay is by Radu Gaciu and Nicoleta Colopelnic, while the producer is Adriana Bumbeș.

The film’s original music was specially composed by Matei Vasilache.
