Independent polling and sociological research in both countries will also be needed to assess public attitudes towards goods labelled “Made in …”. Without such data, statements about future trade will remain largely expressions of intent.

World.title: ‘From crisis management to stability’: Pashinyan unveils new government programme
World.content:
Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

The Armenian government has approved its programme for 2026-2031. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said it marked a shift from crisis management to stability. Looking back on his eight years as prime minister, he said the coronavirus pandemic, followed by the war and the post-war situation, had forced the government to operate in crisis-management mode. Now that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established peace, the government can “return to the unfinished part of the agenda of the 2018 Velvet Revolution”.

The new programme focuses on stability, he said. Pashinyan stressed that it rests entirely on the concept of “Real Armenia” and the principles underpinning the establishment of the Fourth Republic.

In 2025, the ruling Civil Contract party announced a new strategic goal: establishing the Fourth Republic of Armenia. The party congress unanimously adopted a declaration to this effect. According to the document, the Fourth Republic “will be based on the concept of preserving the internationally recognised sovereign territory of the Republic of Armenia, covering 29,743 sq km, in accordance with the 1991 Alma-Ata Declaration”. The declaration says the party reached this decision after analysing the history of the Third Republic. The Third Republic refers to the present-day Republic of Armenia, which declared independence following a nationwide referendum in 1991. The First Republic refers to the republic proclaimed on 28 May 1918. Accordingly, Soviet Armenia is considered the Second Republic.

“Following the 7 June 2026 election, the ideology of ‘Real Armenia’ won. This means it has become the official ideology. Armenia is therefore entering the stage of its history that we call the Fourth Republic. We must continue and give new momentum to democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms,” the prime minister stressed.

Government plans for the next five years

According to the new programme, the Armenian government will pursue the following goals in 2026-2031:

strengthening and further institutionalising the peace established between Armenia and Azerbaijan;

maintaining and further developing a favourable security environment around Armenia, in particular by normalising and developing relations with countries in the region and deepening existing partnerships beyond it;

unblocking Armenia through the Crossroads of Peace project and the “Trump Route” (TRIPP) transit programme;

liberalising the visa regime with the EU for Armenian citizens;

deepening democratic, anti-corruption, economic and public administration reforms.

With whom does Yerevan plan to deepen partnerships under its “balanced foreign policy”?

In 2026-2031, the Armenian government will pursue a “balanced and proportionate” foreign policy.

“It has proved effective in stabilising Armenia’s external environment. Regionalisation plays a key role in foreign policy, whose goal is to ensure conditions in which Armenia can not only live without external support, but do so comfortably,” the document says.

Based on this approach, the government places particular importance on further developing relations with Georgia, Iran, Turkey and Azerbaijan. The government has outlined the following steps for each neighbouring country:

Georgia

Yerevan will continue implementing the measures set out in the Declaration on Establishing a Strategic Partnership between Armenia and Georgia. This will create new mutually beneficial opportunities for political, trade, economic, energy and transport cooperation, as well as regional and joint infrastructure projects.

Iran

Armenia will continue energy cooperation with Iran, develop cross-border infrastructure and expand transport routes through Iran, including North-South and Persian Gulf-Black Sea corridors.

Turkey

The Armenian government will continue efforts to establish diplomatic relations with Turkey, open the Armenian-Turkish border and put at least two modern border crossing points into operation. It also plans to restore and expand transport, energy and digital infrastructure, as well as bilateral and multilateral trade.

Azerbaijan

The government plans to continue efforts to sign and ratify a peace agreement and carry out work on the delimitation and demarcation of the state border. Contacts between civil society and business communities in the two countries will continue, helping to establish bilateral trade.

The foreign policy priorities specifically include deepening strategic partnerships with the European Union, the US, France and China. With Russia, Armenia plans to “transform and deepen its partnership”.

Against the backdrop of tensions over the ban on Armenian food and other exports to Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), which Russia leads, the programme says:

“Work will continue to ensure the full and uninterrupted exercise of the EAEU’s fundamental freedoms — the free movement of labour, services, goods and capital — as well as to develop relations with member and observer states.”

Regarding relations with the European Union, the programme stresses that Armenia will continue working to meet standards in democracy and the rule of law, as well as in the economic, financial and other spheres.

Armenia intends to deepen its partnership with the United States further. Cooperation will continue based on the principles set out in the Strategic Partnership Charter and bilateral memorandums of understanding.

“The TRIPP project, the ‘Trump Route’, will be implemented, at least in terms of operating energy and railway infrastructure, while integrating Armenia into major regional infrastructure projects,” the programme says.

Armenia’s 2026–2031 government programme

World.title: Parrots Rocky and Kiki: Tbilisi Zoo’s brightest residents – video
World.content:
Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

Tbilisi Zoo is home to two species of macaws: scarlet macaws (Ara macao) named Rocky and Kiki, and blue-and-yellow macaws (Ara ararauna) named Chico and Paco. Their bright plumage catches visitors’ attention at first sight.

The macaws at Tbilisi Zoo are currently in the middle of their breeding season. Chico and Paco are expecting chicks. They usually incubate their eggs for 24–28 days. During this period, both parents actively protect and care for their future offspring.

Rocky and Kiki have become particularly cautious during this period. They often hide from people and rarely leave their enclosure. If you are planning to visit them at the zoo, keep in mind that they may be difficult to spot at the moment.

Macaws are known for their strong bonds. Pairs almost always stay together: they preen each other’s feathers, look for food together and protect each other when danger threatens.

With proper care, macaws can live for 50–60 years, and sometimes even longer — more than 70 years. Rocky’s exact age is unknown, but he is the oldest parrot at Tbilisi Zoo. Despite his advanced age, Rocky still has the same short-tempered and grumpy nature he has always had.

Once, when a keeper was a little late with a treat — a nut — Rocky immediately made his “protest” known by biting him on the finger. Because of their powerful beaks, macaw bites can be very painful and may cause serious injuries.

Macaws are incredibly intelligent birds. They have excellent memories, and some can even imitate human voices and words.

Although macaws are often kept as pets, caring for them is no easy task. They need plenty of space, daily attention, mental stimulation and constant variety in their surroundings.

Tbilisi Zoo‘s history spans nearly a century. It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status. The zoo was originally built on 70 hectares in the Vere River gorge. Over the years, the expansion of the capital — and later the devastating flood of 13 June 2015 — significantly reduced the territory of the old zoo. Today, it covers five hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals, each with its own story. In this video series, we will introduce you to the residents of Tbilisi Zoo. We will show how their day unfolds, how they interact with other animals and people, and how their behaviour changes depending on the weather and the season. Get ready to hear many fascinating stories.

Macaws at Tbilisi Zoo

World.title: Opinion from Abkhazia: ‘Nika Gvaramia said nothing new about resolving Georgian-Abkhaz conflict’
World.content:
An interview with Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Georgian opposition, about ways to resolve the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict attracted considerable attention in Georgia. In Abkhazia, however, it attracted almost no attention.

In his blog, Inal Khashig, editor of the Abkhaz newspaper Chegemskaya Pravda, offered his view on why. He believes the lack of interest among Abkhaz people is mainly because Gvaramia said nothing new in the interview and offered none of the things Abkhaz people would want to hear.

Inal Khashig: “From my strictly Abkhaz perspective, Gvaramia did not say anything radically new. If anything, he simply revived the old idea of resolving the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict through Georgia’s integration into the European Union, which would serve as an attractive incentive for Abkhaz people.

Georgian politicians have periodically put forward this idea since the presidency of Mikheil Saakashvili. The most recent was Georgia’s current prime minister, Irakli Kobakhidze, who in 2024 even set a specific deadline for achieving the goal. ‘Georgia will join the European Union together with our Abkhaz and Ossetian brothers by 2030,’ he declared at the time from a high-profile podium. In short, the EU idea has already been discussed many times.”

From Gvaramia’s interview, I also understood that Georgia cannot resolve the conflict through military means at present because it lacks the resources needed to guarantee the desired outcome. In this context, economic development and shared security interests should form the basis for resolving the conflict.

The only “new” idea proposed by the opposition politician is that Georgia needs to overcome the trauma it suffered after the Georgian-Abkhaz war of the 1990s because these memories “prevent it from moving forward and hold back development”. And on this point, I completely agree with Nika Gvaramia.

In my view, Georgia’s constant insistence on the need to regain Abkhazia is actually a heavy burden that prevents the country from achieving its full potential.

It is like a man who devotes all his energy and the rest of his life to trying to win back a wife who left him long ago. You can consider his life wasted.

I am convinced that if Mikheil Saakashvili had not abandoned his reform agenda in favour of “restoring territorial integrity” during his presidency, Georgia would almost certainly have made much greater progress in building its statehood.

I can well imagine that when Nika Gvaramia speaks about the need to overcome the trauma, he actually means giving up once and for all on claims to the lost territories. But as a politician, he understands the consequences of making such an admission openly.

As for the idea of restoring trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians, Gvaramia talks about this as well. But his understanding of “trust” is not very different from that of other Georgian politicians: essentially, “we will open up the world to you and shower you with benefits, but first come back to us”. In other words, it is a kind of bargain, with no guarantee that the other side is not bluffing.

But genuine trust looks very different.

In my view, a tangible step towards beginning the process of rebuilding trust between Abkhaz people and Georgians would be for Tbilisi to abolish the discriminatory Law on Occupied Territories, which does little short of preventing Abkhazia and South Ossetia from breathing freely without Georgia’s permission. But Nika Gvaramia did not mention this law even once. Perhaps that is why his interview went unnoticed in Abkhazia.

World.title: Opinion: ‘Removing Kobakhidze would be logical move for Ivanishvili if prime minister does not move against him first’
World.content:
Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

According to Eka Gigauri, executive director of Transparency International Georgia, removing Prime Minister Kobakhidze could eventually become a logical step for Ivanishvili — provided the prime minister does not manage to seize political power himself.

Eka Gigauri: “The Garibashvili case has once again confirmed what we already knew:”

None of this has anything to do with fighting corruption. Ivanishvili is reshuffling his inner circle, while Kobakhidze — with his approval and Mdinaradze’s assistance — is getting rid of political rivals. In “Georgian Dream”, no one is surprised when people enrich themselves at the public’s expense or engage in corruption: they all steal. The entire system is built on corruption, and Ivanishvili gave them the freedom to do so. So the “fight against corruption” is merely a staged performance designed to conceal a settling of scores. Kobakhidze does not get his hands dirty himself. He has Mdinaradze to do that for him, who has become his loyal executor and servant. It is obvious that the overwhelming majority of “Georgian Dream” supporters genuinely support Garibashvili. The same cannot be said of Kobakhidze and Mdinaradze. Look at the reactions from “Dream” supporters to statements by Garibashvili and his wife. If the authorities imprisoned Mdinaradze and then Kobakhidze, “Dream” supporters would not say a word in their defence. To them, Kobakhidze is still a former NGO worker and employee of international organisations. He is not a churchgoer and has no particular ties to the Church. The same applies to much of his team. There is no friendship, brotherhood or willingness to support one another in the “Georgian Dream” party. Apparently, none of them possesses that quintessential Georgian sense of honour. Out of fear of Bidzina, and now of Kobakhidze as well, they will betray one another, throw each other under the bus and abandon one another in times of trouble. Ivanishvili is deliberately deepening divisions within his own team and turning its members against one another. His goal is to prevent them from uniting against him and to force them to constantly undermine and confront each other. Today, Kobakhidze is clearly Ivanishvili’s favourite. However, he appears to have been carried away by this status. He often talks about his personal achievements, as though he had the power to act even without Ivanishvili. He may not have many genuine supporters within “Georgian Dream”, but today he exercises almost complete control over state institutions. “Georgian Dream” members appear to fear Kobakhidze greatly — perhaps even more than Bidzina. They know that Kobakhidze has direct access to Bidzina and can tell him something about a fellow party member that could ultimately destroy them. Even Garibashvili did not have this kind of influence. Kobakhidze has placed his people almost everywhere, while parliament is under his complete control. He has gradually concentrated enormous power in his hands. If this continues, even Ivanishvili may find it difficult to dismantle the system.

The experience of authoritarian regimes around the world also shows that dictators manage their inner circles according to the principle of “divide and rule”. They periodically replace their favourites and involve everyone in corruption schemes and other crimes, so that they can later use their weaknesses and complicity against them. At the same time, they pit influential groups against one another and keep everyone in a constant state of fear through selective punishment.

Thus, no individual or group can accumulate enough power to pose a real threat to the leader. However, such a system also carries a significant risk: a favourite who has concentrated all the levers of power in their hands may eventually begin building an independent political force. That is why dictators often get rid of their most loyal and influential allies.

At the same time, members of an authoritarian ruler’s inner circle often initiate changes of power. In other words, autocrats and dictators have good reason to fear their own inner circles. Today, if Kobakhidze wanted to, he could even remove Bidzina, and no one in “Georgian Dream” would dare oppose him. Therefore, removing Kobakhidze would eventually become a perfectly logical step — unless he managed to remove Ivanishvili first.

Opinion on Georgian Prime Minister Kobakhidze

World.title: Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov votes in Kurultai elections
World.content:
ASTANA, Kazakhstan, August 23. Prime Minister of Kazakhstan Olzhas Bektenov has cast his ballot in the elections to the Kurultai, the press service of the Kazakh government says.

The elections to the Kurultai, Kazakhstan’s new unicameral parliament established under the new Constitution that entered into force on July 1, 2026, began today.

The Kurultai will comprise 145 deputies elected for a five-year term. The elections are being held under a proportional representation system, with deputies elected from party lists in a single nationwide constituency.

According to the Central Election Commission of Kazakhstan, 12,605,788 voters are registered. A total of 10,423 polling stations have been prepared, including 79 polling stations in 61 countries abroad.

Seven political parties are participating in the elections: Adilet, the Nationwide Social Democratic Party, the Baitak Green Party of Kazakhstan, the People’s Party of Kazakhstan, Auyl, the Ak Zhol Democratic Party of Kazakhstan and Respublica.

International experts are observing the voting process. A total of 777 international observers from 42 countries have been registered, while representatives of 13 international organizations are also taking part in observation missions.

The Kurultai will replace Kazakhstan’s previous bicameral Parliament, which consisted of the Mazhilis and the Senate.

World.title: Swans AFLW captain says support 'just unbelievable' as record smashed
World.content:
Sydney AFLW captain Lucy McEvoy wasn't sure what to expect for her side when they ran out for the first instalment of a historic double-header at the SCG.

The Swans dominated headlines across the country all week, filling both front and back pages of every newspaper, for a scandal that called the club's culture into question.

Swans fans descend on SCG amid club scandal Sydney Swans fans react to an emotional week, where a scandal continues to engulf the club, as they prepare to watch a historic double header at the SCG.

What the women's team got was an outpouring of support which broke the side's attendance record with 16,672 fans filling the stands to watch them play.

That is more than double the previous club record of 8,264.

"It's amazing. We weren't sure what we were going to expect this week, but to see the support that we've received today is just unbelievable," McEvoy told Fox Footy after the game.

"The members and fans are so tight and they know that we're united as a club and we're better than what we were at the start of the week.

The Swans doubled its crowd attendance record. (Getty: Cameron Spencer)

"I'm just so grateful to have the support that we had today and the girls were able to turn it on.

"We had a few nervous girls, that's for sure, but we absolutely turned it on."

The scenes were particularly celebratory on the ground post-siren, after Sydney beat Essendon by 24 points.

It was just the second time the women have played on the SCG for premiership points and the first in a double billing with the men's.

Loading Instagram content

Before locking in to warm up, star men's players Errol Gulden and captain Callum Mills got around the women's players.

Gulden was also seen going up to the crowd giving the fans a big thank you for turning out in droves.

Some of those fans left before the men's game, as a boycott had been suggested in the days before the match as a scandal continues to engulf the club.

It's unclear how many fans left in protest to the scandal, but a steady stream was seen leaving.

Swans players spent time with fans after the game. (Getty: Cameron Spencer)

Five players — Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon — have been stood down by the Swans for breaching the club's standards on drinking and staying out late following last Sunday's win over Essendon in Melbourne.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad are separately investigating a report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a player allegedly touching a woman without her consent.

Police have not made any arrests or laid charges.

Swans fans cheer from the stands. (Getty: Darrian Traynor/AFL Photos)

Lulu Clarke, who has been a Sydney Swans fan for as long as she can remember, was one of the fans who walked out.

Ms Clarke had bought a ticket to the men's game, unaware the women were also playing, but once the news broke of the incident she knew she would not be staying for both games.

"Of late, I've definitely drifted apart from the Swans and the AFL industry as a whole," Ms Clarke said.

"I decided that I'm absolutely not going to the men's game, even if those five players were still stood down. There's no way I could just show up and watch it. It just didn't sit right with me."

Former Matilda Sarah Walsh also left the stadium after the women's game, saying it had been a "tough week", but stressed she was not boycotting the men's team.

"It's not a new story but I have a five-year-old daughter who I brought here today to support the women's team," Ms Walsh said.

"I think you can have a club and not expect someone to be a fan of both teams.

"I think that's the nuance of sport, don't expect Socceroos fans to be Matildas fans … We've got a long way to go in society. I don't think this is a Sydney Swans issue at all … it's a societal issue and we all need to do better."

Swans fans Kayley and Georgia went to the SCG to support the AFLW side. (ABC)

Swans fans Kayley and Georgia told ABC News they were there to support the women and will likely just watch a bit of the men's game.

"It's very disappointing from the men's team … I feel like we were very disappointed in everything that happened," Georgia said.

Kayley said the situation was upsetting.

"We've been supporting the Swans since we were kids as well. So, it was just shocking," she said.

"We never thought that any players from this team could do something like this. It was really upsetting."

Many fans held signs during the game along the lines of "I'm here for AFLW".

World.title: Thousands line riverbank to welcome Spirit IV 'home' to Devonport
World.content:
After years of delays and cost overruns, there was cause for celebration in Devonport today as one of the two new Bass Strait ferries arrived at its home port for the first time.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff was among the crowd welcoming Spirit of Tasmania IV to the north-west coast.

"I was here around 7am and I was with thousands of other Tasmanians … people of all ages," Mr Rockliff told reporters.

"I got the real sense there that this was a dawn of a new era for tourism, for freight, for Tasmania.

"And the sense of occasion was most certainly there.

"People were excited and people were very proud as they could see their ship, Spirit IV, sail up the river, turn on a dime and back in perfectly to the gantry."

Premier Jeremy Rockliff and TT-Line chair Ken Kanofski welcomed Spirit of Tasmania IV to Devonport. (ABC News: Mackenzie Heard)

Crowds gathered to watch Spirit of Tasmania IV arrive at its home port for the first time. (ABC News)

But it has not been all smooth sailing to get to this point.

Spirit IV, and its sister ship Spirit V, were initially planned to be ready for service in 2021.

But the ferry replacement program has been beset by delays and cost blowouts relating to both the ships themselves and the wharf infrastructure needed to accommodate them.

In May, state parliament's Public Accounts Committee heard the program, which started in 2018, had cost $717 million more than was forecast in the original business case.

Spirit of Tasmania IV was stored in Scotland before leaving Europe for Australia. (Supplied: TT-Line)

Most of the cost overrun related to the new berth at Devonport.

"You can always look back," Mr Rockliff said today.

"But this is about looking forward … and big projects like this have their challenges, there's no doubt about that.

"But big projects are here for the next generation, the next three decades or more.

"They are the projects that are worth the investment, they're worth the blood, sweat and tears because they always deliver."

Loading...

One of those in the crowd, Rodney Winwood, said "it was nice to see" the ship arrive.

"I had my doubts whether it would fit, but I think a lot of people are here to see whether it would fit really," he said.

Rodney Winwood was among the crowd to see the ship arrive. (ABC News)

Two days of testing

Ferry operator TT-Line's chair, Ken Kanofski, said Spirit IV would be in Devonport until tomorrow afternoon, with its hydraulics, loading systems and the management systems set to be tested.

"The purpose is really to test the gantry and the ship together in a live environment," Mr Kanofski said.

Ken Kanofski says Spirit IV is undergoing two days of testing in Devonport. (ABC News: Monty Jacka)

"We've been doing it in Geelong with both ships for a number of times now.

"The gantries are built to designs, clearly, but you want to fine tune the systems, bring the two together for the first time," he said.

Spirit IV will return to Victoria following the testing.

"We'll also bring Spirit V here in September in order to undertake testing of Spirit V with the gantry as well," Mr Kanofski said.

Mr Kanofski said the new ships were still on track to start ferrying passengers in October.

People lined the Mersey River to see the ship arrive. (ABC News: Mackenzie Heard)

Emotion and nostalgia on banks of Mersey

Tasmania's Infrastructure Minister Kerry Vincent said there was celebration and nostalgia among the crowd gathered on the banks of Devonport's Mersey River to see the new ship arrive.

"A lot of emotion. There's a lot of old people here that … could remember the Princess and the Empress all talking about the changes and how important these new ships would be for Tasmania," he said.

The Princess of Tasmania and later the Empress of Australia connected Tasmania with Victoria from 1959 until TT-Line's Abel Tasman took over the route in 1985.

The cafeteria on board Spirit of Tasmania IV. (ABC News: Maren Preuss)

Mr Rockliff said during his first year in politics, he saw Spirits I and II arrive in Tasmania.

"That was also controversial at the time, and I think I might have even broken away from my team at the time as a candidate and supported the two new ferries when our side of politics didn't," he said.

"[To] 24 years later to see brand new ships … and these are purpose-built, brand new for Tasmania and Tasmanians, it's a very proud [moment]."

The ship's arrival has been labelled the "dawn of a new era" by the premier. (ABC News: Mackenzie Heard)

Devonport Mayor Alison Jarman said the new ship would be the city's "shining light".

She said there was a sense of celebration around town.

"We're getting hugs, we're getting high fives, we're getting people shaking our hands and congratulating us. And we're just saying to them, 'now, just tell everybody we're ready to go'," Councillor Jarman said.

World.title: Hundreds walk through Brookfield after alleged early morning sexual assault
World.content:
Hundreds of people have walked in solidarity to oppose violence against women following an alleged sexual assault in Brisbane's west.

Crowds gathered in the suburb of Brookfield this morning and walked along Brookfield Road in a display of community strength and support.

It comes after a 23-year-old woman was allegedly stalked and sexually assaulted while walking in the area on Thursday morning.

The area where a young women was allegedly sexually assaulted last week is a popular walking spot. (ABC News: Lucy Loram)

Police allege 32-year-old Jacob Dave Henry Hauraki had been driving to work and approached the woman from behind, then dragged her into nearby bushes.

He has been charged with six counts of rape, and one count each of stalking, assault with intent to commit rape, assault occasioning bodily harm and deprivation of liberty.

Mr Hauraki remains in custody and is expected to reappear in court on September 18.

Drawing 'a line in the sand'

Event organiser Emily Hall said she wanted to highlight the "spirit of community in Brookfield" in the wake of the alleged assault.

"[We wanted] to put a line in the sand and say as a community we will not stand for violence against anyone, particularly women," Ms Hall said.

Emily Hall organised the event to "highlight the spirit of community" in Brookfield. (ABC News)

"It's an issue for everyone, and we all need to stand up.

"We all need to be prepared to call out behaviours that we don't think are appropriate and support one another when these incidents do occur."

Local state MP Christian Rowan said it was "very encouraging" to see Brookfield residents come together.

"Our community is united," Mr Rowan said.

"It's really important when it comes to ending not only sexual violence against women, but also all forms of violence across communities, not only locally, but throughout Queensland and Australia."

A number of alleged sexual assault incidents have made headlines around the country this month. (ABC News: Emma Johnson)

Hope for change

The alleged rape at Brookfield is one of several alleged sexual assault incidents to make news across Australia in recent weeks.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad are investigating a report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a Sydney Swans player allegedly touching a woman without her consent.

In NSW, three 17-year-old boys were charged over the alleged group sexual assault of a 17-year-old girl in Sydney's south-west last Saturday.

And earlier this month, a 13-year-old boy and two 14-year-old boys were charged with the alleged sexual assault of a girl in a Sydney alleyway.

Brookfield resident Debbie Moylan says she regularly walks in the area with her three daughters. (ABC News)

Mother-of-three Debbie Moylan said she joined the Brookfield walk to send a message.

"It really shows that there are a lot of people out here thinking about what's going on in the world at the moment," she said.

"They're worried, they're scared.

World.title: Coalition wants to split Court of Appeal to focus on tougher sentences
World.content:
The Victorian opposition is promising to introduce a specialist Court of Criminal Appeal to deal with serious offenders and sentencing, if it wins the November election.

The Coalition plans to split the existing Court of Appeal into two separate courts, a Court of Criminal Appeal and a Court of Civil Appeal.

It says specialised judges with expertise in criminal prosecutions would be appointed to the new standalone court to handle appeals by offenders and ensure sentencing for serious crime meets community expectations.

The latest crime statistics for Victoria showed youth crime had fallen for the first time in four years, but adult crime rose by 10 per cent due to factors including increases in breaches of bail, retail theft and breaches of family violence orders.

Jess Wilson and James Newbury say they will recruit judges with experience in criminal justice for the Coalition's new Court of Criminal Appeal. (ABC News)

Opposition Leader Jess Wilson said Victoria's criminal justice system was broken and offenders were not afraid of the consequences.

"Victorians are sick and tired of watching offenders walk into our court system and get a slap on the wrist," she said.

"We have a plan to keep Victorians safe, we have a plan to ensure that our court system and our criminal justice system actually meets community expectations."

Former police officer and now Liberal member for Mordialloc, Paul O'Halloran joined Ms Wilson and Shadow Attorney General James Newbury for today's policy announcement.

"Police officers I've worked with over the years are truly frustrated about offenders being bailed, of being released and sentences not reflecting community expectations," Mr O'Halloran said.

"We must have consequences for serious offending."

Paul O'Halloran (centre) joined James Newbury and Jess Wilson at the policy announcement today. (ABC News)

Mr Newbury said he had "consulted with the courts" on the policy but would not say whether he has discussed it with any members of the judiciary.

"I have consulted in the way Victorians would expect," he said.

When new Victorian Premier Ben Carroll took over the leadership from Jacinta Allan last month, he said he was making crime a centrepiece of his leadership.

He said one of his first phone calls was to Victoria Police Chief Commissioner Mike Bush to talk about police resourcing.

Mr Carroll said the Coalition's plan would cause delays to moving cases through the Court of Appeal.

"The modern-day Liberal party is lacking talent and lacking solicitors, and today's policy announcement shows just that," he said.

"We've seen today the Liberal party searching for a policy idea and not doing any homework."

World.title: Almost two in three youth offenders offending on bail, government says
World.content:
The Queensland government says almost two in three serious youth offenders are committing crimes while on bail, and 38 per cent are committing crimes listed under the Adult Crime, Adult Time legislation.

But the number of serious repeat youth offenders has dropped by 29 per cent, as the government prepares to unveil a tough new stance on bail breaches that would send offenders back to jail.

Premier David Crisafulli said the "most significant reforms to bail" in the state's history will form part of the next phase of the government's Adult Crime, Adult Time (ACAT) initiative.

Minister for Youth Justice and Victim Support Laura Gerber said under the changes, breaching bail by committing a crime listed under the ACAT legislation would become a new offence.

Mr Crisafulli also flagged the legislation could include adult offenders.

Laura Gerber says there has been a 20 per cent drop in repeat offenders since the introduction of Adult Crime, Adult Time laws. (ABC News)

"We are doing the work as to who that applies for and for what period that minimum mandatory will be there, but it is the next step of adult crime, adult time," he said.

With youth justice workers set to go on strike tomorrow, unions have raised concerns about the impact of a potential influx of prisoners on the state's corrective services system.

A report from the state's audit office recently found the number of inmates being held in Queensland prisons had increased by 54 per cent over the past decade.

Before the bail reform changes, Queensland Corrective Services (QCS) was already forecasting the number of extra prisoners in the system to increase by between 1,500 and 5,200 by June 2035.

The latest ombudsman report found Wacol Prison in Brisbane's west was operating at 168 per cent capacity. (ABC News: Ned Hammond)

Together Union assistant branch secretary Michael Thomas said the proposed changes would "almost inevitably end up in triple-ups".

Triple-ups are the practice of housing up to three prisoners in a cell designed for one person.

"Even though there is more capacity coming online, there is simply not enough to deal with another 5,000 to 6,000 prisoners," he said.

Michael Thomas says an increase in prisoner numbers will "absolutely" result in corrections officers getting injured. (ABC News)

Mr Thomas said that will put correctional officers at risk.

"We know if we go to triple-up we are going to see more assaults on prison officers," he said.

" This policy will absolutely result in our members being hurt and the government breaching its duty that every employer has to provide a safe workplace. "

Ms Gerber said the government had already brought on "some extra capacity" with a further 1,400 beds to come online "in the next couple of years".

The minister conceded there would likely be more prisoners coming into the system under the bail reforms.

"I'm not saying we're not going to have an increase, because you've seen the data," she said.

A spokesperson for the Australian Workers' Union (AWU), which represents workers in Queensland's youth detention centres, questioned where young people would be held.

"All youth detention centres are at capacity and young people are waiting in watchhouses across the state," AWU secretary Stacey Schinnerl said.

"Every Queenslander deserves to feel safe. That includes our workers in youth detention centres."

Bail reform 'next logical step'

Citing new data, Ms Gerber said the number of serious repeat offenders had dropped by 29 per cent since the introduction of the ACAT legislation.

Ms Gerber said 61 per cent of serious repeat youth offenders went on to allegedly commit an offence while on bail, and 38 per cent committed an offence listed under the ACAT legislation.

"It is a sizeable challenge and the data demonstrates the size of the challenge we're facing," she said.

Mr Crisafulli said bail reform was the "next logical step".

" These will be the most significant reforms to bail in Queensland's history and they will be the strongest bail laws in the country. "

The Queensland government's ACAT laws have already been expanded twice to include a total of 47 offences.

Vyleen White's daughter Cindy Micallef has welcomed the changes. (ABC News: Mark Leonardi)

The changes have been welcomed by Cindy Micallef, whose elderly mother Vyleen White was fatally stabbed by a teenager in a car park in Redbank Plains in 2024.

"For me and my family, had there been stronger bail laws, because our offender had been out on bail three times already, my mother would still be alive," she said.

"There have been so many losses, heartaches and trauma for people that have had a huge miscarriage of justice."

World.title: Wrong landmark spotted on Sydney Marathon medal a week out from event
World.content:
Runners gearing up for the Sydney Marathon next weekend will receive a medal featuring a football stadium in Germany instead of Moore Park due to an "unfortunate error".

Organisers say the design on the back of the 2026 medal features eight circles to represent the Abbott World Marathon Majors, encircled by a "beautiful Sydney skyline" that "brings the course to life, featuring the landmarks runners will experience along the way".

However, a structure meant to depict the Sydney Football Stadium, which under naming rights is currently Allianz Stadium, was actually the Allianz Arena in Munich.

Eagle-eyed internet dwellers were quick to recognise the blunder among local landmarks like the harbour bridge, Sydney Tower Eye and St Mary's Cathedral.

The Allianz Arena football stadium in Munich, Germany. (WikiCommons: Tobias Alt)

Sydney Marathon acknowledged the issue, saying it was not going to run away from the mistake.

"A little too much international flavour has found its way onto the back of the finishers medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium. We're not going to run from it," a spokesperson said in a statement.

"It was an unfortunate error, though it's certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humour."

The organisers did not apologise and made clear there would not be a replacement medal.

The organisers say the mistake adds "international flavour". (Supplied: Sydney Marathon)

"With the event a week away, this is the medal our finishers will receive. It's a beautiful medal, and now a little more unique," they said.

"We're grateful to our participants and partners for taking it in such good humour.

"Behind every one of these medals is months of early mornings, long runs and quiet determination, and having it placed around your neck at the Sydney Opera House is a moment our participants will never forget."

Artist distances himself from error

The front of the medal features a blue and white Indigenous design by First Nations artist Ambrose Killian.

In an Instagram story, he said he was not involved in the design for the back of the medal.

"My artwork and creative contribution to this year's medal was specifically for the lanyard and the front side of the medal only," he said.

Ambrose Killian designed the front of the 2026 Sydney Marathon medal. (Supplied: Sydney Marathon)

"I had no involvement in the design or production of the reverse side of the medal, including the incorrect inclusion of Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney.

" I take my work very seriously and would like to reiterate that my artwork story, importance and originality remains. "

This year's Sydney Marathon has set a record participation with 40,000 entrants stepping up to the start line on Sunday, August 30.

The 42.2 kilometre course starts at the North Sydney Oval, before going over the harbour bridge, looping through the city, heading south to Kingsford and snaking back to Centennial Park, with participants crossing the finish line at the Sydney Opera House.

World.title: Tributes flow for 'formidable' ex-Nationals WA leader after his death
World.content:
Former Nationals WA leader Max Trenorden, who served in state parliament for more than a quarter of a century, has been remembered as a champion for his community and regional WA following his death.

Mr Trenorden, 78, led the Nationals from 2001 to 2005, and was deputy leader of the opposition coalition under the Liberal leadership of Colin Barnett in 2004 and 2005.

He died yesterday.

Nationals WA president Paul Gillett honoured Mr Trenorden at the party's state conference later in the day.

"He was a formidable parliamentarian who dedicated more than a quarter of a century to representing the people of the Wheatbelt and regional WA," he said.

" His contribution to the National Party and the communities he represented will be remembered for many years to come. "

Paul Gillett paid tribute to Mr Trenorden at the party's state conference. (ABC South West: Sam Bold)

Mr Trenorden, a farmer from Wyalkatchem in the Wheatbelt, was first elected to parliament's Legislative Assembly in 1986 for the seat of Avon, a seat he held until it was abolished in a redistribution in 2008.

From 2009 until 2013, he represented the Agricultural Region in the Legislative Council.

In 2013, Mr Trenorden described his shock and disappointment after failing to win preselection for the party and decided to run as an independent.

Although he was not elected, Mr Trenorden said he believed running was still worthwhile as it allowed him to raise important issues.

Following his retirement, he joined the Disability Board in Northam.

'Never lost sight of the people'

Nationals WA leader Shane Love also honoured Mr Trenorden's service, describing him as one of the most respected politicians to emerge from regional WA.

"Max was born and raised in the Wheatbelt, and throughout his political career he never lost sight of the people and communities that sent him to parliament," he said.

" Max understood that strong regional communities are fundamental to the strength of our state, and he spent his life fighting for them. "

Shane Love says Mr Trenorden was a highly respected politician. (ABC News: Kema Johnson)

Central Wheatbelt MP Lachlan Hunter said Mr Trenorden had a remarkable record of service.

"He was also incredibly generous with his advice, encouragement and support for the next generation of country representatives," he said.

"Our thoughts are with Max's family, friends, and all those who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him."

Deputy Premier Rita Saffioti also paid her respects to Mr Trenorden.

"Max played a big role in the state parliament and was a key figure in the party," she said.

"To all of the National Party members, my condolences, and to all those who knew him."

World.title: Australia had an innings win, but these five players didn’t get a pass mark in our player ratings
World.content:
Player ratings SportCricketAustralian cricket Australia had an innings win, but these five players didn’t get a pass mark in our player ratings Daniel Brettig August 23, 2026 — 3:53pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Australia scored a comfortable innings victory over Bangladesh in the second Test, well inside two days. It’s a stark contrast to the comprehensive win that Bangladesh enjoyed in the first Test in Darwin. Here’s how the host team rated individually across the two days in Mackay. Mitchell Starc had a brilliant Test in Mackay. Getty Images Mitchell Starc, 9



Was at his scything best on day one to open the Test up for Australia and made more critical incisions to pave the way to a rapid victory on day two. Now holds the world record for most wickets from the first ball of a Test with four, and is revving nicely for South Africa. Cameron Green, 8 An excellent innings to follow his century in Darwin, showing good sense and shot selection while keeping pressure on the bowlers. Starc pointed to Green’s ability to find a “process” that worked for him as an example for other batsmen to follow. Pat Cummins, 8 Made the right decision at the toss this time and bowled sharply and well at first change, in both innings, threatening with full deliveries as well as short ones. Struck a good balance in his rhetoric between games, acknowledging a bad defeat in Darwin but turning the page effectively here.



Steve Smith, 7 Played well and formed the foundations of a very good partnership with Green, before falling to the most marginal of lbw decisions in favour of Shoriful Islam. Continues to believe that Test pitches, particularly in Australia, have latterly become too difficult for batsmen to cope with. Josh Hazlewood, 7 Bowled well in both innings without getting the same rewards as in Darwin. But the main thing for Australia will be that Hazlewood got through two Tests without an injury concern, a possible harbinger of better things to come over the next 12 months. Nathan Lyon, 7



Made a vital 27 with the bat, helping eke out a lead of 146 with Green and Hazlewood to collect 62 for the final two wickets. Bowled tidily in the second innings and earned the wicket of visiting skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto with drift that turned an attempted cover drive into an outfield catch. Still looking over his shoulder every time the team is selected, however. Alex Carey, 4 Kept wicket tidily in his 50th Test but will be annoyed not to have made any substantial scores in this series. After looking becalmed in Darwin, he was out trying to swing Mehidy Hasan Miraz over midwicket in Mackay. Australia will need him to find a better balance in South Africa. Travis Head, 4



Gave Australia a bright start with the bat but will need to review his series after dragging into the stumps three times in as many innings. Despite a quiet series Head’s value as an opener remains high because of how quickly he can influence a game when the ball is new. Related Article Test cricket Starc claims 10 as Australia complete emphatic two-day triumph in Mackay Beau Webster, 2 Out for a first-ball duck here and unable to take a wicket in either game, Webster also dropped a very simple catch on day one. These outcomes either represent a downturn due after a strong start to his Test career or evidence that opposition teams are wising up to Webster after 18 months of playing against him.



Marnus Labuschagne, 2 Will be fretful about his Test future after failing to make an impact with the bat in either game, stretching a streak without hundreds to more than three years in duration. Was the first man in the nets on the second morning, as is typical of an extremely dedicated cricketer, but Bangladesh’s rapid second innings meant he was never likely to get much of a chance second time round. If he goes to South Africa it may be as a reserve batsman. Matt Renshaw, 2 A brief return to Test cricket ended when he tried to turn a seaming delivery to midwicket and was taken in the cordon. Should be given an extended run at the top, but South Africa will be a bracing start against a bowling attack adept at challenging left-handers. World.title: ‘Queenslanders over crooks’: LNP unfazed by prison overcrowding concerns
World.content:
NationalQueenslandPrisons ‘Queenslanders over crooks’: LNP unfazed by prison overcrowding concerns Courtney Kruk August 23, 2026 — 3:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Detention centres will need thousands more beds to accommodate offenders returned to jail under the Crisafulli government’s proposed breach bail laws, new data has shown, as the LNP dismissed concerns the change will push Queensland’s already stretched prison system to breaking point. Data released on Sunday showed more than 6000 Queenslanders – 5248 adults and 859 children – would have been sent to prison in the last 12 months for committing serious crimes while on bail if the government’s breach bail laws were in effect. Premier David Crisafulli and Minister for Youth Justice and Corrective Services Laura Gerber have dismissed concerns about how the government’s new “breach bail, go to jail laws” could impact overcrowded prisons. Queensland Opposition Under the proposed laws announced last month, children charged with an “adult crime, adult time” offence will be subject to a minimum mandatory sentence if they breach bail conditions, including committing crimes. The Crisafulli government is now considering similar measures for adults accused of committing the same serious offences while on bail.



While the government touted the move as essential to continue driving down victim numbers, Queensland’s prison system is already operating over capacity and is not equipped to manage the number of additional detainees predicted under the new legislation. Related Article Queensland government Nearly half of Queensland prisoners ending up back behind bars Minister for youth justice and corrective services Laura Gerber said the government had already added 2000 extra beds to the system and was working to unlock a further 1400 with the opening of the new Lockyer Valley Prison. She conceded this falls short of expected demand but said, “that’s not going to stop us delivering strong laws”. “Our strong bail laws will also see fewer victims of crime and see fewer youth offenders committing serious offences while on bail because they do act as a deterrent effect,” Gerber said.



“But if you’re asking me the choice between putting them in prison or having them in Queenslanders lounge room committing offences … I’m on the side of Queenslanders who say lock them up. “We will house them in our correctional facilities, and our budget is doing the work to ensure that we build the capacity.” A report by the state’s auditor-general released last month found overcrowded and underfunded Queensland jails are failing to effectively rehabilitate prisoners and reintegrate them into society, with nearly half returning to prison within two years of being released. Of the state’s 20 correctional centres, 13 were detaining more people than originally intended, as Queensland’s prisoner population grew by 54 per cent over the last decade. In youth detention centres, reports have consistently shown most facilities are operating “well above the safe capacity”.



Hundreds of youth detention workers participated in protected industrial action against the state government in recent weeks over ongoing concerns about safety, overcrowding and understaffing. Related Article Queensland government ‘Shifting the crime scene’: Union warns of lack of detail in new bail-breach laws On Sunday, Gerber said the government will continue to negotiate with unions over improved conditions for youth detention staff and denied conversations between representatives had broken down. On whether overcrowding would further strain rehabilitation efforts and safety concerns, Premier David Crisafulli shared Gerber’s view that it was preferable to people remaining out of custody for breaching bail conditions. “Faced with the choice of having extra people in a cell or extra people in your lounge room, I choose Queenslanders over crooks,” Crisafulli said. World.title: ‘Unbelievable’: Hanson intervenes after One Nation MP claims migration target ‘not too different’ from Labor’s
World.content:
PoliticsFederalImmigration ‘Unbelievable’: Hanson intervenes after One Nation MP claims migration target ‘not too different’ from Labor’s Matthew Knott Updated August 23, 2026 — 2:51pm ,first published 10:17am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

One Nation has been plunged into disarray over immigration policy, with leader Pauline Hanson forced to intervene and shoot down MP David Farley’s stunning concession that the party’s headline migration figure would be scarcely different to the Albanese government’s. Farley sought to redefine the meaning of net overseas migration (NOM) in an interview on Sunday, arguing there was a “true form” of the figure that differs to the way it has long been officially calculated. One Nation MP David Farley has sought to clarify the party’s migration targets. Janie Barrett “Well, the raw number is not too different [to the government’s], but the reality is, where do we need them?” Farley told the ABC’s Insiders on Sunday. “We don’t need them in the great urban metroplex. We need them out to be productive, working in agriculture, engineering, mining, etc.”



Editor's pick Immigration One Nation flip-flops on migration policy, announces tobacco excise cut He continued: “I think the big difference is we’re focusing on what are the skills we need as a nation, where do we need these migrants to be? But the raw number is not too different.” Labor and the Coalition leapt upon Farely’s comments to argue that One Nation was divided and lacking clarity on a crucial policy for the party, which has put slashing migration at the centre of its pitch to voters. Amid confusion over its migration policy, One Nation last week clarified that its plan to cap visas was based on a net overseas migration target of 130,000 a year. In his Insiders interview, Farley said this figure did not include a raft of key migrant categories and that these workers would add at least 100,000 people to the target.



“Well, what we’re doing is we’re focusing on the NOM in its true form, he said. “Now, on top of the NOM, of course, we’ve got all the other programs that we run, the PALM program, which is important to my electorate of Farrer, the skilled registered aged care nurses etc are all very important,” he said. The Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) scheme includes around 40,000 workers a year, he said, while aged care nurses would add around another 70,000 – plus more in the engineering and mechanical fields. Migrants are included in the official NOM figure if they stay in the country for a total of 12 months within a 16-month window regardless of their visa category. Farley, elected in a byelection in May, said that “at a minimum” there would be 100,000 extra migrants on top of One Nation’s130,000 target “but the 130,000 is what we call the ‘true NOM’” .



The federal government’s net overseas migration target is 245,000 for 2026-27 and 225,000 for each of the following two years, around the same as Farely’s total estimate of around 230,000. Hanson rejected Farley’s assertion that the party’s migration target was similar to Labor’s in a lengthy social media post on Sunday afternoon, insisting: “One Nation’s policy is to cut net overseas migration to 130,000. “The cuts will come from fewer international students and dependants, a dramatic reduction in temporary graduate visas and their dependants, and a much more targeted skilled migration program focused on the skills Australia genuinely needs ... One Nation’s target is less than half Labor’s current level.” Coalition Home Affairs spokesman Jonno Duniam accused One Nation of making policy on the run on a totemic issue for the party. “One Nation’s migration policy seems to change every time one of its MPs gets in front of a microphone,” Duniam said.



“It is unbelievable that, after years of One Nation campaigning on immigration, Australians still can’t get a straight answer about what their migration policy actually is.” Duniam said Farely had conceded that “One Nation’s headline migration figure certainly bares little resemblance to the actual number of people they would allow into Australia”. Energy Minister Chris Bowen accused Farely of being at odds with Hanson, who recently declared she doesn’t care if migration cuts affect Australian businesses. He said Farely appeared to be “on board” with the government’s efforts to reduce migration while not harming businesses that rely on foreign labor. Bowen said that “the numbers he was talking about are very similar to the numbers the government’s been working towards”.



“I’m not sure what One Nation is saying about immigration because it appears to me, based on what Mr Farley said, that One Nation now agrees with the approach of the government,” he said. Liberal housing spokesman Andrew Bragg has nominated under 180,000 as the size of net overseas migration under a Coalition government. During this year’s byelection, Farley broke with party policy during a candidate forum by suggesting it was “probably not” an issue if Australia’s net migration reached 306,000. “If we’re successful in One Nation’s water policies, we’re going to need more labour, and we’re going to need more labour quickly, skilled labour,” he said. World.title: Trump’s desperate move to mess with markets is destined to fail
World.content:
BusinessThe economyTrump's America Opinion Trump’s desperate move to mess with markets is destined to fail

Jonathan Levin August 23, 2026 — 2:44pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

With the midterm elections less than three months away, President Donald Trump’s Treasury Department is starting to look desperate about the soaring cost to borrow. The Treasury said it would increase its buybacks of longer-term government bonds “by at least double”, an amount that analysts figure would bring purchases to $US32 billion ($45 billion) per quarter. Make no mistake about the motivations: 30-year bond yields this week hit their highest since 2007, pushing borrowing costs higher for the government, businesses and consumers. US President Donald Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Bessent’s Treasury has so far failed in its stated goal to get longer-term borrowing costs lower. Bloomberg Key mortgage rates are back up to around 7 per cent, a fresh blow to voters that were promised easier financing conditions under this government and ended up getting more of the same. US public debt surpassed $US40 trillion for the first time, and has now surged by a third in less than five years, as US lawmakers continue to shrug off calls to contend with historically wide fiscal deficits. In many ways, hedge fund manager turned Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is doing his best impression of King Canute, whose attempt to command the incoming tide to stop inevitably failed.



The Treasury described the buybacks, planned to start September 9, as a form of “liquidity support” — which is what they were intended to be when the program was created in 2024. In this case, “liquidity support” is a clever euphemism for “please bring yields down!” Related Article Opinion

Japan Why fears of a Japanese implosion have the world on edge Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist It’s an inappropriate co-opting of a program that was created to improve market functioning and the government’s cash management, and, as explicitly described by the previous administration, was “not intended to ameliorate periods of acute market stress” — like now. But that’s the way the market sees it, driving yields on 30-year Treasuries lower by as much as 0.10 percentage point on the news. The market’s reaction isn’t surprising. This is only the latest ill-conceived attempt at influencing market forces by the Bessent treasury, which has failed in its stated goal to get longer-term borrowing costs lower. In the administration’s 19 months in office, he has adjusted capital requirements to encourage banks to hold more bonds; supported the GENIUS Act which established a framework for stablecoins to invest in US government securities; and authorised US support for yen intervention, a move that looked custom-designed to dissuade a major foreign holder of Treasury bonds from dumping them to buy its own currency. Don’t expect today’s bond market move to last very long. For those keeping score, none of the above moves have made much of an enduring difference. The effects of the yen intervention in late July started fading almost immediately. And even though the buybacks will double from $US16 billion on a quarterly basis, it’s still minuscule given both the size of the $US31.5 trillion Treasury market and the massive global forces keeping longer-term Treasury yields from falling.



For one, inflation is making a comeback in Japan after a quarter of a century of quiescence. Japanese 10-year government yields, which compete for the money of foreign investors with Treasuries, are now roughly at their highest in 30 years. With the Bank of Japan expected to resume lifting benchmark interest rates by October, the move higher in yields may be just getting started. In the interconnected global financial system, that’s an earthquake that is being felt in all bond markets – and certainly not one the US can counteract with $US32 billion of buybacks per quarter. Also working against Bessent’s scheming is the fact that longer-term investment-grade corporate borrowing has surged to support the buildout of artificial intelligence. Earlier this month, Alphabet sold $US25 billion of bonds in dollars with maturities of up to 40 years. Amazon and SpaceX have likewise been among recent issuers of longer-dated bonds, with bond investors starting to show signs of indigestion. High interest rates are weighing on American consumers. Bloomberg Where the administration actually has a chance to meaningfully and responsibly impact borrowing costs, it has mostly declined to do so. Thanks to the extension of tax cuts to the wealthy last year, the US continues to post record budget deficits, with the shortfall on pace to grow by 5 per cent from 2025. Persistently warm inflation, fanned by Trump’s tariffs and the oil shock from his war with Iran, has also done its part to keep borrowing costs higher. (And while Trump didn’t start the inflation, he’s consistently missed the opportunity to end it.)



One generous interpretation of these developments is that Bessent is effectively making a market-timing bet. By combining buybacks of longer-term bonds with issuance that’s front-loaded in shorter-term securities such as Treasury bills, Bessent is wagering that yields will be lower in the months or years ahead – and that inflation, the AI borrowing glut and the Japanese market moves are transitory. If he is right, Bessent would be vindicated, but it’s the longest of long-shot bets. Related Article US politics Trump’s 2024 grocery photo op now haunts Republicans in the midterms Treasury shouldn’t be in the business of using taxpayer money to time markets like a hedge fund. Don’t forget that Bessent attacked his predecessor, Janet Yellen, for ostensibly similar tactics. If he’s wrong, which is highly likely, this will all go down as a brash attempt to paper over the reality of global bond markets: yields are going to stay relatively high for a considerable time, and the Trump administration will inevitably disappoint the voters that it courted with the promised lower borrowing costs. World.title: ‘Look out, we’re coming’: 18-year-old’s stunning statement with five goals in her second game
World.content:
Daisy Pearce’s West Coast already face an uphill battle to make the AFLW finals after a five-goal haul from second-game forward Alannah Welsh lifted Gold Coast to a stunning 35-point win in Perth.

The Suns entered Saturday’s match featuring nine players who made their AFLW debuts last week, and their youthful exuberance proved hard to stop in the upset 10.9 (69) to 5.4 (34) win.

Alannah Welsh of the Suns celebrates a goal. Getty Images

Welsh was the biggest star of the day, with the 18-year-old kicking 5.0 from 10 disposals in a dominant effort in attack.

“It’s awesome,” Welsh told Fox Footy after the match.

“But we just wanted the result at the end of the day. I’m super excited for the rest of the year. It shows the rest of the comp: look out, we’re coming.”

Charlie Rowbottom was a force in the midfield for the Suns with 26 disposals, six clearances and nine tackles, while second-gamer Ava Usher chipped in with two goals, including a three-bounce effort on the run.

For West Coast, former skipper Emma Swanson battled hard with 26 disposals and 471m gained, while star midfielder Ella Roberts racked up 24 possessions, seven clearances and 301m gained.

But the Eagles, finalists last year, are now 0-2 after starting the season with upset losses to GWS and Gold Coast.

Welsh was a star in the air and at ground level, with her neat dribble goal from the pocket in the second quarter showcasing her quality.

World.title: Alan Joyce’s Musk monopoly warning over in-flight Wi-Fi
World.content:
BusinessCompaniesAviation Alan Joyce’s Musk monopoly warning over in-flight Wi-Fi Chris Zappone August 23, 2026 — 2:04pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Elon Musk’s Starlink is rapidly being adopted by airlines, giving one company, SpaceX, much more sway in the consumer experience of many carriers. But former Qantas chief executive Alan Joyce has warned that airlines will need to ensure market competition for satellite-based onboard Wi-Fi in coming years. Former Qantas CEO Alan Joyce. Louie Douvis “I think everybody would be looking at making sure that you would have some contestability,” Joyce said. “Because there are other people talking about having competitors to Starlink at some stage.” Joyce said that to prevent Starlink from gaining too much influence over the fragmented airline industry, carriers would need to have the ability to switch satellite-internet services.



“I’m sure, like any market, Starlink seems to be making good money out of this,” he said. While Amazon is in the process of building up Leo, its rival to Starlink, Joyce suggested Chinese satellite network providers might eventually enter the industry. Starlink is a division of SpaceX. A bust of Elon Musk in Brownsville, Texas, where SpaceX’s spaceport is based. Bloomberg “I’m sure, like any market, other people will be attracted to it,” Joyce said. Amazon Leo currently has about 400 satellites in orbit versus more than 10,000 Starlink satellites.



Qantas uses Viasat and the nbn Sky Muster satellite service, providing Wi-Fi primarily over Australia and some international destinations. Joyce said that for airlines, what is important is having the ability to switch. “The big cost for the airlines is the technology in the aircraft,” he says. Aircraft maker Airbus is working on a product called HBCplus that will allow a jet to be connected to multiple satellite networks simultaneously. The product will cut down the time it takes for an aircraft to be fitted with a satellite-based Wi-Fi system, and allow more than one provider access to the same plane.



Joost van der Heijden, senior vice president of marketing at Airbus, said in June that HBCplus “brings more competition, and allows airlines to benefit from the latest level of connectivity. A SpaceX rocket launches Starlink satellites. Starlink remains SpaceX’s profit engine. AP “The idea is to provide the best possible connectivity solutions to our airlines to offer to their passengers,” he said. Joyce believes that in time, as with many technologies, “the Chinese will have a product” in the space of satellite-based Wi-Fi for aviation, too. “Airlines then will have more choice on it.”



For now, Starlink seems to have an open field with airlines. The company has signed a major agreement with American Airlines, and has activated its service on a number of new airlines including Southwest, Virgin Atlantic, Iberia and Aer Lingus. In the year to June, United said it flew more than 311,000 flights on Starlink-equipped planes. The airline had more than 500 of its fleet of 1000 planes wired for Starlink, according to the United Starlink tracker website. Joyce, who set up low-cost carrier Jetstar, led Qantas for 15 years and navigated it through COVID-19 lockdowns (not without controversy), is considered an influential voice in the aviation sector. He was also chairman of the International Air Transport Association board of governors in 2012 and 2013, and is known for speaking out on industry issues. In a speech last year, Joyce warned that “if airlines don’t own the customer interface in the age of AI, someone else will, and we’ll become just the plumbing behind the platform”.



Related Article Space Need a tow? SpaceX rocket taken to Christmas Island after splashdown Starlink’s application to aviation goes beyond in-flight experience. It can accelerate communications across many parts of a plane, including better and faster weather information, and provide high-resolution radar and turbulence overlays directly to electronic flight bags, pilots’ bundle of navigation information and checklists. Starlink can also enable easier and faster real-time route adjustments based on winds and fuel, making flights more efficient. In SpaceX’s first quarterly update as a listed company, it revealed subscriptions doubled year on year to 12 million in the second quarter of 2026. World.title: Australia had an innings win, but these five players didn’t get a pass mark in our player ratings
World.content:
Player ratings SportCricketAustralian cricket Australia had an innings win, but these five players didn’t get a pass mark in our player ratings Daniel Brettig August 23, 2026 — 3:53pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Australia scored a comfortable innings victory over Bangladesh in the second Test, well inside two days. It’s a stark contrast to the comprehensive win that Bangladesh enjoyed in the first Test in Darwin. Here’s how the host team rated individually across the two days in Mackay. Mitchell Starc had a brilliant Test in Mackay. Getty Images Mitchell Starc, 9



Was at his scything best on day one to open the Test up for Australia and made more critical incisions to pave the way to a rapid victory on day two. Now holds the world record for most wickets from the first ball of a Test with four, and is revving nicely for South Africa. Cameron Green, 8 An excellent innings to follow his century in Darwin, showing good sense and shot selection while keeping pressure on the bowlers. Starc pointed to Green’s ability to find a “process” that worked for him as an example for other batsmen to follow. Pat Cummins, 8 Made the right decision at the toss this time and bowled sharply and well at first change, in both innings, threatening with full deliveries as well as short ones. Struck a good balance in his rhetoric between games, acknowledging a bad defeat in Darwin but turning the page effectively here.



Steve Smith, 7 Played well and formed the foundations of a very good partnership with Green, before falling to the most marginal of lbw decisions in favour of Shoriful Islam. Continues to believe that Test pitches, particularly in Australia, have latterly become too difficult for batsmen to cope with. Josh Hazlewood, 7 Bowled well in both innings without getting the same rewards as in Darwin. But the main thing for Australia will be that Hazlewood got through two Tests without an injury concern, a possible harbinger of better things to come over the next 12 months. Nathan Lyon, 7



Made a vital 27 with the bat, helping eke out a lead of 146 with Green and Hazlewood to collect 62 for the final two wickets. Bowled tidily in the second innings and earned the wicket of visiting skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto with drift that turned an attempted cover drive into an outfield catch. Still looking over his shoulder every time the team is selected, however. Alex Carey, 4 Kept wicket tidily in his 50th Test but will be annoyed not to have made any substantial scores in this series. After looking becalmed in Darwin, he was out trying to swing Mehidy Hasan Miraz over midwicket in Mackay. Australia will need him to find a better balance in South Africa. Travis Head, 4



Gave Australia a bright start with the bat but will need to review his series after dragging into the stumps three times in as many innings. Despite a quiet series Head’s value as an opener remains high because of how quickly he can influence a game when the ball is new. Related Article Test cricket Starc claims 10 as Australia complete emphatic two-day triumph in Mackay Beau Webster, 2 Out for a first-ball duck here and unable to take a wicket in either game, Webster also dropped a very simple catch on day one. These outcomes either represent a downturn due after a strong start to his Test career or evidence that opposition teams are wising up to Webster after 18 months of playing against him.



Marnus Labuschagne, 2 Will be fretful about his Test future after failing to make an impact with the bat in either game, stretching a streak without hundreds to more than three years in duration. Was the first man in the nets on the second morning, as is typical of an extremely dedicated cricketer, but Bangladesh’s rapid second innings meant he was never likely to get much of a chance second time round. If he goes to South Africa it may be as a reserve batsman. Matt Renshaw, 2 A brief return to Test cricket ended when he tried to turn a seaming delivery to midwicket and was taken in the cordon. Should be given an extended run at the top, but South Africa will be a bracing start against a bowling attack adept at challenging left-handers. World.title: ‘Queenslanders over crooks’: LNP unfazed by prison overcrowding concerns
World.content:
NationalQueenslandPrisons ‘Queenslanders over crooks’: LNP unfazed by prison overcrowding concerns Courtney Kruk August 23, 2026 — 3:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Detention centres will need thousands more beds to accommodate offenders returned to jail under the Crisafulli government’s proposed breach bail laws, new data has shown, as the LNP dismissed concerns the change will push Queensland’s already stretched prison system to breaking point. Data released on Sunday showed more than 6000 Queenslanders – 5248 adults and 859 children – would have been sent to prison in the last 12 months for committing serious crimes while on bail if the government’s breach bail laws were in effect. Premier David Crisafulli and Minister for Youth Justice and Corrective Services Laura Gerber have dismissed concerns about how the government’s new “breach bail, go to jail laws” could impact overcrowded prisons. Queensland Opposition Under the proposed laws announced last month, children charged with an “adult crime, adult time” offence will be subject to a minimum mandatory sentence if they breach bail conditions, including committing crimes. The Crisafulli government is now considering similar measures for adults accused of committing the same serious offences while on bail.



While the government touted the move as essential to continue driving down victim numbers, Queensland’s prison system is already operating over capacity and is not equipped to manage the number of additional detainees predicted under the new legislation. Related Article Queensland government Nearly half of Queensland prisoners ending up back behind bars Minister for youth justice and corrective services Laura Gerber said the government had already added 2000 extra beds to the system and was working to unlock a further 1400 with the opening of the new Lockyer Valley Prison. She conceded this falls short of expected demand but said, “that’s not going to stop us delivering strong laws”. “Our strong bail laws will also see fewer victims of crime and see fewer youth offenders committing serious offences while on bail because they do act as a deterrent effect,” Gerber said.



“But if you’re asking me the choice between putting them in prison or having them in Queenslanders lounge room committing offences … I’m on the side of Queenslanders who say lock them up. “We will house them in our correctional facilities, and our budget is doing the work to ensure that we build the capacity.” A report by the state’s auditor-general released last month found overcrowded and underfunded Queensland jails are failing to effectively rehabilitate prisoners and reintegrate them into society, with nearly half returning to prison within two years of being released. Of the state’s 20 correctional centres, 13 were detaining more people than originally intended, as Queensland’s prisoner population grew by 54 per cent over the last decade. In youth detention centres, reports have consistently shown most facilities are operating “well above the safe capacity”.



Hundreds of youth detention workers participated in protected industrial action against the state government in recent weeks over ongoing concerns about safety, overcrowding and understaffing. Related Article Queensland government ‘Shifting the crime scene’: Union warns of lack of detail in new bail-breach laws On Sunday, Gerber said the government will continue to negotiate with unions over improved conditions for youth detention staff and denied conversations between representatives had broken down. On whether overcrowding would further strain rehabilitation efforts and safety concerns, Premier David Crisafulli shared Gerber’s view that it was preferable to people remaining out of custody for breaching bail conditions. “Faced with the choice of having extra people in a cell or extra people in your lounge room, I choose Queenslanders over crooks,” Crisafulli said.
